soc.bracket_path_difficulty.label: Knockout bracket path difficulty and seeding
soc.bracket_path_difficulty.mechanism: Opponent sequence and tie format a team faces from the current round to the final.
soc.bracket_path_difficulty.rationale: A cup outright price is the product of round-by-round win probabilities; two teams of equal strength differ materially if one has a bracket with a top-ranked opponent in the quarter-final, and the draw, seeding and one-leg vs two-leg format change per-round variance.
soc.bracket_path_difficulty.measurement: From the official draw: list each possible opponent path with its probability given seeding constraints; P(path) times round win probability w_r = P(win 90) + P(draw) * 0.5 (extra time/penalties, slightly tilted to the stronger side by 0.52-0.55); for two-leg ties compute via aggregate simulation; as-of = after the draw or last completed round.

sources.name: clubelo.com / eloratings.net
sources.note: Daily club Elo / national-team Elo

soc.playoff_format_conversion.label: Table-position to title conversion for split-season and playoff formats
soc.playoff_format_conversion.mechanism: Probability of winning the title given final-table place under the competition's playoff structure.
soc.playoff_format_conversion.rationale: In Liga MX, MLS, the Clausura/Apertura leagues and some Argentine/Paraguayan formats the champion emerges from a playoff, so a team ranked first after the regular season has a title probability of maybe 25-35% rather than the 80%+ a pure league implies.
soc.playoff_format_conversion.measurement: For each competition-format: historical P(champion | seed rank) estimated over 10+ seasons with Wilson intervals and shrunk to a strength-based model prediction (k=10 seasons); combine with simulated regular-season rank distribution to give P(title) = sum_rank P(rank) * P(champion | rank).

soc.top_two_order_statistics.label: Order-statistic distribution of first and second place points
soc.top_two_order_statistics.mechanism: Joint distribution of the top two points totals and the leader's margin.
soc.top_two_order_statistics.rationale: The champion's margin is a property of the best two of ~20 noisy totals; a dominant favourite has a long right tail, an open title race has a near-zero mode, and because it is bounded below by 0 the shape is not symmetric.
soc.top_two_order_statistics.measurement: From the posterior-sampled season simulation compute (P1 - P2) over 20k sims per as-of date, recalculate per matchday; report the survival function at integer strikes S(15) etc; calibrate to historical leader margins by league (shrunk to league mean margin with k=5 seasons).

soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.label: UEFA 36-team league-phase simulation: finishing-rank distribution, top-8 / 9-24 / 25+ outcomes and tiebreakers
soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.mechanism: Monte Carlo of the 8 league-phase matches per club against four-pot-drawn opponents, giving the distribution of final rank, points and goal difference and hence direct R16 entry, playoff or elimination.
soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.rationale: The UCL/UEL league phase (36 teams, 8 unequal fixtures, rank 1-8 direct, 9-24 playoff, 25+ out, goal-difference and goals-scored tiebreakers) replaced the group stage from 2024-25, so there is no long history of P(advance | rank); the rank distribution has to be simulated from team strengths and the actual fixed opponent list.
soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.measurement: From the official draw list the eight opponents and venues per club; per match win/draw/loss from the opponent- and venue-adjusted goal model (soc.ratings, Dixon-Coles) with team strength sampled from its posterior; 20,000 simulated league phases using UEFA tiebreak order (points, goal difference, goals scored, away goals, wins, away wins, opponents points, disciplinary). Output P(rank r) and P(top8), P(9-24), P(25+) per club, as-of after the last played matchday, recomputed after each result.

soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.label: Seeded bracket path and opponent set conditional on league-phase finishing rank
soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.mechanism: Maps each league-phase finishing rank (or 9-24 playoff pairing) to the possible playoff, R16, quarter and semi opponents, bracket side and tie venues, so P(reach stage) is a product of path probabilities conditional on rank.
soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.rationale: In the new UEFA format rank 1-8 avoid the playoff and sit on fixed bracket lines while 9-24 face a seeded two-leg playoff; the opponent a club can meet in the R16 depends on its finish, so the same strength gives different stage-reach probabilities by finish and stage-markets cannot be priced from a strength rating alone.
soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.measurement: For each simulated league-phase rank, enumerate playoff, R16, QF, SF opponents from the published bracket lines and seeding rules (no away-goals rule). Each two-leg tie: simulate both legs from the Dixon-Coles lambdas with home advantage, ET if aggregate level (lambda*30/90*0.8), then penalties with p = 0.5 + 0.5*(skill_A - skill_B) where skill is the soc.penalty_shootout_skill n/(n+30)-shrunk value; final is single leg neutral. 20000 draws; P(reach stage) = product along path. As-of after each draw/matchday.

soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.label: Dependence of one club's league, cup and Champions League title events
soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.mechanism: Joint distribution of a club winning the league, domestic cup(s), Supercopa and the Champions League, driven by shared squad strength, a shared injury/fatigue shock and the schedule trade-off between competitions.
soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.rationale: KXSOCCERTROPHIES counts trophies across La Liga, Copa del Rey, Supercopa de Espana and the Champions League, so its price is a sum of correlated Bernoulli events; treating them as independent misprices count thresholds, and the sign of the correlation is mixed (shared strength positive, fixture overload negative).
soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.measurement: Simulate the four competitions jointly: club strength s ~ N(rating, sd from soc.ratings_uncertainty) shared across competitions, plus a shared availability shock a ~ Beta fitted to the club's historical share of squad-minutes lost (Transfermarkt injury days), reducing attack/defence by 0.1*(a). Compute the pairwise correlation of title indicators from 20000 draws; compare to historical co-occurrence of league+cup and league+UCL doubles over 20 seasons and shrink the simulated correlation toward the historical frequency with weight 10/(10+n_seasons_with_data). As-of after each round.

soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.label: Half-specific attack and defence ratings
soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.mechanism: Separate xG creation and concession rates for the first and second half.
soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.rationale: A single full-match rating hides that some teams are strong starters (high press early, fresh legs) and weak finishers, and vice versa; first-half markets need first-half strengths, which differ from full-match by up to 20% for extreme styles. It overlaps soc.period_split and soc.first_goal_hazard (all three describe how scoring is spread over the match); the team-level deviation from the league 1H share is small, so this input is a shrunk correction, not a standalone primary.
soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.measurement: For each team: xG for/against in minutes 1-45+ and 46-90+ per 45 minutes, opponent-adjusted with a ridge regression log(xG_half) ~ attack_i + defence_j + home + half, 30-match window half-life 15, shrink half-effect to the league 1H/2H ratio with k=20 matches; output a 1H multiplier m_1H_team in [0.7,1.3].

soc.second_half_state_multiplier.label: Second-half scoring multipliers conditional on half-time score and cards
soc.second_half_state_multiplier.mechanism: Multipliers on each side's second-half goal rate given the half-time margin and numerical parity.
soc.second_half_state_multiplier.rationale: Second-half markets are state-conditional: teams trailing by one raise output by 20-30% and leaders drop 10-20%, and a red card swings rates by roughly 30%; the 2H total depends on how the first half unfolded.
soc.second_half_state_multiplier.measurement: From league event data: for margin m in {-2,-1,0,+1,+2}, estimate goals per 45 for each side in the second half relative to expectation from pre-match lambda (Poisson regression with offset log(lambda_match*share_2H)), by favourite/underdog; shrink to league effect with k=200 half-minutes; include 10-man indicator at halftime.

soc.half_level_dependence_rho.label: Half-level Dixon-Coles dependence and draw inflation
soc.half_level_dependence_rho.mechanism: Dependence parameters fitted on half-time scores rather than full-time scores.
soc.half_level_dependence_rho.rationale: Full-match rho does not carry over to half scores, where 0-0 and 1-1 cells are heavy; using the full-time rho misprices the half draw and half exact-score ladder.

soc.knockout_cagey_factor.label: Knockout-stage goal-rate and draw-rate multiplier
soc.knockout_cagey_factor.mechanism: Competition-and-stage multiplier on goals and draws relative to league baselines.
soc.knockout_cagey_factor.rationale: Cup knockouts reduce goals and favourite win rates, and the effect varies by round, tie format and leg; a league-fitted draw probability underestimates the ET/penalty mass that Method contracts sell.
soc.knockout_cagey_factor.measurement: For each competition (domestic cup, Champions League knockouts, supercups, tournaments) and stage: ratio R_goals = observed goals/90 divided by model-expected goals from ratings, and draw uplift = observed draw rate minus model draw rate; estimate over 10 seasons, shrink to pooled knockout mean with k=40 matches; separate single-leg, first-leg, second-leg; as-of = previous seasons only.

soc.winning_margin_distribution.label: Winning goal-margin distribution from the joint goal model (league Method-of-Victory alternative reading)
soc.winning_margin_distribution.mechanism: Distribution of the signed goal margin H-A (and its absolute value) in regulation from the joint count model, used if league KX*MOV series settle on margin of victory instead of regulation/ET/penalties.
soc.winning_margin_distribution.rationale: League fixtures cannot reach extra time or penalties, so for KXLALIGAMOV, KXSERIEAMOV, KXBUNDESLIGAMOV, KXLIGUE1MOV, KXBRASILEIROMOV and KXLIGAMXMOV the only coherent reading with a non-trivial outcome set is a margin or draw bucket; its probabilities come from the goal-difference distribution (Skellam-like with Dixon-Coles correction and over-dispersion), not from a knockout path tree.
soc.winning_margin_distribution.measurement: Fit opponent- and venue-adjusted attack/defence strengths (soc.xg_adjusted_ratings, 30-match half-life, shrink k=8 matches) to give lambda_H and lambda_A; compute P(H-A=m) for m=-4..+4 with the Dixon-Coles tau correction (rho from the league-season fit) and a negative-binomial dispersion check; aggregate to the bucket scheme once the rules text is read (win by 1, by 2, by 3+, draw). As-of: confirmed lineups, recompute at each lineup update.

soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.label: Favourite's rotation intensity in mismatch fixtures
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.mechanism: Predicted number and quality of changed starters for a big club facing a lower-ranked side.
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.rationale: A rotated favourite loses 15-30% of attacking output but a full-strength one may win by five; the spread ladder swings between regimes, and the rotation is partly predictable from the cup, midweek schedule and manager history.
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.measurement: Ordinal logit of starters changed (0, 1-3, 4-6, 7+) on: days since last match, days to next major match, competition type, rating gap, manager rotation propensity (past 30 matches); output expected lambda multiplier = sum_k P(k) * m_k, with m_k estimated by regressing xG on number of rotated starters (with player-quality weights); re-evaluate at lineup release. Backtests are restricted to point-in-time proxies that are verifiable historically (previous-match XI changes, days since last match, fixture density, competition type); press-conference and training signals are excluded because no timestamped history exists (rotation_ground_truth).

soc.blowout_tail_inflation.label: Empirical tail of goal difference relative to Skellam, by gap quantile
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.mechanism: Excess or deficit of large margins compared with the independent-Poisson prediction.
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.rationale: At strikes 3.5-5.5 the model's tail fraction is wrong by tens of percent when game-state (garbage time, collapse) is ignored; calibrating on history is the only way to price the deep tail.
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.measurement: Define model P as the production Dixon-Coles/NB goal model refit on an expanding window using only matches before each match date. Pool 10 seasons per league group; bin by pre-match expected goal difference (deciles); per bin compute observed P(margin>=m)/model P(margin>=m) for m in {2,3,4,5}; isotonic-smooth across bins, shrink to pooled-league ratio with k=100 matches per bin; output multiplicative factors. As-of kickoff using only prior-season-fitted factors.

soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.mechanism: Value difference between the lineup announced at about T-60 and the lineup forecast from the previous day.
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.rationale: For outcome prediction what matters is the quality of the XI that plays (soc.xi_strength_delta); the surprise relative to a predicted XI is a timing and edge-detection construct that says when the information is new, and it cannot be backtested without archived predicted lineups (rotation_timing).

soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.label: Altitude difference between home venue and visitor's habitual altitude
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.mechanism: Home altitude minus the visitor's mean altitude over recent matches, with recency of exposure.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.rationale: Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia and Mexico City host matches above 2,000-3,600 m; visiting teams from sea level lose 0.3-0.6 goals of expected margin, the effect is nonlinear in altitude and decays with acclimatisation days, and is outside the usual home-advantage parameter.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.measurement: gap_m = alt(venue) - A_vis, where A_vis = sum_k w_k*alt(venue_k)/sum_k w_k over the visitor's matches in the 60 days before kickoff (w_k=0.5^(days_ago/20)); if no match in window use altitude of the visitor's home venue. x = max(0, gap_m-500)/1000 (km above 500 m). Fit goal-difference ~ ... + beta*x (plus separate beta for 2H if minute data exist) on all matches since 2000 with team home-advantage and rating terms, ridge-shrink beta to 0 with k=50 matches above 500 m. As-of kickoff-1h; altitude values are static venue constants.

soc.friendly_match_intensity.label: Friendly-match rotation and effort index

soc.friendly_match_intensity.rationale: Club friendlies settle like league games but are played with rotated squads, 60-minute starters and mass substitutions, so ratings fitted to competitive matches overstate team quality and understate randomness.

soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.label: Trophy weighting by year and competition for voters
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.mechanism: Estimated vote weight for Champions League, World Cup, continental championships and league titles in each award year.
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.rationale: A Women's Ballon d'Or in a tournament year behaves differently from a non-tournament year; the weight a Champions League final carries versus a World Cup depends on the year, which a pooled model would blur.
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.measurement: From historical winners and top-5 results (2018-2025 Ballon d'Or male and female, plus Super Ballon d'Or), fit a conditional-logit with features: team won UCL, won World Cup/Euros/Copa/AFCON, won league, reached final, interaction with tournament-year dummy; regularised with ridge and cross-validated by leave-one-year-out; output feature weights with sd. Identifiability limit: with about 7 women's ceremonies (pooled with men's and Super Ballon d'Or via shared coefficients) a year-interaction model is under-identified; fit main effects plus a single tournament-year dummy, shrink strongly (ridge), and report intervals; points-scale and panel changes by year are covariates, not ignored.
raw_data: historical vote tables with ranks and points

soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.label: Voter panel aggregation and tie simulation
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.mechanism: Monte Carlo of ballots with a points scale, voter nationality bias and noise, giving winner and tie probabilities.
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.rationale: Close races among two or three candidates are decided by ballots drawn from a distribution; the probability of a tie and the payoff split depends on the scale, voter count and variance.
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.measurement: Utilities u_i = log-scores from soc.award_vote_distribution (conditional logit, market-free features: production, trophies, tournament result) fitted on prior ceremonies only. Each of N voters draws a top-10 ordering from Plackett-Luce with utility u_i + b*home_nation(voter,candidate) + e (e~Gumbel); points 15,12,10,8,7,6,5,4,3,1; N as published for the award. b and the voter noise scale are fitted by maximum likelihood to historical vote totals (2019-2025 Ballon d'Or men's and women's) with ridge toward b=0. 20000 draws; report P(win) and P(tie).
raw_data: vote totals by candidate and voter lists

soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.label: Pre-announcement leak and credible-report signal
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.mechanism: Reliability-weighted indicator that the winner has been leaked ahead of the ceremony.
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.rationale: Previous awards have been leaked days ahead by outlets and club staff; a credible leak moves probability to near certainty and is the most informative late input, but a false leak is also possible.
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.measurement: Event log of each report (timestamp, source tier, named winner). Per tier t estimate hit rate h_t = P(report names the eventual winner) with Beta(2,1) prior updated on past leaks, and false-report rate f_t = 1-h_t over the same sample; LR_t = h_t/(f_t/(K-1)) with K candidates. Posterior log-odds for candidate c = prior log-odds + sum of log LR_t over independent reports (reports from the same upstream source counted once, total LR capped at 20). As-of strictly the report timestamp.
raw_data: timestamped news reports with source tier

soc.team_goal_share_competition.label: Player's share of team npxG and competition for it
soc.team_goal_share_competition.mechanism: Share of team non-penalty xG taken by the player and how it changes with teammates.
soc.team_goal_share_competition.rationale: A player's goal rate equals team chance volume times his share; new signings, injuries to teammates and system changes redistribute shares in ways that per-90 averages miss, and a shared striker role halves volume in expectation.

soc.european_slot_spillover.label: European slot spillover and variable cut line
soc.european_slot_spillover.mechanism: Probability distribution of the number of European places a league gets and how many reach the table.
soc.european_slot_spillover.rationale: A top-4 or qualification contract refers to a cut line that moves: the UEFA coefficient determines league allocation, and a domestic cup winner already qualified through the league moves the places down the table; so a 'top 4' price for fifth place is a function of cup results. Applicable only if a series settles on European qualification; the live titles (KXEPLTOP4, KXLIGUE1TOP4, KXEPLTOP2, KXEPLTOP6, KXUCLTOP8) read as table-rank cut lines and are TITLE_ONLY, so this input is context until a qualification-based series is confirmed.
soc.european_slot_spillover.measurement: For each league-season: baseline number of UCL/UEL/UECL places by coefficient (UEFA published), plus P(cup winner already in higher slot) from the cup simulation, plus UCL/UEL title-holder entry path; effective cut line L = base - E where E in {0,1} with probability from simulation; recompute after each cup round; as-of date stamped.

soc.last_place_extreme_value.label: Bottom-of-table extreme-value distribution
soc.last_place_extreme_value.mechanism: Probability each team ends with the lowest points total, and the gap structure at the bottom.
soc.last_place_extreme_value.rationale: Last place is the minimum of correlated points totals; the favourite for last place often has only 25-40% because others are within a few points, and the shape is not a simple function of a team's own rating.
soc.last_place_extreme_value.measurement: From the posterior-sampled season simulation: for each team compute P(rank=N), P(rank in bottom 3), gap to 3rd bottom and to 4th bottom at each as-of date; calibrate with historical bottom-team final points (shrunk league mean with k=5 seasons); correct tie rules in the minimum.

soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.label: Advancement tree for single-leg and two-leg ties
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.mechanism: Round-by-round conditional probabilities given the legs, the first-leg score and the tie rules.
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.rationale: Advancement is a state-dependent tree: after a first-leg win by 1-0, the second leg's draw/win probabilities differ from a pre-leg symmetrical model; format rules (ET, penalties, away goals) then determine the remaining branch.
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.measurement: State = (leg, aggregate before, venue). For second legs: simulate goals with team lambdas multiplied by state multipliers (placeholders such as trailing +20% and leader -10%, to be estimated from European and cup second legs once a history of that length is assembled, availability unverified), shrunk with k=40 matches; P(advance) = P(agg win in 90) + P(agg level) * (P(ET win) + P(pens win)); P(pens win)=0.5 + small skill adjustments.

soc.contract_expiry_release_state.label: Contract expiry, release clause and renewal-talk state
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.mechanism: Months to contract end, release clause and wage structure, and reported renewal status.
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.rationale: A transfer or release hazard is steeply nonlinear in months to contract end: under 12 months the selling club sells or the player leaves free; above 36 months only a release clause or a rebellion moves the player.
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.measurement: For each player: months_to_expiry at as-of; indicator and amount of a release clause (if public) relative to market value; wage as % of club wage bill; renewal status {talks, agreed, stalled}; build hazard model h(months, status) fitted to 15 years of top-league transfers (discrete-time logit) with club-type effects; shrink to league rates with k=20 cases.

soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.label: Window calendar and deadline-clustering hazard
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.mechanism: Timing of open and closed windows and the daily hazard within them.
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.rationale: Contracts ending before the window opens (e.g. 'before Jan 1, 2027' with a winter window opening only on 1 January) give a different probability than the same question in summer; deals cluster in the last days of a window.
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.measurement: Build calendar of windows by league and country (summer, winter, extended Saudi/Turkish windows); estimate daily hazard share = fraction of deals by days-to-deadline from 10 years of data; probability a deal occurs before date D = integral of window-open days times hazard; adjust for emergency loans and free-agent signings outside windows.

soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.label: Manager dismissal and appointment hazard
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.mechanism: Hazard of leaving a role given results, expectations and board context.
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.rationale: Managers are dismissed after results fall below expectation, with a spike after 4-6 game winless runs, and the 'next manager' contracts depend on the shortlist; national-team coaches depend on tournament cycle.
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.measurement: Cox model: hazard of leaving per matchweek on points-per-game minus expected points-per-game from ratings, league position relative to preseason rank, run of winless games, tenure, owner change; fit to 20 seasons of top-5 league managerial changes; shrink team-specific frailty with k=3 seasons; for national teams use cycle stage and tournament result.

soc.governance_procedure_stage.label: Stage and expected timeline of governance procedures
soc.governance_procedure_stage.mechanism: Procedural stage of a sanction or bid process with historical stage durations.
soc.governance_procedure_stage.rationale: A sanction or host decision resolves only after a sequence of steps; the stated deadline can lapse during a hearing, so timeline and stage durations determine the probability more than the merits.
soc.governance_procedure_stage.measurement: Record procedure stage (allegation, hearing scheduled, hearing concluded, ruling, appeal) with dates; fit stage-duration distributions (log-normal) from comparable cases (financial fair play, UEFA sanctions, FIFA bids) and compute P(final decision before deadline) and the distribution of outcomes (e.g. number of titles stripped) by case type; as-of date stamped.

soc.destination_club_feasibility.label: Buyer-side destination feasibility for next-club and join-league markets
soc.destination_club_feasibility.mechanism: For each candidate destination club or league, whether it can afford the fee and wages, needs the position, offers the sporting project and is a stated or reported preference of the player; normalised across candidates and the no-change outcome.
soc.destination_club_feasibility.rationale: KXJOINCLUB, KXJOINRONALDO, KXJOINSALAH, KXJOINMBAPPE, KXJOINSANE, KXJOINDAVID, KXMLSJOIN and KXJOINLEAGUE are multi-outcome which-club sets; seller-side hazard (contract expiry, window) says when a player moves but not where, and the where is decided by the buyer's financial room, positional need and the player's preference, none of which the seller-side inputs measure.
soc.destination_club_feasibility.measurement: Per candidate club c: wage_room = max(0, 0.70*latest revenue - wage bill - player wage - fee/contract_years) in EUR (0.70 = UEFA squad-cost ratio; league cap headroom for MLS/Saudi); need = 1 if club's best player at the position has rating below the player's by >0.5 SD of the club's squad rating, else 0; pref = 1 if a tier-1 outlet reported the club's interest in the previous 30 days (timestamped). Fit a multinomial logit of historical destinations of comparable players (top-5-league, age band, 15 seasons) on (wage_room/wage, need, pref, same-league flag) with ridge penalty set by CV; softmax over candidates plus a no-move outcome weighted by the seller-side hazard. As-of report timestamp.

soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.label: Ordered vector of per-match win probabilities with cup survival
soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.mechanism: Match-by-match P(win) for all scheduled and possible future fixtures in the contract window.
soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.rationale: A streak is a property of the ordered sequence, not of the average opponent strength; two seasons with the same average p can differ by factor 2-3 in P(5-run), and cup rounds introduce randomness in which matches exist.
soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.measurement: For each scheduled league/cup/European fixture: p_t = P(win in 90 min [+ ET/pens per rule]) from the goal model with venue, rest and lineup scenario; for future cup rounds weight by survival probability s_t; compute vector with dates; P(run>=5) by dynamic programming on the run-length Markov chain, including the current streak count c0; as-of = prior to the next match.

soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.label: Scope flags: competitions counted and what counts as a win
soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.mechanism: Parsed contract flags for which fixtures count and how extra-time or penalty wins are treated.
soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.rationale: The same team and schedule gives different probabilities if friendlies and the Community Shield count, or if shootout wins count as wins; scope can change the probability by 20% or more.
soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.measurement: Parse rules text for flags: competitions_all vs league_only, friendlies_count (bool), shootout_win_counts (bool), men_only, calendar window; store as version-hashed record per series; unknown flags remain UNKNOWN and require manual check; the sequence builder filters fixtures accordingly.

soc.latent_form_persistence.label: Latent form persistence (serial correlation of match residuals)
soc.latent_form_persistence.mechanism: Autocorrelation of match outcome residuals beyond ratings and strength drift.
soc.latent_form_persistence.rationale: If outcomes carry positive serial correlation after controlling for strength, runs are more likely than the independent calculation; if it is zero, ratings with drift suffice. Estimating it matters because the streak is a run statistic.
soc.latent_form_persistence.measurement: Residual e_t = (points won - expected points) where expected points come from pre-match club Elo (clubelo.com, value as of the day before kickoff) with home advantage; for each club-season, regress e_t on e_(t-1) controlling for expected points; estimate pooled AR(1) coefficient phi by mixed model with club random intercepts over top-5 leagues for 10 seasons, report cluster-bootstrap interval. Elo is already a form tracker, so phi is residual persistence only. Use phi in the copula only if its 95% interval excludes 0. As-of prior matches only.
raw_data: match results for top leagues over 10 seasons

soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.label: Calibrated tail dispersion of match totals by league and mismatch bucket
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.mechanism: Excess probability of 5+ and 6+ goal matches relative to independent Poisson, by league and expected-total bucket.
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.rationale: High strikes (5.5-7.5) are tail contracts: Poisson with league-average mean misses by factors of two, and the tail multiplier depends on mismatch size and league defending quality.
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.measurement: Pool 10 seasons per league; bin matches by model expected total (deciles) and expected absolute goal difference; compute observed P(total>=k)/model P for k=4,5,6,7; isotonic smoothing; hierarchical shrinkage across leagues with k=150 matches per bin; output tail multiplier function m(league,bucket,k); as-of prior matches only.

soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.label: Match-level shared openness factor
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.mechanism: Latent factor that moves both teams' scoring rates together, estimated from residual correlation.
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.rationale: Totals are controlled by how open the match is for both sides, which is more than the sum of two independent rates; ignoring it understates both 0-0 and 5-goal frequencies.
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.measurement: Fit a bivariate model with a shared log-normal factor: log lambda_home = a_h - d_a + gamma*z, log lambda_away = a_a - d_h + gamma*z, z~N(0,1); estimate gamma per league by marginal likelihood over 5 seasons; also the team-pair covariates: both teams' PPDA and line height difference; shrink gamma toward the league value with k=30 matches per team-pair class.

soc.xi_attack_defence_split.label: Lineup attack and defence value split
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.mechanism: Separate expected-goals deltas for the attacking and defending halves of the confirmed XI.
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.rationale: A scalar lineup-strength delta cannot say whether goals will rise or fall: a missing centre-back raises the total while a missing striker lowers it, and these may cancel in a scalar.
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.measurement: From a ridge regression on team xG for and against per match on minutes-weighted player indicators (separate models for xG_for and xG_against), compute attack_delta = sum over starters of player_attack_value minus season-average XI value, and defence_delta likewise (including the keeper); expected total change = attack_delta_h + attack_delta_a + defence_delta_h + defence_delta_a (signs per convention); evaluate at lineup release.

soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.label: Corners generated per attack by shot outcome (blocked, saved, deflected)
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.mechanism: Expected corners from the counts of blocked, saved-and-parried, and deflected attempts and crosses.
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.rationale: Corners are a by-product of how attacks end; two teams with equal shots differ in corners according to the share of blocked shots and crosses; shot-based expected corners provide a more accurate estimate than past corner counts.
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.measurement: Poisson regression of team corners per match on its saved-shot count and blocked-shot count (Understat result field) with opponent defence and home terms, trained on the last 3 seasons (match weights half-life 25 matches), coefficients ridge-shrunk toward league values with k=40 matches. Expected corners for the fixture = coefficients times expected saved/blocked shots from the soc.shots model (blocked share from the opponent's block rate). Crosses are included only if a paid feed is available. As-of kickoff-1h using prior matches.

soc.corner_state_multiplier.label: Score-state multipliers on corner rate by team role
soc.corner_state_multiplier.mechanism: Corner rate multiplier for the trailing and leading team by minute bucket and goal margin.
soc.corner_state_multiplier.rationale: Totals and team counts depend on when goals happen: an early goal by the favourite reduces its corners, a late equaliser chase increases the trailer's, so unconditional averages mis-state the favourite's team threshold.
soc.corner_state_multiplier.measurement: From event data with minute and score: corners per 10 minutes for trailing, level and leading states by pre-match favourite/underdog; estimate multiplier m_state relative to level state with Poisson regression, 8 seasons; shrink per team with k=300 minutes; combine with simulation of goal timing to get distribution of corners.

soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.label: Share of attacks through wide areas and crosses

soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.label: Starter/substitute/DNP mixture and settlement-adjusted probability
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.mechanism: Probabilities of starting, entering as a substitute at each minute, and not playing, with the contract's fair-price rule applied.
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.rationale: Because a DNP settles at the fair price and a pre-first-goal substitution voids first-goalscorer contracts, the effective probability must be computed as a conditional on playing; mixing in a DNP loss biases prices of bench players downward.
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.measurement: p_start from a logistic model on prior 5 starts, minutes, injury flags and rest (calibrated), p_sub|bench from historical sub rates by position and score state; substitution minute distribution from league data (median about 65 for attackers); P(plays) = p_start + (1-p_start)*p_sub; effective price probability P_eff = P(goal|plays) with the refund rule; for first goalscorer also P(on pitch at first goal); as-of strictly lineup release.

soc.assist_set_piece_role.label: Assist share by set-piece delivery and open-play creation
soc.assist_set_piece_role.mechanism: Player's share of team assists and key passes split by route (set-piece delivery, crosses, through balls).

soc.assist_set_piece_role.measurement: Over the player's last 40 club matches (half-life 20): set-piece xA/90 and open-play xA/90 from Understat shots (situation in {FromCorner,SetPiece,DirectFreekick} vs OpenPlay, credited to the assisting player), each shrunk to position mean with k=900 minutes. soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.label: First goalscorer allocation model with competing risks and sub timing
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.mechanism: Joint probability that the player's team scores first and that he is the scorer, including time-varying intensity and substitution.
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.rationale: P(first goalscorer) = integral over time of team first-goal intensity × player's share of that team's goals at that time × P(on pitch at t), which is not equal to team probability × season goal share, especially for early set-piece takers and substitutes.
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.measurement: Combine first_goal_hazard per team with the player's share of team goals by minute bucket (open play, set piece, penalty) from last 40 matches (shrink k=10) and P(on pitch at t) from the substitution model; P_first = ∫ h_team(t)·S(t)·share_i(t)·P_on(t) dt; also P(no goal) from joint survival; Monte Carlo 20k per match; as-of lineup release.

soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.label: Expected saves from opponent SOT and shot quality
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.mechanism: Expected saves = expected opponent SOT minus expected goals conceded, using shot quality.
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.rationale: Keeper saves are a difference of two counts: high SOT volume with many easy shots gives many saves, while the same volume of high-quality shots gives goals, so two matches with equal SOT can differ by two saves.
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.measurement: E[saves] = E[SOT faced] - E[goals conceded]; E[SOT faced] = opponent expected shots × SOT rate (opponent-adjusted, last 25 matches, half-life 12); E[goals] = E[SOT] × mean(PSxG per SOT) × keeper adjustment (shrunk PSxG-GA/SOT with k=60 SOT); includes penalty probability; variance via compound negative binomial; as-of lineup release.
raw_data: team shots, SOT, goals conceded, PSxG

soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.label: Joint distribution of two named players' World Cup tallies
soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.mechanism: Equality contracts pay on the two tallies being identical, so the full pmf of each tally and their dependence are needed.
soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.rationale: P(equal) is driven by low counts and by the probability each team exits early; a model of expected goals alone misprices it. Dependence arises if the two teams can meet or share a bracket half; goal contributions add assist attribution noise.
soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.measurement: For each player simulate, inside the tournament simulation (N>=100,000), matches played from his team's path, start probability and minutes (last 12 internationals, shrunk to role prior k=6), and per-match goals (and assists) as negative binomial with mean from international npxG/90 plus penalty duty; record both tallies per draw and compute P(A=B) directly; update after each match day.

soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.label: Penalty duel skill prior for exhibition contestants
soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.mechanism: The 1v1 duel winner is set by each contestant's conversion as kicker and save rate as keeper on a small net.
soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.rationale: Professional shootout data do not transfer to amateurs on a 10x6 ft net with alternating roles; only weak priors from published content and any prior PrizePicks events exist, so the input mostly expresses how far from 50% the price should be allowed to move.
soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.measurement: Per contestant, Beta prior on per-kick conversion (mean 0.65, strength 10) and on save rate (mean 0.30, strength 10), updated with counted kicks/saves from prior filmed duels (each kick one trial, dated before listing); win probability by exact enumeration of five alternating kicks each plus sudden death.

soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.label: Joint distribution of tournament placings from a full group-and-bracket simulation
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.mechanism: Union, exact-order and any-group-winner contracts are functions of the joint placings of many teams, which bracket structure makes dependent.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.rationale: Summing marginal title odds is right only for disjoint unions; exact orders (KXWCFINISHINGORDER, KXWCGROUPORDER) and 'any nation of a set wins its group' need the joint draw, and group-mates are negatively correlated. Tiebreak rules and the best-third-place allocation make the dependence discrete and non-trivial.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo of the full competition (N>=200,000 draws) from current team ratings with posterior rating draws per simulation, official group composition, FIFA/UEFA tiebreak order, best-third allocation table and bracket; store per draw each team's placing (group rank, stage reached, final placing 1-4); contract probabilities are frequencies of the defining event; rerun at each as-of time after every match day.

soc.match_format_rules_profile.label: Match format rules profile for non-standard game series
soc.match_format_rules_profile.mechanism: Match length, players per side and substitution rules change the goal rate and the draw probability of a 3-way market.
soc.match_format_rules_profile.rationale: All-star, college and small-sided (Baller League) GAME series share the 3-way text with league games but not the 11-a-side, 90-minute process; applying league draw rates to them misprices the Tie leg. The subtle part is that the Baller League text states no window, so the format's own rules define what 'tie' means.
soc.match_format_rules_profile.measurement: Per competition, a static record updated each season: regulation minutes, players per side, maximum substitutions and re-entry flag, level-game procedure (draw stands / shootout / golden goal), plus the competition's empirical goals per match and draw rate over the last 2 seasons (or all available games if fewer than 100), shrunk toward a format-class prior with k=50 games; as-of the market listing.

soc.wc_award_selection_profile.label: World Cup Ball selection profile and its link to team progress and scoring
soc.wc_award_selection_profile.mechanism: FIFA Ball selections favour players of the finalists and knockout performers, coupling them to bracket outcomes and to the Golden Boot race.
soc.wc_award_selection_profile.rationale: Golden/Silver/Bronze Ball and combo markets cannot use journalist-ballot models: the selector is FIFA, the winner usually comes from a finalist, and the Golden Boot leg is count-based; the dependence between legs makes the combo far from independent.
soc.wc_award_selection_profile.measurement: Conditional logit fitted on World Cups 1982-2022 (about 11 editions, 3 Balls each): candidate features = team final placing (1-4, QF, earlier), goals+assists in knockout rounds, total goals, position, captaincy; Golden Boot from simulated tournament goal counts with FIFA tiebreaks; joint simulation inside the tournament Monte Carlo (N>=100,000) to price combos; ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-edition-out.
raw_data: historical Ball winners with team placing and stats

soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.label: Player's distribution of tournament matches and minutes from team progression
soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.mechanism: A player's tournament goal tally is bounded by the number of matches his team plays, which is random and set by the bracket.
soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.rationale: World Cup goal counts, leaders, top scorers, streaks and record series all scale with matches played; equal per-90 scorers on teams with different progression odds have very different tallies. The subtle part is that progression and scoring are positively correlated (a team goes further partly because its striker scores).
soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.measurement: From the tournament simulation (N>=100,000 draws) take per team the number of matches played (3-8, third-place match included) and extra-time periods; multiply by the player's start probability and expected minutes per start (last 12 international matches, shrunk to role prior with k=6) to get a minutes distribution; simulate per-match goals jointly with match outcomes so correlation is preserved; update after each match day.

soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.label: Skills-challenge format and entrant drill skill
soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.mechanism: The skills-challenge winner is set by drill scores under the event's format among the announced entrants.
soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.rationale: KXMLSSKILLS is a novelty exhibition whose outcome is driven by the format (which drills, team vs individual) and entrants; match statistics only weakly proxy drill skill (e.g. long-pass completion for passing drills), and the event is TITLE_ONLY so even the outcome set is unconfirmed.
soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.measurement: From the event announcement: list of entrants and drills; per entrant a drill-skill score = z-scored season long-pass completion, shot accuracy and cross accuracy (last 2 MLS seasons, shrunk to league mean with k=200 attempts), mapped to win probability by softmax with temperature fitted to past skills-challenge results (2019 onward); fixed as of the announcement time.

soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.label: Within-team first-goal race across one match or a tournament
soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.mechanism: Team-first and country-first goalscorer markets are races among one team's players, repeated across matches until the team scores.
soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.rationale: Match-level first-goalscorer models race all 22 players; the team-first and country-first versions condition on one team and (for the tournament) roll over to the next match if the team does not score, so a starter in the opening game has a large edge and the no-scorer leg depends on the team's goal rate over its schedule.
soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.measurement: Per player per match: share of team npxG (last 12 internationals or 20 club matches, shrunk to positional prior with k=8) times start probability and expected minutes share, plus penalty share times team penalty rate; per match the team's goal hazard from the match model; simulate matches in order (N>=100,000) until the first non-own team goal, recording the scorer or 'no goalscorer' if the team exits without scoring.

soc.tournament_goal_environment.label: Tournament goals-per-match environment from past World Cups and tournament-specific drivers
soc.tournament_goal_environment.mechanism: Expected goals per match across a whole tournament, set by the mix of strong and weak teams, the group format and rule directives such as added time and VAR.
soc.tournament_goal_environment.rationale: Total goals is a sum of 104 correlated matches, so the level matters more than any one team. Past World Cups sit around 2.6 to 2.7 goals per match but a 48-team field adds more lopsided group games, and a longer-added-time directive raises totals. A model built from club league averages misses the tournament-specific level.
soc.tournament_goal_environment.measurement: For each World Cup since 1998: goals per match incl. ET split by group stage and knockout, by rating-gap bucket and by added-time directive era (2022 onward longer). Fit a Poisson-gamma mixture across matches; set the 2026 mean from team ratings of the actual 48-team field through the draw, shrunk to the historical mean with k=3 tournaments. Output expected and distribution of the 104-match sum incl. ET and own goals. As-of = after the draw; update after each round.

soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.label: Shared tournament-wide factor affecting all matches' scoring
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.mechanism: Common causes that move every match together: ball, climate, officiating directives, travel burden and a low-scoring or high-scoring tournament style.
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.rationale: Match outcomes within a tournament are not independent: one referee directive on penalties or a heat wave across venues shifts the whole distribution. Ignoring this makes the variance of totals and counts too narrow, which matters most for tail strikes such as a record goals total.
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.measurement: Estimate the between-tournament variance of per-match goals residual after team strength, using World Cups and continental finals since 2000 (random effect per tournament); report the intraclass correlation and its posterior. Use the implied standard deviation as the dispersion widening for tournament sums. As-of = pre-tournament; update only with documented directive changes.

soc.shootout_length_distribution.label: Penalty shootout length and per-kick conversion distribution
soc.shootout_length_distribution.mechanism: A shootout lasts five rounds each unless decided early, then sudden death; its length is a stopping-time of kick conversions.
soc.shootout_length_distribution.rationale: The longest shootout is an extreme of a small random number of shootouts. With kick conversion p near 0.70 at World Cups, a shootout is level after five rounds with probability about 0.27 and each sudden-death round continues with probability p^2+(1-p)^2 (about 0.58), so P(9+ rounds) per shootout is roughly 0.05. Goalkeepers usually kick only from round 11, so Goalie Penalty Goal depends on the same tail.
soc.shootout_length_distribution.measurement: From all World Cup shootouts since 1982 (34 through 2022) plus Euro, Copa America, AFCON and Asian Cup shootouts (well over 100 in total), compute per-kick conversion with beta shrinkage (prior mean 0.70, strength 40 kicks), the probability of a level score after five rounds, the sudden-death continuation probability, and P(length>=k rounds) under the paired-kick definition, including the share of shootouts ending mid-round. Combine with soc.ko_round_outcome_counts to give the distribution of the maximum. As-of = bracket known.

soc.group_gap_composition.label: Distribution of strength gaps across scheduled group and knockout matches
soc.group_gap_composition.mechanism: The tournament's schedule fixes a list of pairings whose strength gaps determine how many lopsided and how many balanced matches occur.
soc.group_gap_composition.rationale: Goal totals and trailing events depend on gap: lopsided matches produce more goals and fewer comebacks, balanced ones more draws and shootouts. A 48-team field has more lopsided group games than 32 teams, so past World Cup rates cannot be applied unadjusted.
soc.group_gap_composition.measurement: Using pre-tournament team ratings and the final draw, compute for each of the 72 group matches the rating gap and the implied goal expectations; bucket into quintiles and compare with past World Cups' bucket frequencies. As-of = after the draw.

soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.label: Per-team goals scored and conceded expectations over the team's actual fixtures and simulated path
soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.mechanism: A named team's tournament goals are the sum over its three drawn group opponents and any knockout opponents of match-level scoring rates, with the number of matches random from 3 to 8.
soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.rationale: Team Goals and Tournament Goals are single-team ladders, not tournament totals; Goals Allowed, most-allowed and fewest-by-group extremes need the conceding side. A strong attack drawn with two weak sides can post 8+ group goals, and full-tournament totals depend on advancement depth. Rotation in matchday 3 after qualification is secured and star-forward absence lower the sum; own goals are credited to the beneficiary for scoring and to the erring team for conceding.
soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.measurement: For each team and each scheduled or simulated fixture: lambda_for and lambda_against from a Dixon-Coles international model (attack/defence, half-life 2 years, friendlies weighted 0.5, shrink k=10 matches to confederation mean) adjusted for venue altitude/heat and for knockout via soc.knockout_cagey_factor; ET adds 30 minutes at 0.8x rate in level KO ties. Sum over the comp_sim path (20000 draws) to output the distribution of group-stage goals, full-tournament goals and group-stage goals conceded per team, plus group sums. Matchday-3 rotation multiplier from soc.group_stage_scenarios. As-of = draw, updated after each match.

soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.label: Per-round knockout outcome counts from bracket simulation (shootouts per round, group winners lost in R32)
soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.mechanism: Each knockout round has 16, 8, 4, 2 or 1 ties whose pairings come from the bracket; the count of ties level after 120 minutes and the count of group winners losing in the R32 are sums of dependent Bernoullis over that round's simulated pairings.
soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.rationale: Historical World Cup knockout shootout frequency is about a quarter of ties (2014 4/16, 2018 4/16, 2022 5/16), far above a few percent, and balanced pairings raise it. Contracts are per round ('exactly 4' in the Quarterfinals), so the needed object is the per-round count distribution, not a tournament binomial. Group winners face third-placed or runner-up teams in the R32, so upset counts depend on the 495-combination allocation.
soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.measurement: In each comp_sim draw, record for each round the number of ties level after 120 minutes, using P(level after 90) from the joint goal model times P(level after ET | level at 90) calibrated to soc.method_path_tree_calibration-style counts for World Cups and continental finals since 1986 (beta shrinkage k=30 ties per node), and the number of group winners eliminated in the R32. Output P(count = n) per round for n=0..ties. As-of = after each completed round.

soc.concession_race_schedule.label: Cross-match concession race: kickoff ET timestamps and per-minute concession hazard of named teams
soc.concession_race_schedule.mechanism: The first of several named teams to concede is the minimum over their matches of the clock time of their first goal conceded; earlier kickoffs give a head start that opponent-specific hazards then modify.
soc.concession_race_schedule.rationale: Concede First is settled by ET timestamp regardless of match minute or matchday, so a team playing first in the calendar (Mexico played the 11 June opening match) has a large structural edge; a strong defence playing days later rarely beats an early kickoff. If none of the four concede in the tournament, Yes pays $1/N, which matters only for strong defences with long clean-sheet runs.
soc.concession_race_schedule.measurement: Per match, conceding intensity h(t)=lambda_against*f(t) with f estimated as the historical share of goals per minute bucket (0-15, 15-30, 30-45+, 45-60, 60-75, 75-90+) from World Cup/Euro goal minutes since 1998 normalised to mean 1 per 90; first half 45+U(1,5) min, half-time 15 min, second half 45+U(2,8) min. Convert match minute to ET wall-clock using official kickoff time; simulate 100000 times the first concession timestamp across all named teams' matches (earliest wins); P(no concession in all matches) separately. As-of schedule fixed; update after each match.

soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.label: Probability the eventual champion never trails, mixed over champion identity and path
soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.mechanism: P(YES) = sum over teams of P(team wins the tournament and never trails in any of its 7-8 matches); trailing requires conceding while level or ahead turning to behind, and winning a match conditions on mostly leading.
soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.rationale: The contract follows the champion, not any match winner. Conditioning on winning seven or eight matches sharply lowers the trailing rate, and strong favourites with elite defences dominate the mixture. Recent champions mostly trailed at least once (e.g. Argentina 2022 lost its opener to Saudi Arabia), so the base rate is low but highly path dependent.
soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.measurement: In each tournament simulation draw simulate each match's goal times (inhomogeneous Poisson from match lambdas with the soc.score_state comeback multipliers) through 120 minutes; the champion 'trails' if at any moment in any of its matches it is behind in goals; penalty-shootout kicks do not count. P = fraction of draws in which the eventual champion never trails; report decomposition by champion. Validate vs. never-trailed share of 1986-2022 World Cup champions (shrink to simulation with k=5 tournaments). As-of pre-tournament, rerun after each match with realised states.

soc.group_table_pattern_probability.label: Joint W/D/L pattern probability within each group (cyclic 4-4-4-4 tables)
soc.group_table_pattern_probability.mechanism: All four teams on 4 points requires each team to have exactly one win, one draw and one loss; this is a specific joint pattern of six results with two draws and four decisive matches arranged cyclically.
soc.group_table_pattern_probability.rationale: The probability is small per group and highest in balanced groups with high draw rates; it is not a function of any team's marginal points. Twelve groups make the any-group event materially more likely than one group, and matchday-3 incentives (a draw suiting both sides) can raise the draw count.
soc.group_table_pattern_probability.measurement: From the comp_sim group simulation (20000 draws) record each group's final points vector and the indicator that all four equal 4; use Dixon-Coles match probabilities with soc.draw_propensity adjustment for balanced pairs and a matchday-3 mutual-draw uplift estimated from World Cup and Euro group stages since 1998 (shrunk to zero with k=30 matches). Output P(any of 12 groups). As-of = draw, updated after each matchday.

soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.label: Player-level tournament goal distributions with club attribution and knockout-round continuity
soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.mechanism: Each player's tournament goals are his share of team goals per match times minutes, summed over the team's matches; club pools sum players by club contract, hat tricks are per-match counts of 3+, and every-round scoring needs a goal in each of five knockout matches.
soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.rationale: Hat Trick counts concentrate in mismatch group games and in teams with a dominant finisher; Club Goals maximum is driven by clubs with many attackers at deep-running nations (Real Madrid, Manchester City, Bayern, PSG types); Goal in Every Game needs a finalist's player to score in five straight knockout matches, a tiny probability concentrated on penalty-taking strikers of favourites.
soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.measurement: Per player in the 26-man squads: npxG/90 and penalty duty (soc.player_xg, soc.penalty_taker_status logic) shrunk toward a position prior (k=900 minutes), expected minutes per match from soc.player_minutes_expectation, share of team lambda = player xG share. Per simulated match draw player goals as Poisson-thinned team goals (incl. ET). Output distribution of tournament hat tricks, max club total (club from squad list at tournament start), and P(any player scores in R32..Final). As-of = squad lists, updated with injuries and lineups.

soc.rare_goal_event_base_rates.label: Per-match base rates of direct free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals
soc.rare_goal_event_base_rates.mechanism: Each of these goal types is a rare event per match; P(at least one in 104 matches) = 1 - exp(-104 * rate) adjusted for taker quality, with rates differing by many orders of magnitude.
soc.rare_goal_event_base_rates.rationale: Direct free-kick goals occur a few times per World Cup (so YES is likely), olimpicos are rare (well under one per tournament on average) and open-play goalkeeper goals are almost unheard of at World Cups outside late set pieces; a model must use type-specific base rates rather than goal totals. Elite free-kick takers present raise the first.
soc.rare_goal_event_base_rates.measurement: From event data for World Cups, Euros and Copa Americas since 2010: counts of goals by type (direct free kick credited to taker, direct corner, goalkeeper scorer excluding own goals and shootouts) per match; Poisson rate with gamma prior from top-5 league rates per match (prior strength 200 matches); adjust free-kick rate by the share of squads with a designated taker whose club direct-FK conversion is above league median. As-of = squad lists.

soc.bracket_slot_graph.label: Official tournament match graph: slots, match numbers, venues and third-place allocation
soc.bracket_slot_graph.mechanism: The published schedule fixes which slot plays which, in what stadium and on what date; entrants to each knockout slot come from group finishing positions through a fixed mapping.
soc.bracket_slot_graph.rationale: Whether two teams can meet, and in which round, is fixed by structure: group winners and runners-up feed defined R32 slots, the eight best third-placed teams are assigned by an annex lookup depending on which groups they come from, and later slots follow the tree to the final and third-place match. A single wrong cell changes which pairs can meet in a Semifinal or a Quarterfinal, so the graph must be read from the regulations.
soc.bracket_slot_graph.measurement: Transcribe the regulation's match list into a directed graph: nodes are match numbers with date, city and stadium; edges map group position (1st, 2nd, best 3rd by combination) to slot. Encode the third-place table as a function of the set of qualifying third-place groups and validate that every combination yields a legal bracket. Test by checking against the official bracket for a hypothetical result. As-of = regulations publication; re-fetch if amended.

soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.label: Joint distribution of group finishing positions across all groups
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.mechanism: Simulated finishing order in each group plus the cross-group ranking of the twelve third-placed teams, from which the eight best advance.
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.rationale: Which team lands in a knockout slot depends on not just its own group but on the other groups through the best-thirds ranking. The cross-group coupling makes marginal group probabilities insufficient: the combination of third-place qualifiers decides slot assignment and so venue.
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.measurement: Simulate all group games with the team goal model, apply the group tie-break order transcribed from the 2026 regulations (secondary reports: points, then head-to-head points, goal difference and goals among tied teams, then overall goal difference and goals, then conduct score and FIFA ranking; unverified until Article 13 is read), rank third-placed teams on points, goal difference, goals scored, conduct and ranking, and output the joint distribution of slot occupants for each knockout match. 20000 draws minimum. As-of = last completed match.

soc.pair_meeting_probability.label: Probability a named pair of teams is confirmed as the matchup in any match, a named round or a final
soc.pair_meeting_probability.mechanism: For two teams, P(meet) = 1 if drawn in the same group (any-match wording), otherwise the sum over knockout rounds r of P(both occupy the two slots of the same round-r match), computed from the joint simulation because their paths share opponents.
soc.pair_meeting_probability.rationale: Teams in Game, Matchup, USA Opponent and the Champions League final all settle on joint slot occupancy at qualification. Marginal reach probabilities multiplied together are wrong: two teams on the same bracket side can meet only once and only before the final, and the best-third allocation makes cross-group meetings depend on other groups. Settlement at qualification means the R32-onward meeting is fixed as soon as both win the feeding ties.
soc.pair_meeting_probability.measurement: In each comp_sim draw (World Cup) or UEFA knockout simulation draw (Champions League), record for every pair the round in which they are confirmed in the same match (group, R32, R16, QF, SF, third place, final) and for USA the QF opponent or none. Output P(meet in any match), P(meet in round r) and the categorical over USA QF opponents including No Team; Monte Carlo standard error below 0.002 for pairs above 1%. As-of = after each completed match.

soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.label: Risk that scheduled World Cup games in a named host country/state are moved or not played
soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.mechanism: A host region settles YES if at least one of its scheduled games is played there before the deadline; NO requires every scheduled game in the region to be relocated, cancelled or abandoned before being played.
soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.rationale: Mexico had 13 scheduled matches (Mexico City, Guadalajara, Monterrey) and Massachusetts (Foxborough) several, so NO needs a region-wide failure: security events, political action to move games from certain US cities, immigration/visa disputes or stadium unavailability. The base rate is very low but the risk is news-driven and clustered, and it is independent of team results.
soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.measurement: For region r with n_r scheduled matches: base per-match relocation/cancellation hazard h0 = (relocated or cancelled matches)/(scheduled matches) in World Cups, Euros, Copa Americas and Olympics since 1990, Beta(0.5,50)-shrunk; region-level decision probability q_r from a dated news-flag ladder (0 none, 1 official statement of discussion, 2 formal FIFA review) with q_r = 0.002/0.03/0.20 priors, updated by Bayes with timestamped reports. P(no game in r) = q_r + (1-q_r)*h0^(n_r) assuming within-region independence given no decision. As-of = latest news timestamp.
raw_data: scheduled matches per host region with dates

soc.extra_time_phase_scoring_rate.label: Extra-time scoring rate conditional on reaching 90 minutes level
soc.extra_time_phase_scoring_rate.mechanism: Goal intensity in the 30 extra minutes differs from a pro-rata share of the 90-minute rate: legs are tired, a further substitution window opens, and both sides often trade risk for the shootout.
soc.extra_time_phase_scoring_rate.rationale: MOF/MOV contracts split level-at-90 mass between ET and penalties, so the ET rate (not the regulation rate) decides how much of that mass ends before a shootout. Pro-rating lambda_90 by 30/90 overstates ET goals in finals; the subtle part is that the discount depends on remaining substitutes and bench quality, which differ between the two sides.
soc.extra_time_phase_scoring_rate.measurement: From single-match knockout ties that went to extra time (finals, one-off rounds, single-tie domestic cups; second legs of two-legged ties are excluded or carried with an aggregate-level covariate because extra time there follows a level aggregate, not a level match) in UCL/UEL/UECL, World Cup, Euros, Copa America and top domestic cups since 2010: ET goals per 30 min divided by (model lambda_90 x 30/90) for the same match, fitted as a ratio with covariates (subs remaining at 90', bench xG-value per 90, red cards, final vs earlier round); shrink competition effects to the pooled ratio with k=40 matches; output per-team ET lambda as of the confirmed XI (T-60).

soc.late_level_risk_appetite.label: Late-regulation risk appetite when a knockout match is level
soc.late_level_risk_appetite.mechanism: In the last 15 minutes of a level single-match knockout, one or both teams often lower attacking intensity and accept extra time, so the hazard of a decisive goal falls below the in-play baseline.
soc.late_level_risk_appetite.rationale: The probability the match is level at 90 is not a pure function of team goal rates: if both teams slow down at 1-1 after 75', the regulation-draw cell is inflated relative to Poisson/Dixon-Coles even after the stage-level cagey factor. The effect is asymmetric: a weaker side or a side with a better shootout record has more reason to play for ET.
soc.late_level_risk_appetite.measurement: Event-level: goals and shots per minute in minutes 75-90+stoppage when the score is level in single-match knockouts versus level league matches with the same pre-match rating gap; expressed as the RESIDUAL ratio after the cagey-factor draw multiplier has already been applied (so it adds only late-level caution beyond the average stage effect); ratio estimated by competition tier with team random effect, shrink to pooled ratio with k=60 matches; split by pre-match underdog/favourite and by remaining substitutes; as-of = pre-match.

soc.neutral_final_venue_split.label: Neutral-venue final: crowd share, travel and pitch familiarity split
soc.neutral_final_venue_split.mechanism: Finals are played at pre-assigned neutral stadiums, so the usual home advantage is replaced by a partial advantage from ticket allocation, travel distance, climate and pitch familiarity.
soc.neutral_final_venue_split.rationale: Using league home advantage for a final mis-sets the strength gap and therefore the regulation-win versus level split. Allocation is often equal by rule, but secondary-market tickets, diaspora (e.g. World Cup matches in North America) and travel distance tilt it. The tilt is small; the risk is over-applying it.
soc.neutral_final_venue_split.measurement: Per final: x1 = official ticket-allocation share of side A minus side B; x2 = (great-circle km from B's base to venue - same for A)/1000; x3 = kickoff offset hours from team base time zone difference; x4 = indicator side played at the stadium in the last 24 months; de facto host flag if the venue country is a finalist's own (then use full soc.home_advantage). Regress goal difference residual (actual minus rating-based expectation, neutral venue) on x1..x4 over neutral-venue finals since 2000 with ridge so each coefficient prior is N(0, 0.05 goals); output the goal-rate offset. As-of announcement date.

soc.lead_protection_knockout_conversion.label: Knockout advancement probability after scoring first, by minute and strength gap
soc.lead_protection_knockout_conversion.mechanism: In single-match knockouts the side that scores first advances most of the time, but the conversion depends on the minute of the goal, the strength gap and whether extra time and penalties remain as an escape route for the trailing side.
soc.lead_protection_knockout_conversion.rationale: This is the conditional advancement curve the Messi-scores-first leg feeds into. It differs from league win probability after scoring first because a trailing team that equalises can still win in extra time or on penalties, and favourites who lead protect differently than underdogs.
soc.lead_protection_knockout_conversion.measurement: From knockout matches since 2002 (World Cup, Euros, Copa America, UCL/UEL knockouts): for each match, minute of first goal (5-min buckets), pre-match rating gap (Elo difference deciles) and whether the first scorer advanced; fit logistic P(advance | first goal minute, gap, scoring side) with spline on minute; shrink tournament-specific effects to pooled with k=50.

soc.prepack_leg_definition_parse.label: Parsed leg definitions of each prepack (windows, own goals, shootout, player participation)
soc.prepack_leg_definition_parse.mechanism: Each prepack leg may use a different settlement window and event definition; the combo settles YES only if every leg's own definition is met.
soc.prepack_leg_definition_parse.rationale: The sampled prepack counts the first goal across regulation, stoppage and extra time, while advancement includes penalties; the scorer leg has no stated rule for own goals, a goalless 120 minutes or the player not playing. A wrong parse changes the YES set, so it must be a recorded flag per series, not an assumption.

soc.return_to_play_timeline.label: Injury return-to-play timeline for a named player
soc.return_to_play_timeline.mechanism: A currently injured player re-enters selection only after a recovery period whose length depends on injury type, severity, setbacks and the club's or federation's medical caution.
soc.return_to_play_timeline.rationale: Window contracts (play before a date) are dominated by whether the player is fit for any qualifying match before the deadline; the right object is the distribution of the return date, which is right-skewed with setback risk, not a point estimate from a press release.
soc.return_to_play_timeline.measurement: Per player at the as-of date: injury type and body part, date of injury, reported expected absence; map to a reference-class return-time distribution (median and quantiles by injury type and age from historical absence records, e.g. hamstring grade 2 median about 3-5 weeks); add setback probability per injury type; update daily with training-return reports; output P(available on date d) for every date in the window.

soc.pair_onpitch_overlap_model.label: Joint on-pitch overlap probability for two named players
soc.pair_onpitch_overlap_model.mechanism: Two players are simultaneously on the pitch only if both are available and the coach uses them together, which depends on whether they are complements or substitutes for the same role.
soc.pair_onpitch_overlap_model.rationale: Marginal start probabilities miss positional competition: two midfielders who can each play the defensive midfield role may be rotated as alternatives, producing negative correlation, while two first-choice starters overlap almost surely when both are fit. The overlap is also helped by one starting and the other entering before the first leaves.
soc.pair_onpitch_overlap_model.measurement: Unit = club match in current and prior season under the same coach with both players fit. y=1 if both have >0 overlapping minutes on pitch. Logistic regression of y on both players' starting probabilities (from the soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement start model), competition type, days rest and same-position flag, with ridge penalty. Window probability = 1 - prod_m (1 - p_m) where availability states follow a two-state Markov chain per player (injury onset/recovery rates from soc.return_to_play_timeline), simulated 20000 times. As-of kickoff-1h.

soc.window_qualifying_fixture_count.label: Number and type of qualifying matches inside the contract window
soc.window_qualifying_fixture_count.mechanism: Window contracts are a union over matches; the more qualifying fixtures (official vs friendly, club vs national team) fall inside the window, the more chances to appear.
soc.window_qualifying_fixture_count.rationale: Calendars differ by window: a national-team window may have only a few friendlies before a tournament, a club window at season end may include a final matchday with heavy rotation, and an NWSL window spans a full season. Whether friendlies count is often unstated, so the count must be carried per scope reading.
soc.window_qualifying_fixture_count.measurement: For the subject team and window [as-of, deadline]: list scheduled fixtures with competition, official/friendly flag and date; conditional fixtures (cup replays, playoffs) weighted by survival probability; for national-team windows count official tournament matches (e.g. the USA's World Cup group and knockout games before the deadline) weighted by survival probability, separately from friendlies; output counts under each scope reading (official only; including friendlies); refreshed when fixtures are added or moved.

soc.registration_and_league_eligibility.label: Registration, contract and league eligibility to play for the named team
soc.registration_and_league_eligibility.mechanism: A player can appear for a team only if registered with it under the league's or federation's rules; this depends on contract status, transfer windows, roster limits and national-team eligibility.
soc.registration_and_league_eligibility.rationale: For contracts like 'plays for any NWSL team before a date' or 'plays for the national team before a date', the binding constraint can be off-field: an expired contract, an unfinished move abroad, a roster-registration deadline, or a federation switch. soc.national_team_call_up_history.label: Call-up, caps and minutes under the current national-team coach
soc.national_team_call_up_history.mechanism: National coaches pick final squads mostly from players they have repeatedly called up and used; a candidate's selection record in recent camps is the strongest single predictor of final-squad inclusion.
soc.national_team_call_up_history.rationale: Coach familiarity usually outweighs club form for established core players, but for fringe candidates and veterans recent club minutes and sharpness (soc.player_minutes_expectation) lead call-up changes: players absent from the last several camps are rarely added to a final list, while ever-present players are dropped mainly for injury. The input must be measured under the current coach because a new coach resets the pool.
soc.national_team_call_up_history.measurement: Per candidate at the as-of date: number of camps called up and matches started/minutes in the last 6 international windows under the current coach (weight w=0.7^k for window k back), caps, and, only where the federation publishes one, whether named in the latest provisional list (FIFA does not publish provisional lists, so this field is optional and often missing); shrink coach-specific rates to the federation's historical retention rate with k=4 windows.

soc.positional_slot_competition.label: Positional slot competition and quota for the final squad
soc.positional_slot_competition.mechanism: A final squad has a fixed number of slots with de facto positional quotas (three goalkeepers, two per full-back side, etc.), so inclusion is a ranking among direct rivals for those slots.
soc.positional_slot_competition.rationale: Selection is zero-sum within a position: a rival's injury or form surge changes a candidate's chance without any change in the candidate. Versatile players who cover two positions gain value in a squad of fixed size.
soc.positional_slot_competition.measurement: Per federation and position group g, quota Q_g = mean number of that position in the coach's last 2 final squads (round to integer, spread from the federation's last 3 tournaments). Selection score s_i = 0.4*callup_share (soc.national_team_call_up_history) + 0.3*club minutes share in last 10 matches (decay 0.9) + 0.2*international minutes share + 0.1*fit indicator, weights fitted by logistic regression on past final squads (leave-one-tournament-out). Simulate 20000 times: each rival injured with probability from soc.return_to_play_timeline and score perturbed with sd from the fit; P(included) = P(rank within quota); versatile players enter two queues, counted once. As-of date.
raw_data: past final squads of the coach by position

soc.squad_list_deadline_and_replacement_.label: Squad-list deadlines, size and late-replacement rules
soc.squad_list_deadline_and_replacement_.mechanism: Tournament regulations set the provisional and final list dates, squad size and conditions under which a named player may be replaced, all of which change what counts as final for settlement.
soc.squad_list_deadline_and_replacement_.rationale: KXWCSQUAD counts players added after the initial announcement but before the team's first match, and keeps a withdrawn player as YES.
