soc.squad_announcement_leak_reports.label: Pre-announcement reports of squad lists and starting XIs
soc.squad_announcement_leak_reports.mechanism: Journalists and federation sources often report squad lists or lineups hours to days before official release, with reliability varying by source.
soc.squad_announcement_leak_reports.rationale: Squad and XI decisions are made before they are announced; credible leaks move the probability close to 0 or 1 ahead of the official list. Source tiering is essential because speculative lists are common. Same tier-weighted method as the existing soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal, kept as a separate input because that definition is specific to award-winner leaks and its calibration sample (past award ceremonies) does not transfer to squad lists and starting XIs.
soc.squad_announcement_leak_reports.measurement: Log each report with timestamp, tier (official, established beat reporter, aggregator) and claimed in/out or starter/bench. Per tier t, accuracy a_t = share of its past claims later confirmed by the official list (2018-2025 tournaments, Beta(2,1) prior); claim LR = a_t/(1-a_t) per independent source, log-odds summed with same-upstream reports counted once and total |log LR| capped at 4. As-of report timestamp; the official list is used only for back-testing.

soc.player_tournament_participation_inte.label: Player's stated intent to take part (retirement, availability declarations)
soc.player_tournament_participation_inte.mechanism: Veteran stars can self-select out through retirement or by declaring themselves unavailable, and late-career players sometimes signal intent long before the squad is named.
soc.player_tournament_participation_inte.rationale: For marquee veterans the coach's choice is close to automatic if the player wants to go; the residual risk is the player's decision and his late-season fitness, not competition for the slot.
soc.player_tournament_participation_inte.measurement: Log each statement with timestamp and class (retired, will be available, undecided). State weight w = 0.5^(days since statement/60); P(named | available) from the base rate of veterans (30+) who declared availability and were named across 2010-2024 squad lists, Beta(2,1)-shrunk; P(named | retired)=0.02 unless a dated reversal exists; P(final) = P(intent state) * P(fit by list deadline) with P(fit) from soc.return_to_play_timeline. As-of statement timestamp; never use later statements.

soc.current_win_run_state.label: Current consecutive-win run and threshold status at the as-of date
soc.current_win_run_state.mechanism: A streak contract is path dependent: the probability of reaching N consecutive wins depends on how many consecutive wins the team already has and whether the threshold has already been reached inside the window.
soc.current_win_run_state.rationale: Once five straight wins occur in the window the contract is settled YES (absorbing state); before that, a team on a three-win run needs only two more, so the as-of run length changes the probability far more than any rating change. Runs that started before the window boundary may or may not count.
soc.current_win_run_state.measurement: At the as-of timestamp: number of consecutive wins in all counted competitions ending at the latest completed match, split into wins inside and before the window start; max run achieved inside the window so far; indicator threshold_reached; applied rule for wins on penalties per the scope flags; recomputed after each match.

soc.calendar_year_fixture_sequence.label: Ordered fixture sequence across a calendar year spanning two seasons
soc.calendar_year_fixture_sequence.mechanism: A calendar-year window crosses the end of one season and the start of the next, with a summer gap, a World Cup in 2026, and cup fixtures whose existence depends on survival.
soc.calendar_year_fixture_sequence.rationale: Streaks need consecutive wins in an ordered list, so the order of hard and easy fixtures matters: five winnable matches in a row are far likelier to produce a streak than the same matches split by away games at top sides. soc.season_boundary_strength_reset.label: Strength change across the summer between seasons
soc.season_boundary_strength_reset.mechanism: Squad turnover, transfers, a new manager or tactical change over the summer can move team strength materially between the spring and autumn halves of a calendar-year window.
soc.season_boundary_strength_reset.rationale: A single rating applied to the whole year misstates the autumn win probabilities; the uncertainty about the reset is large at the as-of date and is shared across all autumn matches, which widens the streak probability's dependence on one latent variable.
soc.season_boundary_strength_reset.measurement: Per club: change in pre-season rating relative to end-of-season rating in each of the last 10 summers (from Elo or xG ratings), regressed on net transfer spend relative to squad value, manager change and departures of top-minute players; forecast distribution of the summer shift as of the as-of date, sd shrunk to the league-wide sd of summer shifts.

soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.label: Promotion and relegation play-off bracket conversion
soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.mechanism: Maps the simulated regular-season rank to the probability of promotion (or survival) through the competition's post-season play-off bracket, tie by tie, under that season's format rules.
soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.rationale: Promotion series settle on being promoted by any route, so ranks 3-8 (EFL Championship from 2026-27) or 3-6 (Segunda) carry probability through a short knockout: the format decides how much rank matters. The EFL six-team format adds single-leg eliminators hosted by the higher seed, so 5th-8th face an extra ~50% gate that 3rd and 4th skip; in Segunda the better-placed side wins a level tie after extra time, which tilts every semi and the final toward the higher seed with no shootout coin-flip. Subtle: the Segunda reserve-team rule (filial sides ineligible) shifts which ranks qualify, and formats change between seasons (EFL change confirmed March 2026, final details pending).
soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.measurement: Per competition-season, encode the format: entrant ranks, round structure, legs, host rule, away-goals (none in either), extra time and tie-break (EFL: ET then penalties; Segunda: ET then higher regular-season rank). For each simulated final table, simulate each tie with team goal rates from the as-of ratings: single legs via soc.extra_time_shootout_model at the higher seed's venue, two-leg ties via soc.tie_advancement_state_tree (second leg at the higher seed), Segunda ties replacing the shootout branch with P=1 for the higher seed. P(promoted_i) = sum over simulated tables of [rank_i automatic] + [rank_i in play-off] x P(win bracket | bracket draw). Calibrate P(win bracket | seed) against 20 seasons of EFL and Segunda play-off results (Wilson intervals, shrink to the simulation with k=10 seasons). As-of: format rules published before the season; ratings as of the pricing timestamp.

game_side.mechanism: Match-side markets (1X2, two-way, handicap, exact score, first-half and second-half results) are settled by the joint goal difference in a defined window. The mechanism is a latent attack/defence strength per team, adjusted for opponent and venue, converted to a goal distribution with low-score dependence, then modified by who plays (confirmed XI), rest/rotation, motivation and a game-state process. The market's sharp price carries much of this information, so the incremental inputs are those that arrive late or are mispriced (lineups, rotation, stakes) plus market-structure details.
game_side.target: Win/draw/loss or goal-difference threshold in regulation (or a half), as defined in the rules text.

inputs.why: Opponent- and venue-adjusted xG attack/defence is the base strength estimate for the goal-difference distribution.
Elo/Dixon-Coles ratings provide the long-memory prior that stabilises noisy xG samples.
Team/league-specific home offset shifts both goal rates and draw probabilities.
Low-score dependence sets draw and 1-0/0-1 cells that dominate side markets.
Confirmed lineup quality vs typical XI converts team news into a strength adjustment.
Predicting rotation before the XI release gives an early signal when quotes are stale.
Key absences and suspensions known days ahead shift expected goal difference.
Match importance for each side alters effort, rotation and draw acceptability.
Team-pair draw tendency beyond Poisson baselines for 3-way prices.
Past finishing over-performance should be shrunk, not extrapolated.
De-vigged sharp closing odds are the benchmark prior any model must beat.
Quote path shows when the Kalshi price last absorbed team news.
Wording decides regulation-only vs advancement and abandonment/void handling.
Raw and state-adjusted team xG for/against feeds the adjusted rating and sanity-checks goal-based ratings.
Timestamped confirmed XI: only lineups visible before the decision time may be used, and quotes before release are stale.
Qualitative stakes (title, survival, cup priority) that the leverage index quantifies.
Days of rest and travel feed fatigue and rotation expectations for both sides.
Tactical matchup residual visible once the XI is out.
Derbies compress goal margins and raise cards, nudging results toward draws.
Long trips matter in continental cups and tournaments, mostly for the away side.
Depth at the touch decides whether any model edge is executable.
Fee drag sets the minimum net edge for a trade.
Realised settlement labels for calibration of the model.

interactions.hypothesis: A rating built on full-strength XIs should be reduced in proportion to the confirmed XI shortfall; the interaction is multiplicative in the attack/defence components, not additive.
Low-leverage matches raise rotation probability, so the expected-XI shift is larger exactly when stakes are low and the effect on the draw probability is largest.
Strong home edge moves mass from draw to home win in evenly matched sides; weak-HFA venues (neutral, empty stadium) raise draw share.
The edge from comparing a model with sharp odds depends on correcting favourite-longshot and draw-price distortions, otherwise the apparent gap is a de-vig artefact.
Quote adaptation after lineup release measures how stale pre-XI quotes were and when informed flow arrives.

game_total.mechanism: Total-goal style markets (over/under rungs, team totals, BTTS, first-half totals) are determined by the sum of two correlated count processes. The mechanism is each team's expected goals (attack vs opponent defence), a dependence structure that handles low scores, a tempo/openness factor from both teams' styles, weather, referee/penalty tendencies and lineup quality, and game-state feedback (leading teams sit deep). Strength uncertainty fattens tails so high rungs are more probable than a plain Poisson implies.
game_total.target: Total goals (or team total / both-score events) in the contract's time window relative to a strike.

inputs.why: Adjusted xG attack and defence give the two lambdas whose sum is the total.
The count distribution (over-dispersion and dependence) converts lambdas into ladder rung probabilities.
Low-score cells matter most for 0.5/1.5 rungs and BTTS.
Team-pair tempo and pressing change shot volume and openness.
Scoring-probability and clean-sheet propensities set BTTS and team-total rungs.
Keeper quality changes the conversion of shots on target to goals.
Starting lineup changes attack and defence strengths separately.
Wind/rain/heat mildly reduce quality and tempo.
Penalties add high-xG events with referee/VAR variation.
Set-piece xG is a persistent goal source for underdogs and in cagey games.
League-season goal baseline anchors the intercept of all lambdas.
Market-implied lambdas enable cross-rung consistency checks.
Cross-rung consistency exposes mispriced thresholds.
Historical realised frequency per rung checks calibration.
Open-play and set-piece xG for/against by team is the raw material of the lambdas.
Shot volume by game state gives tempo/volume cross-check to xG.
Corner volume reflects wing play and territorial pressure, correlated with totals.
Card/foul tempo and red-card risk change game flow and variance.
Attacking vs defensive formations change openness.
Confirmed lineups give the actual attack/defence units.
Rest and congestion alter intensity and rotation.
State-adjusted xG removes the bias of being ahead/behind in sampled matches.
VAR reviews shift disallowed goals/penalties and stoppage time.
Longer added time raises late-goal chances.
Liquidity by rung indicates which rungs are efficiently priced.
Realised totals for calibration by rung.

interactions.hypothesis: Two high-tempo teams raise total xG more than the sum of main effects, so tempo scales both teams' lambdas rather than adding a constant.
Wind/rain hurt possession-based high-press sides more than direct teams, so the weather effect on totals depends on style.
Over-dispersion and rho shape the whole ladder; a mis-specified distribution creates systematic residuals that look like per-rung mispricing.
Keeper changes interact with outfield rotation: a weaker defence in front of a weaker keeper raises opponent goal expectation convexly.

season_outcome.mechanism: Season-outcome futures (title, top-N, relegation, qualification, advancement, outright, host, trophies) are the outcome of a stochastic tournament: remaining fixtures are simulated from team strengths with uncertainty and drift, then tiebreak and slot rules are applied. The mechanism is the aggregate of many match outcomes, so value comes from correct rating uncertainty, schedule strength, rule details, squad depth and injuries, and correlation across teams. Long-horizon prices embed more information drift than match prices, so the underlying rating prior and rule parsing matter most.
season_outcome.target: Final league position/qualification/advancement or trophy outcome, as defined by competition rules and the contract wording.

inputs.why: Fixture-by-fixture Monte Carlo is the structural engine that maps strengths to season outcomes.
Strength posterior and drift determine tail probabilities and avoid over-sharp futures.
Order, venues and rival fixtures shift expected points among equal-rated teams.
Tiebreak order and slot allocation decide close cut-offs.
Sanctions shift points irrespective of on-pitch strength.
Depth affects strength under injuries and congestion over the horizon.
Current long-term absences adjust remaining-season strength.
Window moves and manager changes update stale ratings.
Early-season futures lean on priors until matches accumulate.
Multi-competition load links separate futures for the same team.
Leverage tells which remaining fixtures matter for the cut-off.
Sharp futures and match prices are strong priors for ratings.
Contract wording defines the exact qualifying outcome (including playoff/ET handling).
Top-N rungs must be consistent with winner and relegation probabilities.
xG-based ratings are less noisy than points for long-horizon strength.
Elo/Dixon-Coles ratings are the strength input to the simulation.
Late-season incentives change effort and rotation in simulated fixtures.
Postponed/abandoned fixtures reshuffle the schedule and can void markets.
Knockout advancement beyond 90 minutes includes shootouts.
Advancement-wording markets include extra time and penalties.
Aggregate state in two-legged ties.

interactions.hypothesis: Propagating strength uncertainty into the simulation flattens title/relegation probabilities relative to fixed-strength sims; the flattening is largest for the favourites and near the cut.
Schedule matters most when the table is tight and tiebreaks (H2H, GD) decide; the interaction is non-linear near cut-off.
Teams in multiple competitions with thin squads lose more strength in the league run-in, so depth interacts with cup progression.
A deduction changes who reaches a tiebreak and which tiebreak applies, creating non-additive effects in relegation and qualification markets.

season_stat.mechanism: Season-stat markets (team points, points margin, player total, season leader) settle on an accumulated count over remaining fixtures. The mechanism is a sum of match-level processes (points or goals) with strength uncertainty, rotation and injury risk, and tie-break or rounding rules. Player stats additionally depend on minutes, role, penalty duty and finishing luck regression; team points depend on schedule strength and draw variance.
season_stat.target: A season-end count (points, goals, assists, margin) relative to a threshold or relative to another entity.

inputs.why: Full distribution (variance, skew) of points for threshold and margin markets.
Remaining opponents and venues set expected additional points.
Posterior strength uncertainty widens the distribution of totals.
Current tally, minutes and remaining fixtures set player race outcomes.
Player shot volume and shot quality produce expected remaining goals/assists.
Expected minutes are the largest uncertainty for player counting stats.
Penalty duty adds high-xG chances for scoring totals.
Observed over-performance should be shrunk toward xG-implied production.
Injury hazard truncates player and team output.
Draw variance drives dispersion of points totals.
Defines what is counted (league only, own goals, tie-break rules).
Threshold ladder must be consistent with distribution.
Team-level xG is the strength basis for expected points.
Dead-rubber effects on late-season points.
Shot volume supports player-level rate estimation.
Set-piece role contributes to scoring totals.

interactions.hypothesis: Expected goals scale with minutes times per-90 rate, so uncertainty in minutes dominates when per-90 rates are stable; the product is the primary mean driver.
A leader with large positive finishing delta is overrated by the tally; the gap to chasers should be reduced by the regression term.
Teams with higher draw propensity have narrower points variance for the same mean, so thresholds near the mean differ.

off_field.mechanism: Off-field and novelty soccer markets (transfers, managerial changes, rule changes, competition hosts, special events) are decided by committees, clubs and individuals rather than by on-pitch performance. The mechanism is information flow and incentives: reporters' leaks, deadlines, evaluation reports, club finances and political preferences. There is no standard predictive model; the useful inputs are timeline structure, base rates of rumour-to-confirmation conversion, resolution wording, and market microstructure.
off_field.target: A discrete announcement or event (appointment, host selection, transfer) that is formally confirmed by an official source before a deadline.

inputs.why: Decision calendars and base rates of leaks converting to announcements.
Transfer/manager news flow and club finances shape probabilities.
Administrative/regulatory processes follow official timelines.
Rules and eligibility criteria set which outcomes are possible.
Wording defines what counts as official confirmation and the cut-off time.
Price path reveals when leaks reached the market.
Order-flow around news windows shows informed trading.
Volume shows whether the price reflects much information.
Open/close/halt timing relative to the announcement date.
Manager statements timestamp announcements and intentions.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability that matters is the chance of an official confirmation inside the contract window, so base rates must be conditioned on deadline and wording.
Price jumps accompanied by signed trade imbalance indicate informed leaks; jumps without flow indicate stale quote repricing.

player_other.mechanism: Head-to-head and other player/team comparison markets resolve on the relative performance of two entities (finish higher, score more) rather than absolute levels. The mechanism is joint simulation: two entities share the same league structure (direct match, shared rating uncertainty) so outcomes are dependent, and the relevant input set is differences in rating, schedule, injuries and the correlation structure rather than marginal probabilities.
player_other.target: Which of two teams/players ends ahead on a defined metric at a defined time.

inputs.why: Joint dependence between the two entities' outcomes.
Joint Monte Carlo gives P(A ahead of B).
Shared and independent strength uncertainty control tail probability.
Differences in remaining fixtures matter.
Differential injuries/suspensions shift relative strength.
Depth affects long-horizon relative strength.
Tie-break rule decides which entity is 'ahead' when equal.
Defines the metric, tie and void handling.
Sharp prices for each entity give a cross-check.
Team xG gives a performance-based cross-check on league position.

interactions.hypothesis: Direct meetings plus common rivals create dependence; P(A>B) differs from the ratio of marginal probabilities.
Ties on points occur frequently enough that the tiebreak rule changes the comparison probability materially.

season_award.mechanism: Season-award markets resolve by voters or juries who combine production statistics, team success and narrative. The mechanism is a ranking function: individual production (goals, assists, xG, defensive actions), team trophies, tournament results, and exposure. Probabilities depend heavily on the awarding body's criteria and timing, and on the competing candidates' paths to trophies.
season_award.target: Winner of a named individual award decided by a defined panel/process.

inputs.why: Voting criteria, narrative and team success drive the choice.
Production totals feed the production component.
Underlying shot/chance production vs finishing luck.
Counting-stat race state matters for stat-heavy awards.
Team trophy probabilities flow into award probabilities.
Availability and minutes over the eligible window.
Injury risk for candidates before the vote date.
Eligibility window, voting body and tie rules are in the contract.
Bookmaker award prices aggregate narrative information.
Team strength context for award narratives.

interactions.hypothesis: Award odds are conditionally linked to team trophies, so probabilities must be computed jointly with competition outcomes.
Voters see goals not xG; counting stats inflated by finishing luck still win votes, so the regression term applies to the stats not the vote.

period.mechanism: Period markets (first-half result/total/handicap/exact score, second-half result) are settled on a sub-window of the match. The mechanism is the same goal process cut by time: first-half goal rate is below the full-match average share, early dynamics are cautious, and half-specific dependence leads to many 0-0 and 1-1 first halves. Lineup information and game-state dynamics matter differently by half, and added time at half-time interacts with rules text.
period.target: Result/goal count within the first or second half under the wording of the contract.

inputs.why: Half-specific share of goals converts match lambda into period lambda.
Team strength still drives the period difference, with larger noise.
Half-time distributions are low-count so dependence is large.
Second-half dynamics depend on first-half state and substitutions.
Timing of the first goal determines early-half outcomes.
Starters matter more in the first half before substitutions.
High-press sides front-load chances.
First-half draws are very frequent so draw modelling dominates.
Half definition (including stoppage time) and abandonment handling.
Period ladders must be consistent with full-time markets.
Team xG per half style gives the strength baseline.
Starting XI is what plays most of the first half.
Early corners reflect territorial pressure.
Early shot volume reflects tempo.

interactions.hypothesis: Pressing teams concentrate chances earlier, raising their first-half share; the period share depends on style not just league average.
Second-half goal rate is conditional on half-time score; the unconditional split averages over states that change risk-taking.
A high first-half draw share comes from both dependence and low lambda; they must be modelled jointly to price half-time draws.

first_event.mechanism: First-event markets (first team to score) depend on the competing hazard rates of the two teams, the probability of no goal at all, and the time-dependence of scoring intensity. The mechanism is a race of two inhomogeneous Poisson processes truncated by the end of the match: the leading probability of scoring first is lambda_A share modified by the probability of a goalless draw, penalties and set-piece timing, and lineup information.
first_event.target: Which team scores first (or none) as defined in the rules.

inputs.why: Minute-resolved hazards define the race and the null outcome.
Relative team strength sets the hazard ratio.
P(0-0) determines the null outcome mass.
Set-piece and early-press attacking patterns affect early hazard.
Lineups shift attacking hazard.
Penalties and own-goals create abrupt first-goal events.
Early goals depend on first-half scoring share.
How a goalless match, own goal and abandoned match settle.
Consistent with match result and total markets.
Team chance creation sets the hazard ratio.
Starters determine early threat.
Early shot volume and shot quality.

interactions.hypothesis: The goalless-match probability is both a hazard integral and a Dixon-Coles cell, so they should be consistent; inconsistencies flag model error.
Teams reliant on set pieces have fewer early open-play goals and lower early hazard until dead-ball opportunities occur.

match_result_3way.label: Match result (3-way / two-way winner)
match_result_3way.target: Home/draw/away outcome after regulation time (or per wording for two-way).
match_result_3way.mechanism: A joint goal model converts opponent-adjusted attack/defence strengths and home advantage into the 3-way probability vector. The draw is the hard part: it depends on closeness, total expected goals, Dixon-Coles dependence and team draw propensity. Incremental information arrives through confirmed lineups, rotation and stakes, so the price must be updated for team news that is stale in earlier quotes. A two-way winner wording changes how draws are treated (void/advancement/extra time) and must be parsed.

inputs.why: Opponent-adjusted attack/defence is the main strength estimate.
Long-memory Elo/DC prior to stabilise xG ratings.
Team/league-specific home goal-rate offset.
Drives draw and narrow-win probabilities.
Team-pair draw tendency beyond baseline.
Confirmed XI quality shift - the channel through which it moves the Match result (3-way / two-way winner) price.
Pre-XI probability of rotation.
Effort/rotation incentive - the channel through which it moves the Match result (3-way / two-way winner) price.
Fatigue and rest for each side.
Keeper quality shifts conceded goals.
Referee penalty and foul tendencies move result probability slightly.
Sharp de-vigged 1X2 is the benchmark.
Regulation vs advancement and void wording.
Confirmed XI timestamped before the Kalshi decision time.
Stakes narrative converted into leverage.
Rest and travel for both teams.
Raw xG feed into adjusted ratings.
Tactical matchup residual - the channel through which it moves the Match result (3-way / two-way winner) price.
Derby compression of margins - the channel through which it moves the Match result (3-way / two-way winner) price.
Marks when lineup information is new relative to an expectation formed hours earlier; the outcome effect itself is carried by soc.xi_strength_delta.
A first-order home advantage driver in the Bolivian, Ecuadorian and Colombian leagues in this ledger bucket.
Friendlies appear in the ledger bucket (KXCLUBFGAME) with settlement identical to competitive matches but a distinct data-generating process.
Sets the scoring environment and draw mass for GAME series that are not standard 11-a-side fixtures.

interactions.hypothesis: Lineup shortfalls reduce the attack/defence components separately, so a missing striker mainly lowers own goals and a missing centre-back mainly raises opponent goals.
Dead-rubber matches raise rotation, which changes both expected strength and the draw share.
Evenly matched teams at a strong-HFA venue convert draw mass to home wins; in neutral venues the draw share is higher.
Price comparison needs favourite-longshot and draw-bias correction to avoid false edges on the draw rung.

The result impact of a missing player scales with team dependence on him and with opponent strength; a surprise absence of a star in a close match moves P(win) by an unmeasured amount (a few points is a hypothesis) while the same absence in a mismatch barely matters.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress outcome on surprise times rating gap; compare to additive.

interactions.hypothesis: Altitude adds to the home advantage once the visitor altitude gap exceeds about 500 m (the single breakpoint used throughout this record), rises roughly linearly above it and saturates for well-acclimatised sides near 3,000 m; the 500 m and 3,000 m values are hypotheses to be fitted, not established thresholds.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit home effect by altitude bins in Bolivian/Ecuadorian leagues.

interactions.hypothesis: Rotation is most likely precisely when stakes are low and the next match is bigger, so rotation times (1 - leverage) predicts strength cuts; stakes alone does not.
interactions.how_to_test: Interaction regression of lineup strength on rotation index and leverage.

interactions.hypothesis: Draw probability is determined jointly by the expected goal difference (peaks at 0), the total goals (lower totals raise draws) and rho; a rating-only model gets the ordering right but misprices the draw because it ignores total-goal environment.
interactions.how_to_test: Calibrate P(draw) against total expected goals and gap; check by decile.

interactions.hypothesis: In friendlies the effective rating gap is compressed (rotation, substitutions) and the variance is higher, so P(favourite win) is a flattened function of the rating gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate slope of win probability on rating gap separately for friendlies.

interactions.hypothesis: League-estimated draw propensity applies only under the 11-a-side 90-minute regime; in all-star and small-sided formats the higher goal rate collapses the draw mass, so the draw input must be replaced, not adjusted, when the format profile changes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised draw rates in All-Star/Baller League games with the league-model prediction for equal-strength pairings.

nonlinearities.shape: Ordered-logit style S-curve in rating gap for win probability; draw peaks at zero
nonlinearities.why: P(home win) and P(away win) are logistic in the gap, while P(draw) is hump-shaped; a linear gap feature cannot represent the draw leg.

nonlinearities.shape: Zero below a 500 m gap, roughly linear above it, saturating near 3000 m (breakpoints are hypotheses to be fitted)
nonlinearities.why: The physiological penalty to acclimatised visitors saturates at extreme altitude and is minimal below the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: Possibly asymmetric: bad surprises may count more than good ones (hypothesis, unsupported)
nonlinearities.why: A key absence may reduce output more than a returning starter raises it because replacement quality is below the starter by more than depth adds; the asymmetry is an unsupported hypothesis and is not tied to market expectations.

mechanism_review.summary: The 3-way result is the sign of the regulation goal difference, with the draw as a separate priced leg. Expected goal difference comes from adjusted team strengths and team-specific home advantage, then moves with the actual lineup (the part that was not predicted), rotation and stakes, fatigue and travel, and for specific leagues altitude. The draw probability depends on the total goal environment and on low-cell dependence, peaking when teams are balanced and totals are low; referee shocks and red cards add rare large effects. The contract settles on 90 minutes plus stoppage time with extra time and penalties excluded and a fair-price void for postponements, and friendlies and cups share the same settlement but different incentives.

stages.name: Team strength differential
stages.description: The expected goal difference comes from opponent-adjusted attack and defence strengths with decay and shrinkage, plus home advantage by team and league, and a preseason or promotion prior when evidence is thin. The rating gap, scaled by the competition's goal environment, sets the shape of win/draw/loss probabilities.
stages.distribution: Latent strengths are Bayesian posteriors with sd about 0.1-0.15 in log goal-rate; three-way outcome follows from a bivariate goal model.

stages.name: Who plays: lineup, rotation and surprise
stages.description: The outcome depends on the quality of the XI that actually plays; the deviation of the actual lineup from the predicted one is only a timing construct for when information arrives, together with suspensions, injuries to key players and manager rotation in congested weeks. A missing goalkeeper or playmaker is worth roughly 0.1-0.25 goals of expected goal difference.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup scenarios; effect on goal difference is heavy-tailed and sparse (most matches change little, some change a lot).

stages.name: Fatigue, travel and situational context
stages.description: Rest days, minutes load, travel and time-zone change, international-break returns and the stakes of the match (title or relegation leverage, dead rubbers, rivalry) shift effort and rotation; altitude and heat in parts of South America and CONCACAF alter the physiological advantage of the home side far beyond ordinary home advantage. The size of the altitude penalty (a few tenths of a goal in extreme cases) is unsourced and to be estimated.
stages.distribution: Smaller effects (0.05-0.15 goals) except altitude which can be 0.3-0.5 goals; many correlated small shocks.

stages.name: Draw mass and low-scoring structure
stages.description: The draw is the most mispriced outcome: its probability depends on the total goal environment (lower totals raise draws), on the dependence between teams in low cells (Dixon-Coles) and on team-specific draw tendencies from style (low-block, cagey sides). Draw probability is about 26% on average, peaking when expected goal difference is near zero.
stages.distribution: Discrete 0-0/1-1 cell masses; draw rate is bounded in the 20-33% range for league games with a peak at balanced matches.

stages.name: Officiating and shocks
stages.description: Referee choices (penalties about 0.3 per match, red cards about 0.1) and VAR create sudden shifts in the match; a first-half red card changes the expected goal difference by about 0.5 goals. These are mostly unpredictable but have referee-level baselines.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete shocks with large effects; right skewed on goal difference.

stages.name: Settlement and market-type bookkeeping
stages.description: Settlement is the 90-minute score; the contract boundary must be correctly implemented for cup ties, and the three outcome markets must be consistent. Friendlies and cups use different incentive structure but the same settlement; the market-derived odds are only a benchmark for validation.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the final regulation score; no randomness beyond the match.

stages.name: Non-standard formats: all-star, college and small-sided games
stages.description: A minority of GAME series are not ordinary 11-a-side competitive fixtures: the MLS All-Star Game pits selected squads with mass substitutions and low defensive effort, NCAA games use unlimited re-entry substitutions and different squad depth, and Baller League games are short small-sided matches with their own clock and scoring rules. For these the goal rate, home advantage and draw mass cannot be borrowed from league models; the format profile (match length, players per side, substitution rule, how a level game is decided) sets the scoring environment and the tie probability, and team strength must come from the competition's own results.
stages.distribution: Format-specific: all-star and small-sided games have high goal rates and thin draw mass; college games resemble lower-tier league games with larger rating uncertainty.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted attack/defence and team-specific home advantage supply the expected goal difference.

opponent_matchup.note: Style interaction (pressing versus low block) and derby effects on draw rate.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager rotation habits and tactical system.

environment.note: Altitude, travel and time zones plus heat, humidity and pitch conditions from soc.weather (added) cover the environment channel.

game_context_script.note: Aggregate state and stakes dictate risk taking and draw rate; soc.second_leg_aggregate_state is a catalog-defined input that is not in this archetype audit list and is therefore unaudited here.

pace_volume.note: Chance volume from xG-based strength; tempo effects on result are second order for a 3-way outcome.

efficiency_conversion.note: Goalkeeper shot-stopping and finishing; both shrunk.

distribution_variance.note: Draw mass shaped by low-cell dependence and team tendency.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Congestion, stakes and the special case of friendlies.

officiating_rules.note: Referee/VAR-shrunk penalty award rate (soc.penalty_rate, added) is the main officiating input; soc.referee is audited WEAK and is secondary cover only.

settlement_contract.note: Regulation-only counting, Tie as a separate outcome and the 48-hour fair-price clause are parsed from the rules text; soc.market_odds is a BENCHMARK_ONLY audit item and is not an input to any stage or category.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Each match has three mutually exclusive binaries (home wins, away wins, 'Tie is the result'), settled on the score after 90 minutes plus stoppage time; extra time and penalties are explicitly excluded, so in cup ties a team that wins on penalties still leaves 'Tie' as the YES outcome. Club matches cancelled or rescheduled more than 48 hours away resolve to a fair price; eight series use 'over two weeks away' instead (KXWCGAME, KXFIFAGAME, KXAFCACGAME, KXINTERCONCUPGAME, KXFINALISSIMAGAME, KXCONCACAFCCUPGAME, KXESPSUPERCUPGAME, KXITASUPERCUPGAME); KXCLUBWCGAME has a third clause: a postponed game keeps the market open until the rescheduled game is played (within two years), and a cancelled game not played resolves 33/33/33 across Tie and both team markets. All 155 live series are single-match GAME series (143 with rules text, 12 TITLE_ONLY); the exception is KXBALLERLEAGUEGAME (Baller League small-sided format), whose text ('If Club 360 and Super Ninos tie in the ... Baller League soccer game') states no 90-minute window and no postponement clause.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official match report score at full time of regulation (90 minutes plus stoppage time) from the competition's governing body, which Kalshi's data provider mirrors; extra time and shootouts not used.
variants_and_edge_cases: Three binaries per match must be coherent: P(home)+P(draw)+P(away)=1; each is its own series entry (e.g. KXMLSGAME ticker suffix -TIE vs team codes), so mispricing can sit in the draw leg alone.

Some texts phrase the draw leg as 'If Tie wins the ...' (KXFIFAGAME, KXINTERCONCUPGAME) rather than 'Tie is the result'; both are the same 3-way partition. No two-way (no-draw) soccer winner text exists in the 143 texts read.

Cup ties, club friendlies and Libertadores/Sudamericana knockouts mix incentives (aggregate state, rotation, substitution waves up to 6 players) under the same 90-minute settlement; two-leg aggregate position changes the draw rate without changing the contract.
Stoppage time is part of the window: late goals in 90+ minutes count, and 90+N length depends on VAR and substitution; abandonment mid-match (weather, crowd) is not covered in the sampled text.

Exhibition and non-standard formats share the 3-way wording: MLS All-Star Game (KXMLSASTGAME, MLS vs Liga MX all-stars), NCAA men's soccer (KXNCAAMSOCCERGAME), club friendlies; Baller League is a small-sided format with its own match length and tie rules (stage s7).

Postponement clauses differ: 48 hours (most club texts), two weeks (eight tournament and super-cup texts), and KXCLUBWCGAME's stay-open-then-1/3-each rule for a cancelled game; Baller League has none.

total_goals.label: Total goals and team totals
total_goals.target: Total (or team) goals in regulation relative to a strike ladder.
total_goals.mechanism: Total goals is the sum of two correlated, over-dispersed count processes. Price requires team-pair lambdas (attack x opposing defence, home effect), tempo/openness, lineup quality, set-piece/penalty channels and a count distribution that handles low scores and uncertainty. The ladder of rungs must form a consistent distribution; kinks across rungs indicate pricing noise. Weather, referee and game state add smaller adjustments.

inputs.why: Adjusted xG sets the two lambdas.
Tempo/pressing sets shot volume.
Count distribution with dependence/over-dispersion.
Low rungs and 0-0 probability.
Confirmed lineups for both attack and defence.
Keeper quality modulates conversion.
Set-piece xG source - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Wind/rain/heat effect on tempo and quality.
Penalty/foul tendencies - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Baseline goals per game - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Market-implied lambdas - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Cross-rung consistency - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Calibration per strike - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Team xG is the base of both lambdas.
Shot volume cross-check - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Corner volume and territorial play.
Tempo/red-card variance - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Confirmed XI units - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
State-adjusted xG - the channel through which it moves the Total goals and team totals price.
Over- or under-performance against xG regresses, so totals should use xG not goals.
Goalkeeper save luck regresses.
The sampled strikes of 5.5 to 7.5 make tail multipliers the first-order calibration term.
Directly models correlation between the team counts that drives the tails of totals.
Totals respond to the sum of attack and defence changes with different signs for each side.

interactions.hypothesis: Tempo scales both teams' lambdas multiplicatively, so high-tempo matchups of two attacking sides produce more extra goals than additive terms predict.
Weather suppresses possession-and-press styles more than direct styles, changing the weather sign by matchup.
Rung residuals vs a fitted distribution identify mispricing independent of team views.
A weaker keeper plus a rotated defence raises opponent scoring convexly.

A shared latent openness factor multiplies both lambdas, so Var(total) exceeds the sum of lambdas by a term growing with (lambda_H + lambda_A) squared: mismatches with a high summed lambda amplify the tail more than balanced low-lambda games.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit gamma by league and check calibration of P(total>=5) in high-lambda games.

interactions.hypothesis: A missing centre-back raises the total only if the opponent has strong attack ratings, and a missing striker lowers it only if the side's chances are concentrated in him; the lineup split effect is conditional on opponent attack quality from the ratings.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress totals on the defence delta times opponent adjusted attack rating.

interactions.hypothesis: Tails switch regime with lead size: up to a three-goal gap totals grow, beyond it damping or collapse dominates, so tail multipliers must condition on the expected gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate tail multipliers within bins of expected absolute goal difference.

interactions.hypothesis: Heavy rain or wind lowers the effectiveness of high-tempo passing teams more than direct teams, so the weather effect on totals is scaled by the style of the teams playing. (speculative style interaction with no supporting evidence cited; hypothesis only)
interactions.how_to_test: Interact weather indicators with team passing-directness index.

interactions.hypothesis: Totals depend on both teams' finishing and both keepers; hot finishing against a hot keeper nets out; the joint distribution of finishing and keeper residuals sets the variance, not each separately.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare totals variance with joint shrinkage of finishing and keeper residuals vs separate.

interactions.hypothesis: Only for low-leverage or very high-leverage league fixtures: rotation is likelier in dead rubbers and changes both sides' attack/defence ratings, while leverage itself may open or close the game; the total-goals shift is conditional on the leverage regime and of unknown sign.
interactions.how_to_test: Pooled regression of totals residuals on leverage percentile buckets and realised starters changed, league fixed effects, 5 seasons.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in league mean but convex in rung probability at 5.5+
nonlinearities.why: A 0.2 shift in league average goals changes P(total>=6) by more than 20% relative because the tail is exponential in the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Monotone isotonic multiplier increasing with k
nonlinearities.why: Tail multiplier relative to Poisson is not constant across rungs: the multiplier is near 1 at central rungs and larger in the tail, with the size to be estimated (1.5-2.5 at 6.5+ is a placeholder).

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in wind speed (a value near 30 km/h is a placeholder to be fitted)
nonlinearities.why: Weather affects scoring materially only beyond thresholds (strong wind, heavy rain), with near-zero effect otherwise.

mechanism_review.summary: Total goals is the sum of two correlated overdispersed counts settled at 90 minutes plus stoppage. The mean comes from opponent-adjusted attack and defence strengths and the league's goal environment; the lineup's attack and defence composition moves the two sides in opposite directions, so it needs a split rather than a scalar. A shared latent openness factor correlates the team counts and thickens both tails; game-state damping and mismatch collapses shape the right tail, which is what the high rungs (5.5 to 7.5 in the sampled series) price. Finishing and keeper luck, set-piece and penalty events, weather and referee tendencies add noise, and the ladder is a nested monotone set with regulation-only settlement.

stages.name: Two scoring intensities and their sum
stages.description: The total's mean is the sum of both teams' opponent-adjusted lambdas; the lineup's attack/defence composition (which attackers and which defenders play) determines each side's contribution separately, and the sum rewards openness on both sides. League goal environment, home goal share and season trend set the baseline, with strong cross-league differences (2.3 to 3.3 goals per match). Stakes and rotation shift both lambdas: soc.rotation_index lowers the rotating side's attack and raises the opponent's via a weaker defence, and soc.stakes_leverage flags dead rubbers and six-pointers whose effect on the total has no established sign (more open in dead rubbers, cagier in high-leverage relegation games are both plausible).
stages.distribution: Sum of two overdispersed counts; mean around 2.7 with variance excess over Poisson to be estimated (10-15% is a placeholder).

stages.name: Shared openness and style factor
stages.description: Some matches are open for both sides (high lines, weak defences, derbies without stakes) and some closed (cautious, low blocks); this match-level latent factor correlates the two teams' scoring and thickens both tails of the total beyond independent Poisson, which is why 0-0 and 5-3 are both more common than the independent model predicts.
stages.distribution: Mixture over a latent openness variable; positive correlation between team counts at the match level, negative conditional correlation within game-state.

stages.name: Game-state and tail dynamics
stages.description: Once a lead builds the leader eases off, so tails are shaped by two competing forces: collapse of a weaker team (red card, mismatch) pushes the total upward in bursts, while garbage-time damping caps it; the net is a heavy right tail only in strongly mismatched fixtures and in leagues with poor defending. High strikes depend on the tail, not the mean.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail from mismatch mixture; P(total>=7) well above Poisson tail in cups with divisional gaps.

stages.name: Finishing, keeper and set-piece luck
stages.description: Realised totals include finishing and goalkeeper variance: a keeper in hot form or a team that has overperformed xG for months is a regression candidate, and set-piece and penalty events add lumpy goals; weather (wind, rain) modifies shot quality and keeper handling modestly.
stages.distribution: Overdispersion from persistent skill plus transient luck; penalty events add about 0.25-0.3 goals per match in expectation with high variance.

stages.name: Ladder and settlement
stages.description: Rungs form a monotone ladder in P(total>k); the contract uses regulation goals including stoppage, and team totals use one side's count; extra time and shootouts are excluded; cross-rung consistency is a constraint, not an input.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping; ladder is an implied distribution.

talent_strength.note: Adjusted attack/defence strengths and league goal environment.

opponent_matchup.note: Style pairing determines openness; set-piece matchup for lumpy goals.

role_personnel.note: Which attackers and defenders play and the keeper.

availability_news.note: Lineup news about an hour pre-kickoff; late changes to the defence matter for totals.

coaching_scheme.note: Pressing and tempo of each manager's system.

environment.note: Wind, rain and temperature adjust goal rates a few percent.

game_context_script.note: Score-state damping and collapse shape the tail.

pace_volume.note: Shot and possession volume per side.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and keeper luck separated from skill.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersion and tail of the total.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Leverage of the result and predicted rotation shift both team lambdas; the sign of the stakes effect on totals is empirical.

officiating_rules.note: Referee penalty and card tendencies add shock goals.

settlement_contract.note: Regulation-only, nested ladder and strike construction.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Match totals: YES when 'over N goals are scored' in the named match 'after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)', N a half-goal strike so there is no push; the strikes form a nested monotone ladder. Team totals ('records above N goals', same window) count one side and state that own goals count towards the team awarded the goal. The World Cup series KXWCTOTAL and KXWCTEAMTOTAL use exactly this per-match wording (e.g. a France vs England game), so no tournament-aggregate series remains here. No totals text contains a cancellation, postponement or abandonment clause (the game-total secondary text is only the trademark disclaimer).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official match report final regulation score (home plus away goals) from the competition's governing body; team totals credit own goals to the team awarded the goal, as their texts state; extra time and penalties excluded.
variants_and_edge_cases: Strike ladder: each rung is P(total >= k+1), monotone decreasing. The sampled strikes are the top listed rungs (3.5 to 11.5, mostly 5.5-7.5, e.g. 11.5 for KXWCTOTAL, KXUCLTOTAL, 10.5 for KXEFLCHAMPIONSHIPTOTAL), consistent with the sampler picking the highest strike of each event; the central rungs (1.5-3.5), where the mean and low-score structure dominate, are not visible in the text but almost certainly listed.
Team-total series (KXUECLTEAMTOTAL, KXEPLTEAMTOTAL-style) require a single side's count; an own goal credited to the side counts, so the opponent's attack feeds a team's count at about 3-5% of goals.

Totals for halves (1H/2H) are in first_half_and_period, and the same 'Point Total' ledger title is used for goals totals; league and cup versions differ in incentives (aggregate scores, ET) while settlement is regulation-only.

198 live series, 155 with rules text, all with the regulation-only wording; 43 are TITLE_ONLY (mostly cup and team-total series, plus the generic KXSOCCERTOTAL); abandonment mid-match with goals already scored and postponement are not addressed.

Scope: all live series are per-match totals or team totals, including KXEPLTOTAL, KXUCLTOTAL, KXWCTOTAL and KXWCTEAMTOTAL (verified per-match wording); the Team Points series moved to team_points_and_margin and KXWCTOTALGOAL/KXWCTEAMGOALS to unreg:tournament_aggregate_event_props.

handicap_and_exact_score.label: Handicap and exact score
handicap_and_exact_score.target: Goal-difference threshold or exact final score in regulation.
handicap_and_exact_score.mechanism: Handicap and exact-score markets are functionals of the full joint goal distribution: handicap prices need the goal-difference distribution including margins, and exact score prices need every cell. They are sensitive to the distribution tail, dependence parameters and lambda errors. Push/split rules for integer and quarter lines matter. The edge, if any, is more likely in consistency across rungs than in a lineup effect.

inputs.why: Lambdas for both teams - the channel through which it moves the Handicap and exact score price.
Low-score cells dominate exact scores.
Joint distribution (over-dispersion).
Lambda uncertainty fattens margin tails.
Home offset shifts handicap center.
Lineup effect on goal difference.
Late-chase dynamics produce larger margins.
AH/total implied lambdas calibrate the grid.
Long-shot cells are systematically distorted.
Handicap steps must be monotone.
Push, half/quarter-line and void rules.
Raw team xG for lambda estimation.
Confirmed XI changes margin expectation.
Dead-ball mismatch moves narrow margins.
Red-card risk fattens margin tails.
Large cup mismatches are the main source of high spread and exact-score rungs and need explicit division bridging.
Dominant spread driver in cup fixtures that no strength rating captures.
Mismatch-driven spreads depend more on tail calibration than on mean strength.
Calibrates base rates of lopsided games by league, where sampled spreads reach 5.5 goals.

interactions.hypothesis: Integrating lambda uncertainty fattens tails; ignoring it under-prices big margins and high scores.
Fitted rho and lambdas must be consistent with AH and total lines; residual score cells are the exact-score signal.
Late game chasing makes heavy favourites' margin distribution depend on bench depth and substitutions.

Rotation scales the favourite's attack, and the cross-tier gap sets the baseline; their product determines whether a cup mismatch is a 5+ goal margin or a tight win, so the combined effect is much larger than either factor alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Interaction regression of margin on rotation intensity times rating gap in cup ties.

interactions.hypothesis: Beyond a three-goal lead the match switches from a scoring regime into a damping regime for the leader, while a red-card collapse switches the opposite; the margin tail therefore has two regimes depending on which happens first.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate hazard of next goal by lead size and numerical advantage.

interactions.hypothesis: Exact-score cells are determined jointly by marginal counts and the dependence correction; shifting rho changes 1-0/0-0/1-1 cells but leaves 3-1 unchanged, so the ladder must be fitted as a joint distribution, not rung by rung.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare log-loss of exact-score pmf with and without the dependence correction by cell.

interactions.hypothesis: In lopsided leagues, rating uncertainty adds disproportionately to the probability of big margins because the convex tail of the margin distribution amplifies variation in the strength gap. (hypothesis: convexity of the margin tail in rating uncertainty is asserted, not measured)
interactions.how_to_test: Compute league balance from an external statistic (final-table points sd or Gini from standings, not from the ratings model) and compare P(margin>=4) calibration by balance tercile and posterior width.

interactions.hypothesis: Home advantage in the margin depends on the home side being at full strength; a rotated home favourite loses much of its crowd-driven edge over an organised underdog, so the venue term is conditional on lineup quality. (hypothesis, size unmeasured)
interactions.how_to_test: Fit home effect separately for rotated vs full-strength lineups.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex mapping from rating gap to P(margin>=4)
nonlinearities.why: The probability of a large margin grows faster than linearly in the expected goal gap because the Skellam tail increases roughly exponentially.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at 4+ changed starters
nonlinearities.why: Changing one to three players barely affects output, but rotating most of the attack changes the favourite's lambda abruptly.

nonlinearities.shape: Isotonic non-parametric correction by margin
nonlinearities.why: The ratio of observed to model tail probabilities is not constant in margin; it needs a flexible monotone fit.

mechanism_review.summary: A handicap or exact score settles on the regulation goal difference or scoreline, so the object is the joint distribution of two team goal counts. The mean gap comes from team strengths (with a bridge between divisions for cup mismatches) and from the confirmed lineup; the favourite's rotation in mismatch games is a major discrete driver. The tail of the margin differs from independent Poisson: leaders ease off after a large lead and underdogs can collapse, and the base rate of mismatches depends on the league's competitive balance. Exact-score rungs depend on cell-level dependence in low scores and on the trailing side's scoring while chasing. The ladders are nested (spreads) or a partition (scores), settled at 90 minutes.

stages.name: Strength gap between the two teams
stages.description: A handicap and a correct score first require the full distribution of the strength gap: league-adjusted attack/defence strengths for both teams, venue, and a bridge between divisions when cup sides come from different tiers. Rating error for the weaker side is large in cups (small samples, no common opponents), so the mismatch size is itself uncertain.
stages.distribution: Log-normal-ish posterior of attack and defence per team; the gap between divisions has sd of about 0.3-0.5 log-goals when linked only by sparse cup results.

stages.name: Lineup and rotation of the favourite
stages.description: In cups and congested weeks big clubs rotate heavily against small clubs, which reduces the favourite's lambda by 15-30% and changes who plays up front; the confirmed XI shifts the margin distribution far more than the opponent does. Depth of the favourite's bench determines how large the drop is.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup states (full strength / rotated / reserves) with probabilities that depend on stakes; lambda scale shifts by regime.

stages.name: Goal-difference distribution and its tail
stages.description: Given the two lambdas the margin is a Skellam-like difference, but real blowouts have a different tail: after a 3-0 lead the favourite eases off (lowering its lambda), while a collapsing underdog (red card, tactical disorganisation) concedes in bunches. The league's competitive balance sets how often mismatches occur and how fat the tail of margins is.
stages.distribution: Difference of correlated overdispersed counts; the tail beyond margin 4 is thicker than Skellam in lopsided leagues, thinner after garbage time sets in.

stages.name: Low and mid scoreline structure for exact scores
stages.description: Exact-score rungs depend on the joint distribution cell by cell: the 0-0, 1-0, 1-1 cells use Dixon-Coles dependence, and cells like 3-1, 2-2 depend on the two teams' high-count behaviour; the loser's scoring chance when trailing (chasing) matters for 4-2 vs 4-0.
stages.distribution: Joint pmf over scorelines with heavy mass at 1-0, 1-1, 2-1; each cell probability below 15% so rung prices are small and noise-sensitive.

stages.name: Ladder consistency and settlement
stages.description: Spread strikes form a nested monotone ladder (P(margin>3.5) <= P(margin>2.5)) and correct-score rungs form a partition; regulation-only settlement and the 'winner' conditional in each rung determine mapping. No cancellation, abandonment or fair-price clause is visible in any spread or correct-score text, so postponement handling cannot be mapped from the contract.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping; constraint structure rather than randomness.

stages.name: Extra-time-inclusive scoreline (KXWCSCOREET)
stages.description: For the World Cup 'Correct Score after Extra Time' series the settled scoreline is the 90-minute score when regulation produces a winner, and otherwise the level 90-minute score plus the two teams' extra-time goals. The scoreline pmf is therefore the regulation pmf on non-draw cells plus a convolution of each drawn cell (0-0, 1-1, 2-2) with a low-rate tired extra-time process; drawn 120-minute scores stay possible because the shootout does not alter the score, and group-stage games (no extra time) collapse to the regulation pmf.
stages.distribution: Mixture: regulation joint pmf on decided cells, plus drawn cells convolved with extra-time counts of mean about 0.4-0.5 combined; P(level after 120 | level after 90) near one half (to be estimated).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Whether the favourite prioritises the match (cup rounds between league fixtures, European weeks) is only partially encoded in rotation and stakes inputs and has not been linked to margin tails; effect of priority on exact-score ladder is unmeasured.

officiating_rules.note: Referee card and penalty propensity (shrunk) drives early-red-card and penalty regimes that change the margin tail; soc.fouls_cards (audited WEAK) is no longer cited.

settlement_contract.note: Regulation-only margin and consistency across rungs.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Spread series: YES when the named team 'wins by more than' the x.5 strike 'after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)', so 'more than 2.5' needs a margin of 3+ and there is no push. Correct-score series: each market is one scoreline for a named winner ('Manchester United wins 6-2') on the same 90-minute window, except KXWCSCOREET, whose text counts the score 'during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)', so a knockout game level after 90 settles on the 120-minute score (a shootout does not change it). Spread texts carry only the trademark disclaimer and correct-score texts no secondary at all: no postponement, abandonment, draw-rung or 'other score' clause is visible. Own goals count in the score.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official match report final score after regulation including stoppage time (own goals credited to the beneficiary) for all spread and correct-score series; extra time counts only for KXWCSCOREET ('during the entire game'), and shootout kicks never change the score.
variants_and_edge_cases: Spread strikes are x.5 'wins by more than' with strike_type greater (e.g. KXLALIGA2SPREAD 3.5): P(margin>=4) is a deep-tail event for most pairings, so the tail of goal difference and mismatch magnitude (cup ties across divisions) dominate rather than lambda differences.

Exact score requires a correct joint distribution of each team's count: a 'wins 5-2' rung needs the loser to score 2, which is very sensitive to the loser's conversion in a chasing game; the ladder across hundreds of rungs must be a proper joint distribution (monotone and summing to one).

Cup ties that need a winner go to ET and penalties but spreads and regular correct scores settle at 90 minutes; neither spread nor correct-score texts contain a postponement or abandonment clause (the 48-hour rule is visible only in sibling GAME texts).

180 live series, 156 with rules text (spreads: identical 'wins by more than N goals ... after 90 minutes plus stoppage time' wording, sampled strikes 2.5 to 7.5 being the top listed rung; correct scores: one scoreline per market, sampled up to 7-6); 24 are TITLE_ONLY; first-half spreads are in first_half_and_period.

KXWCSCOREET is the only extra-time-inclusive series: for a World Cup knockout game the scoreline is the 90-minute score if a side wins in regulation and the 120-minute score otherwise, so P(score) mixes the regulation joint pmf with the extra-time increment conditional on a draw at 90 (stage s6).

btts_and_clean_sheet.label: Both teams to score and clean sheet
btts_and_clean_sheet.target: Both teams score at least once (full match or first half).
btts_and_clean_sheet.mechanism: BTTS requires each team to score at least once, so it is controlled by the lower-lambda team's probability of scoring and by the dependence between scoring events. Keeper quality, defensive absences and tempo shift clean-sheet probability; the dependence parameter shifts the joint zero-zero and one-nil cells. First-half variant is lower-count and more dependent on the half split.

inputs.why: Scoring probability and clean-sheet propensity for each team.
Lambdas determine P(score >= 1).
Joint low-score cells decide BTTS-no.
Keeper conversion adjusts clean-sheet odds.
Missing defenders/strikers shift scoring probabilities.
Team failing-to-score streaks regress.
Clean-sheet streak partly keeper luck.
Openness raises joint scoring.
First-half variant needs the split.
Leading team's defensive posture reduces late conceding.
Regulation/half definition and abandonment.
Confirmed defenders/forwards and keeper.
Shots on target for/against - the channel through which it moves the Both teams to score and clean sheet price.
Red-card variance alters scoring.
Set-piece route for the weaker team to score.
BTTS-No wins are blanks by one side; excess zero mass is the direct driver and is not in any existing input.
Turns static lambdas into the sequential process that BTTS actually follows.
Gives the minimum-lambda channel a quality-weighted measurement instead of a mean.

interactions.hypothesis: BTTS-no is dominated by 0-0, 1-0 and 0-1 cells so rho changes the price more than lambda for low-scoring pairs.
Hot-keeper form regresses; the shrunk keeper effect, not recent clean sheets, should enter clean-sheet markets.
Missing first-choice defenders matter more for the team that already concedes openly; effect is convex in lambda.

The weaker side's P(score>=1) is 1-exp(-chances x conversion against this keeper): a high count of big chances only turns into BTTS-Yes if the opposing keeper's shrunk shot-stopping does not cancel it, so the keeper term scales the weaker side's chance-quality channel (direction: strong keeper cuts it).
interactions.how_to_test: Bin matches by weaker-side big-chance count and by opposing keeper shrunk PSxG-GA tercile; compare realised weaker-side scoring rate with the additive model.

interactions.hypothesis: Keeper effect applies only if the shrunk-rating starter actually plays; a backup keeper replaces a +0.05 PSxG-GA/shot starter with a replacement-level one, so the keeper term must be conditioned on the confirmed lineup, not season data.
interactions.how_to_test: Split matches by keeper change vs no change and compare residual conceding rate.

interactions.hypothesis: Before the first goal the pairing behaves as in a static Dixon-Coles game; after it, the trailing manager's choice switches the match into an open regime, so the effective dependence is positive below one goal and may flip later in the match (hypothesis, timing not established from data).
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate scoring hazard conditional on state at each minute bucket; test if BTTS error clusters in 1-0 games with a chasing side.

interactions.hypothesis: Zero inflation is amplified when the focal striker is out: the same excess-FTS teams blank far more often without their one forward, while diffuse attacks barely move.
interactions.how_to_test: Interaction regression of blank indicator on focal-striker absence times excess_FTS.

interactions.hypothesis: A weaker side with elite set-piece xG crosses a threshold at which its P(score) stays above the rating-implied level (the 0.55-0.6 figure is an unsourced hypothesis to be estimated) even against a dominant opponent; below the threshold it collapses to counter-attack luck.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin set-piece xG share; compare weaker-side scoring rate vs open-play-only prediction.

interactions.hypothesis: For 2H BTTS the half-time state selects the second-half multipliers: a level half-time score keeps both rates near baseline, a one-goal lead raises the trailer's and lowers the leader's 2H rate, which raises P(trailer scores) but lowers P(leader scores), so the net effect on 2H BTTS depends on the asymmetry.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin historical 2H BTTS outcomes by half-time margin and compare with an independent-half model.

interactions.hypothesis: Only in cross-division cup ties: the lower-tier side's goal rate comes from the bridge rating gap, and a heavily rotated favourite (7+ changes) raises that rate and lowers its own clean-sheet probability, so BTTS Yes moves up most when a large tier gap coincides with heavy rotation; within-league fixtures are unaffected.
interactions.how_to_test: On cross-tier cup ties, compare calibration of P(weaker side scores) by rating-gap bucket with and without the bridge term, split by realised starters changed by the favourite.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating (1-exp(-lambda)) in each side's rating, so equal rating errors cost more at low lambda
nonlinearities.why: The BTTS probability is a product of two saturating terms; the lower-lambda factor dominates the error and a linear rating-difference feature misprices extremes.

nonlinearities.shape: Small linear-in-shrunk-PSxG effect with a heavy shrinkage factor
nonlinearities.why: Raw PSxG-GA swings of +-0.15 per shot are mostly luck over a season; the usable effect is the shrunk fraction (about 15-25% of raw).

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: affects only the four low cells
nonlinearities.why: Rho adjusts the joint 0-0/1-0/0-1/1-1 probabilities and is exactly zero above 1 goal each, so its influence concentrates on the BTTS-No mass.

mechanism_review.summary: BTTS is the intersection of two goal-count events, P(H>=1 and A>=1), so it is governed by the lower of the two scoring rates and by their dependence. Each side's rate comes from opponent-adjusted chance volume and quality, adjusted for the confirmed starting XI and keeper; each side's shutout probability exceeds the Poisson value for teams with concentrated attacks. The two processes are coupled by game state: after the first goal the trailing side chases (raising both sides' chance rates) or the leader parks. Discrete shocks (a red card, a penalty, a keeper swap) and the regulation-only settlement window (extra time excluded, own goals credited) complete the chain. The binary has no strike ladder, so the key modelling objects are min(lambda), zero inflation and the state-conditional hazard. Half variants (1H and 2H BTTS, 55 series) need each side's half-specific rate, half-level dependence and, for the second half, the half-time state.

stages.name: Team scoring intensities
stages.description: Each side's regulation goal rate is the product of shot volume against this specific opposition (tempo, territory, set-piece route) and chance quality given lineup and keeper. BTTS needs BOTH rates to be non-trivial, so the binding quantity is min(lambda_home, lambda_away), not the total: a 3.0 total split 2.7/0.3 is a low BTTS price while 1.6/1.4 is high. The weaker side's attack against the stronger side's current back line and keeper is the swing stage. In cross-division cup ties (Copa del Rey, Copa do Brasil, Coupe de France, FA Cup and DFB-Pokal early rounds, the Israeli Cup) the two sides share no league opponents, so the weaker side's lambda, which binds BTTS Yes and the favourite's clean sheet, is set on a common scale by soc.cross_tier_strength_link and then scaled by the favourite's expected rotation (soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch), which raises the underdog's scoring chance when the big club rests starters.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like counts per side with overdispersion; P(side scores>=1)=1-exp(-lambda) is concave, so uncertainty in lambda matters most for the low-lambda side.

stages.name: Zero-state structure and failed-to-score clustering
stages.description: Whether a side draws a blank is not purely a Poisson coin: low-block teams that cede territory but concentrate chances in a few counters/set pieces, and teams with a single focal striker, show more shutouts than their xG implies, while teams with distributed threat show fewer. Keeper shot-stopping and the bottom end of the finishing distribution sit here. This is the stage the ratings-only model misses and where a zero-inflation term lives.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated / negative-binomial count per side; failed-to-score rate varies across teams beyond Poisson with a heavy dependence on single-player availability.

stages.name: Cross-team dependence and score-state response
stages.description: The two scoring processes are not independent: after the first goal the trailing side commits numbers (raising both its attack rate and the leader's counter chances), while a leader that goes two up shuts the game down. Dixon-Coles rho captures only the 0-0/1-0/0-1/1-1 cells; the BTTS-relevant mechanism is the conditional hazard that the still-scoreless side scores after conceding first, versus the leader parking the bus.
stages.distribution: Joint (bivariate) goal distribution with time-varying conditional intensities; positive correlation at low scores, negative at high scores through game-state.

stages.name: Match-day shocks: red cards, penalties, timing
stages.description: Late lineup news (keeper, centre-back, striker), a first-half red card, or a penalty award each move one side's scoring chance by a large discrete amount. A penalty (about 75-80% conversion, awarded in roughly a quarter of matches) is a near-guaranteed route for an otherwise blanked team; referee and VAR tendencies and the lineup timestamp determine how much of this is knowable before kickoff.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete shocks (red card ~8-10% of matches, penalty ~25%) layered on the count process; right-skewed effect on lambda.

stages.name: Settlement mapping
stages.description: Goals are counted in regulation plus stoppage with own goals credited to the beneficiary; extra time, penalties and shootouts are excluded for the full-match texts. Half variants count only goals of the named half, so 45+ and 90+ stoppage attribution to halves must follow the provider's period field; knockout ties with advancement incentives change the 90-minute goal process (cagey first legs) without changing the contract.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the goal event log; only the regulation-window definition and abandonment handling vary.

stages.name: Half-window joint scoring for 1H and 2H BTTS
stages.description: For the 56 half series (46 first-half, 10 second-half) both sides must score inside one 45-minute window: P(YES) is roughly (1-exp(-l_home_h))(1-exp(-l_away_h)) with half rates l_h derived from each team's half share of goals, then corrected for half-level dependence. First-half rates are lower and cagey openings lower both together; second-half rates are conditional on the half-time score, because a trailing side commits numbers while the leader sits deeper, so a 1-0 half-time state raises the trailer's 2H rate and lowers the leader's. A first-half red card shifts both 2H rates.
stages.distribution: Product of two low-mean half counts (half means about 0.5-0.8 per side) with draw-like coupling; P(1H BTTS) typically 0.12-0.25, P(2H BTTS) slightly higher.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted strengths within a league; the cross-division bridge rating puts both sides of a cup mismatch on one scale.

opponent_matchup.note: Weak-attack versus strong-defence pairing is what sets the lower lambda; set-piece routes let low-block teams still score.

role_personnel.note: Single-striker dependence and the starting keeper/centre-back pair drive blank probability.

availability_news.note: Confirmed XIs and the favourite's predicted rotation in cup mismatches.

coaching_scheme.note: Whether a manager chases or parks after the first goal sets the conditional hazard; pressing style sets openness.

environment.note: Weather, altitude and pitch change goal rates by a few percent in aggregate; for a binary requiring both sides to score the effect is second-order and is absorbed by league/venue baseline ratings, so no separate BTTS-specific environment input is proposed.

game_context_script.note: Score-state response after the first goal is the main source of dependence; not pregame-observable but estimable from history.

pace_volume.note: Shot volume sets how many attempts each side gets; tempo raises both lambdas jointly.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and keeper luck separated from skill, plus excess failed-to-score beyond Poisson.

distribution_variance.note: Low-score dependence and zero-inflation are the distribution inputs that move P(0) directly.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Aggregate state of two-legged cup ties, predicted rotation and dead-rubber leverage shift the weaker side scoring chance and the stronger side defensive intensity; effect sizes for BTTS are still to be estimated.

officiating_rules.note: Referee/VAR-shrunk penalty-award rate gives the discrete route by which a blanked side still scores; card counts (soc.fouls_cards, audited WEAK) are no longer cited as cover.
