contract_review.settlement_definition: Three window variants share one both-score wording. Full-match BTTS (147 series, 129 with text): YES when both named sides score 'after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)'. First-half BTTS (46 series): only goals scored during the 1st Half count. Second-half BTTS (10 series, e.g. KXEPL2HBTTS, KXUEFASC2HBTTS): only goals scored during the 2nd Half count, regardless of the half-time score. In every variant own goals count towards the team awarded the goal; BTTS-No is the complement and there is no ladder. None of the 185 BTTS texts read contains a cancellation, postponement or abandonment clause, and the half texts do not say whether a half's stoppage time or (for 2H) extra time is included.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official league/competition match report goal events with goal credit (own goals credited to the beneficiary), as published by the governing league and tracked by Kalshi's data provider; minute of goal not needed for the full-match contract, needed for the first- and second-half variants (period attribution of stoppage-time goals).
variants_and_edge_cases: Knockout/cup ties (KXCOPADELREYBTTS, KXISRSCUPBTTS, KXCONMEBOLSUDBTTS): extra time is excluded, so a 1-0 after 90 that finishes 2-1 in ET is still BTTS-No; the 90-minute-only goal process, not the advancement process, is what must be modelled.

203 live series, 185 with rules text: 129 full-match texts use the regulation-only wording plus the own-goal clause, 46 first-half and 10 second-half texts use 'Only goals scored during the 1st/2nd Half count'; 18 series (e.g. KXSOCCERBTTS, KXCLUBWCBTTS, KXFINALISSIMABTTS) are TITLE_ONLY and assumed to follow the full-match wording.

Half-window variants (KXUCL1HBTTS, KXEPL1HBTTS, KXMLS2HBTTS, KXWC2HBTTS) need half-split scoring rates and half-level dependence; second-half BTTS also depends on the half-time score through chase/park behaviour (stage s6).
Own-goal credit means P(team scores) must include opponent own-goal probability (about 3-5% of goals), a small positive term for weak attacks facing high lines and crosses.

No clean-sheet series is listed under this key; postponement, abandonment and (for 2H variants in knockout games such as KXUEFASC2HBTTS, KXWC2HBTTS) extra-time treatment are not stated in any BTTS text.

first_half_and_period.label: First-half and second-half markets
first_half_and_period.target: Result/total/handicap/exact score within the first or second half.
first_half_and_period.mechanism: Half-window markets are the same goal process restricted to 45 minutes plus stoppage. The key parameters are each team's first-half goal share, early-match caution and the distribution of low counts (many 0-0, 1-0). Draws are very likely in first-half result markets, so dependence and draw propensity dominate. Second-half markets need conditional modelling from half-time state and substitution dynamics.

inputs.why: Half share of goals by team - the channel through which it moves the First-half and second-half markets price.
Strength difference scaled to a half.
Dependence in low-count windows.
Half-time draw tendencies - the channel through which it moves the First-half and second-half markets price.
Early hazard shapes first half.
Press intensity front-loads chances.
Starters matter most in the first half.
Second-half rates conditional on score.
Half-time stoppage influences windows.
Definition of half boundaries and abandonment.
Consistency with full-time ladders.
Team xG baseline scaled by period share.
Starting XI - the channel through which it moves the First-half and second-half markets price.
Early territorial pressure - the channel through which it moves the First-half and second-half markets price.
First-half goals are rare events; finishing luck dominates.
Gives the first-half and second-half lambdas their own team-level scaling rather than a fixed league 45/55 split.
Provides the conditional structure for 2H markets and for combining first-half simulations with second-half rates.
The Tie and exact-score ladders for halves are controlled by these parameters.

interactions.hypothesis: High-press teams get a larger first-half share, so period lambdas depend on style, not on a league-average split.
First-half draw probability is the intersection of dependence and low lambdas, so the two must be jointly modelled.
Second-half goal multipliers depend on half-time score and on bench strength after substitutions.

The second-half rate depends on the half-time margin and on who was favoured: a favourite trailing at the break lifts output strongly, while an underdog leading drops it, so the effect has opposite signs by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress 2H goals on HT margin interacted with pre-match favourite status; compare residuals.

interactions.hypothesis: High-press teams front-load their chances; pairing a high-press side with a deep-block opponent (proxied by the opponent's PPDA and territory, since line height itself is not in free data) raises first-half expected goals more than the sum of the parts.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit 1H goals on pressing intensity interacted with the opponent PPDA/deep-block proxy; line height needs a tracking-data provider and is not available free.

interactions.hypothesis: An early first-half goal produces the half-time margin that then selects the second-half multiplier: the opening-period hazard determines which state regime the 2H starts in, so P(2H total over 1.5) differs by who scored first and when (direction: a favourite conceding first lifts 2H output, an underdog scoring first lowers it).
interactions.how_to_test: Condition 2H goal counts on first-goal minute bucket and scorer favouredness, and compare with a model that uses only the HT margin.

interactions.hypothesis: A long first-half delay (VAR checks, injuries) adds exposure minutes: the extra time scales the half's expected goals proportionally (roughly one minute per 1/45 of the half rate; the size of a typical delay is to be measured) and matters most for close 0.5 total strikes.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast 1H goals per minute vs added time buckets.

interactions.hypothesis: Late lineup news (a missing first-choice striker) affects the opening-period rate more than the match average, because replacements need time and bench players are used later; the effect is conditional on the half.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare 1H vs 2H goals by lineup-change indicator.

interactions.hypothesis: Above a heat-index or altitude threshold the second half loses intensity (fewer high-intensity runs, more drinks-break pauses), so the first-half share of goals rises and 1H totals/1H BTTS gain probability relative to the full-match lambda; in temperate sea-level matches the split is unchanged.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress the second-half share of goals on kickoff heat index and venue altitude with league and kickoff-hour fixed effects, pooled over multiple seasons.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: 1H share bounded about 0.35-0.55
nonlinearities.why: Team shares shrink heavily to the league mean; the response of half lambda to the raw observed share is strongly sublinear because of small samples.

nonlinearities.shape: Asymmetric and piecewise in HT margin
nonlinearities.why: A one-goal margin changes rates by about 20% but a three-goal margin does not change them further (garbage time), so the multiplier saturates beyond 2.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in added minutes with small slope
nonlinearities.why: Each extra minute of exposure adds about 1/45 of the half's expected goals, but late-minute urgency makes second-half minutes denser.

mechanism_review.summary: A half contract counts goals scored inside one 45-minute period (plus that period's stoppage), so the outcome is a low-count process derived from full-match team intensities scaled by the team's own first/second half profile. The first half is shaped by cautious starts and a shorter stoppage, so 0-0 and 1-1 dominate and draw probability for a half is high; the second half depends on the half-time score through the trailing team's chase and the leader's retreat, so the halves are correlated through state. Dependence among low cells, lineup quality and the added-time minutes of the referee complete the chain, and settlement counts only that half's goals with fair-price resolution if the match is moved.

stages.name: Full-match scoring rates
stages.description: The per-half rates are a fraction of the match's two team intensities, so the full-match opponent-adjusted lambdas, the confirmed lineup and any xG-based ratings come first. For a half-spread of 2+ goals the favourite's lambda dominates; for a half total of 0.5 the sum of both lambdas does.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like team counts over the match; half contributions are thinned sub-samples with overdispersion due to state.

stages.name: Time profile of scoring across halves
stages.description: About 44-46% of goals arrive in the first half and 54-56% in the second, driven by fatigue, substitutions, tactical commitment when trailing, and longer second-half stoppage. A cautious opening raises P(0-0 at half-time), and team style (pressing intensity early, deep block) changes the split; the first-half share also varies by competition (heat, schedule) and kickoff time. Kickoff heat, humidity and altitude (soc.weather) can lower second-half intensity relative to the first, shifting the 2H share of lambda downward in hot afternoon or high-altitude venues (Liga MX at Toluca/Mexico City, summer Brasileiro, the 2026 World Cup afternoon slots); the sign is expected but the size is unestablished.
stages.distribution: Time-inhomogeneous intensity, roughly increasing across the match; team-level share varies with a heavy shrinkage to the league (sd about 4 percentage points).

stages.name: Within-half low-count dependence
stages.description: Half totals are small numbers (mean about 1.2), so joint outcomes concentrate on 0-0, 1-0, 0-1 and 1-1; draw probability for a half is far larger than a Poisson implies because early cagey play and equalising dynamics couple the sides. The relevant dependence parameter is half-level, not the full-match Dixon-Coles rho.
stages.distribution: Bivariate low-count distribution with draw inflation; half draw rate about 40-45%; tail beyond 2 goals each is thin.

stages.name: Second-half state and conditional rates
stages.description: For second-half markets the half-time score matters: the trailing side's attack rate rises, the leading side's falls, substitutions arrive around minute 60, and a first-half red card alters everything. The 2H total is therefore a function of the 1H result, which plausibly creates dependence between halves whose sign by match type is a hypothesis to be tested, not an established fact.
stages.distribution: Conditional intensity multipliers by half-time margin (sizes such as +25% trailing or -15% for a two-goal leader are unsourced hypotheses to estimate), plus discrete red-card shocks.

stages.name: Stoppage, officials and settlement
stages.description: Added time (in minutes) and VAR delays extend each half's exposure and differ by half and referee; second-half stoppage is typically longer than first-half stoppage (lengths to be measured). Settlement uses the half's regulation 45+ stoppage and ignores the other half, with fair-price resolution for postponements in the winner, total and spread texts (48 hours, two weeks for World Cup series); first-half correct-score texts have no such clause.
stages.distribution: Added time per half is a small discrete variable (1-3 min in the first half, 4-8 in the second); goal rate per minute times added minutes shifts expected goals by about 0.03 to 0.15.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted full-match strengths with luck regressed supply the base rates for both halves; raw soc.xg is audited DUPLICATE_OF soc.xg_adjusted_ratings and is not cited.

opponent_matchup.note: Teams that start fast against high-line sides versus those that finish strong create a half-specific matchup.

role_personnel.note: Starting XI sets first-half quality; the substitute bench matters for second-half intensity.

availability_news.note: Lineup vintage at about 60 minutes pre-kickoff; late changes are decisive for first-half rate.

coaching_scheme.note: Managers' substitution timing and chase/park behaviour determine the half-specific rates.

environment.note: Heat, humidity and altitude at kickoff shifting the second-half share of the full-match lambda.

game_context_script.note: Score-state response and half-time score give the conditional 2H rate.

pace_volume.note: Tempo and territory determine volume of attempts per half; corners proxy early pressure.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing luck is regressed so that a hot-streak team is not priced as a high-scoring first half.

distribution_variance.note: Half-level draw inflation and low-cell dependence shape the exact score and Tie markets.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Stakes and congestion alter rotation and half-time effort; modelled through the state multiplier and the lineups.

officiating_rules.note: Referee added-time habits set exposure minutes in each half and the referee/VAR penalty and red-card propensity drives the discrete first-half shocks named in stage s4.

settlement_contract.note: Half-only goal counting, Tie rule and fair-price clause; the ladder across half-strikes must be monotone.

contract_review.settlement_definition: YES settles on goals scored within one half only. Winner/Tie texts (e.g. KXEPL1H, KXSERIEA2H, KXUEFASC2H) judge the half 'after 45 minutes plus stoppage time', and a 0-0 or equal half resolves 'Tie'; total texts ('more than N goals in the 1st Half') and spread texts ('win by more than N goals in the 1st Half') say only that goals scored during the half count; 1st-half correct-score texts ('the score at the end of the 1st Half is A 3, B 2') carry no secondary clause at all. Total, spread and winner texts resolve to a fair price if the game is cancelled or rescheduled more than 48 hours away (two weeks for the six World Cup half series KXWC1H, KXWC2H, KXWC1HTOTAL, KXWC2HTOTAL, KXWC1HSPREAD, KXWC2HSPREAD); strikes are x.5 'more than' so no pushes exist. No half text mentions own goals (credit to the beneficiary is presumed, not stated). 177 of 216 series have text; 39 are TITLE_ONLY.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official match report goal events with minute (goal minute and period as recorded by the league/Kalshi data provider, with 45+N counted as first half and 90+N as second half); own-goal credit is not stated in any half text and is presumed to follow the beneficiary.
variants_and_edge_cases: Second-half contracts are conditional-in-state: the 2H goal rate depends on the half-time score (leader parks, trailing side chases), yet the contract ignores the half-time score itself; 1H and 2H are therefore correlated through state, not independent halves of a Poisson.

First-half exact-score ladder (KXMLS1HSCORE, KXLIGUE11HSCORE) is a custom strike set of mutually exclusive scores with mass concentrated on 0-0, 1-0, 0-1, 1-1; tail scores like 3-2 in a half are rare, so the ladder is dominated by Dixon-Coles low-cell structure.

Half spread 'wins by more than 1.5 goals' (KXBUNDESLIGA1HSPREAD, KXUCL1HSPREAD) needs a 2-0+ half lead, a rare event (about 5-8% for a strong favourite), so estimates are sensitive to the tail of the half goal distribution.

216 live series, 177 with rules text (half winner/Tie, half totals, half spreads, first-half exact score); 39 are TITLE_ONLY, including the 8 residual half-BTTS series still filed here (KXCOUPEDEFRANCE1HBTTS, KXCONCACAFCCUP1HBTTS, KXCLUBWC1HBTTS, KXAFCAC1HBTTS, KXITASUPERCUP1HBTTS, KXESPSUPERCUP1HBTTS, KXFACUP2HBTTS, KXCLUBWC2HBTTS); the other 56 half-BTTS series moved to btts_and_clean_sheet.

Cup half series (KXTACAPORT1H, KXUSOPENCUP1HTOTAL, KXFACUP2H, KXUEFASC2HTOTAL): the winner/Tie texts fix the 2nd Half at 45 minutes plus stoppage, but the 2H total and spread texts only say 'goals scored during the 2nd Half', so whether extra-time goals could count there is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
First-half correct-score series (KXMLS1HSCORE, KXWC1HSCORE) have no secondary text: neither a postponement clause nor an 'any other score' rung is visible.

competition_winner_and_top_n.label: Competition winner, top-N and trophies
competition_winner_and_top_n.target: Winner or finish within the top N of a league/cup, or number of trophies, at the competition's end.
competition_winner_and_top_n.mechanism: Title and top-N prices are outputs of a season simulation: remaining fixtures from calibrated goal models, strength uncertainty and drift, schedule order and tiebreak rules. Multi-competition futures need a joint fixture-list simulation where one team's cup run affects its league strength. Top-N rungs must be consistent with winner and relegation probabilities, and rule wording (playoffs, ties) is decisive.

Uncertainty/drift flattens outcomes.
Fixture difficulty of the run-in.
Decides ties at the top - the channel through which it moves the Competition winner, top-N and trophies price.

Multi-competition coupling - the channel through which it moves the Competition winner, top-N and trophies price.

Window changes - the channel through which it moves the Competition winner, top-N and trophies price.

Prior early in the season - the channel through which it moves the Competition winner, top-N and trophies price.
Sharp outright markets - the channel through which it moves the Competition winner, top-N and trophies price.
Top-N consistency - the channel through which it moves the Competition winner, top-N and trophies price.
xG ratings for long-run strength.
Rating inputs to the simulation.
Late-season incentives - the channel through which it moves the Competition winner, top-N and trophies price.
Schedule disruption - the channel through which it moves the Competition winner, top-N and trophies price.
Cup and tournament outrights are determined by path, which no existing input in the archetype captures.
Converts a table simulation to a champion probability in about a third of the leagues in this ledger bucket.
Directly the random variable of the point-margin series, and it is not the same as the title-winner probability.
Supplies the seeding and bracket side for KXUCL16*, KXUEL16*, KXUCL8, KXUCLTOP, KXUCLBOTTOM, KXUCLLEAGUE-type series where table position, not strength alone, decides the stage reached.
Needed because UEFA stage-reach series (R16, R8, finalist, advance) are settled by bracket position determined by the league-phase finish.
Provides the dependence structure the trophy-count series needs and which no independent per-competition probability can deliver.
Prices team-set unions, exact finishing orders and group outcomes that marginal title odds cannot.

interactions.hypothesis: Posterior strength uncertainty flattens favourites' title probability; fixed-strength sims overstate it.
Deep cup runs reduce league strength more for thin squads, making title and trophy futures negatively linked.
In tight races, head-to-head fixtures and tie-break order determine more of the outcome than average schedule difficulty.

For promoted or rebuilt clubs the preseason prior fixes the posterior mean while its width sets the tails: early in the season title odds of a mid-ranked contender are convex in prior width, and the prior weight fades as matches accumulate, so the interaction is large in the first third of a season and near zero afterwards (hypothesis on timing).
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest title and top-N calibration by matchweek bucket with prior sd inflated versus fixed, and compare Brier score in the first ten matchweeks.

interactions.hypothesis: Whether the table converts to a champion by points or by playoff regime switches the sensitivity of title odds to regular-season strength; in playoff leagues rank 1 vs rank 4 differ by only a few percentage points while in pure leagues they differ by tens.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(champion | rank) by format and compare with a points-only prediction.

interactions.hypothesis: Cup and European progress costs league points in proportion to how thin the squad is: deep clubs rotate with little loss, thin ones lose several points of league expectation per extra competition round, so load times (1 - depth) predicts league slippage.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress league PPG deviation on congested-week count times squad depth over past seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Cup outright odds are conditional on the draw: after the draw is made the same ratings produce different outright prices, and the effect is largest for strong teams drawn into the same quarter.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare pre- and post-draw price movements to the change in path-difficulty.

interactions.hypothesis: Exact group orders and any-nation-wins-group events depend on the joint table, where tiebreak order (head-to-head vs goal difference, fair-play points) decides discrete reorderings; a model with correct marginals but wrong tiebreaks mis-prices permutations far more than single-team group-win odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated vs realised group-order frequencies in past World Cups with and without the tiebreak module.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex payoff of title odds for non-favourites
nonlinearities.why: Because the champion is the maximum of noisy totals, odds of outsiders rise faster than linearly with posterior width.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in games remaining
nonlinearities.why: Schedule strength has weight proportional to the remaining match count; it is near zero in matchweek 5 and large after matchweek 30, so effect is not linear in the strength score.

nonlinearities.shape: Product-like decay for exact orders
nonlinearities.why: An exact 1-2-3-4 order is roughly a product of conditional probabilities, so small errors in each team's rating compound multiplicatively and the contract is extremely sensitive at low prices.

mechanism_review.summary: A competition outright is a sum over scenarios of a latent strength vector, a schedule and a format. Strength is uncertain and drifts; the remaining matches are sampled to produce a joint table; the title, top-N finish or group placing is then read from the sampled tables, with the format converting table position into a champion in split-season and knockout competitions (bracket paths, extra time, shootouts). Multi-competition clubs trade league points for cup progress, and trophy-count contracts need the joint path. Top-N series read the rank against a cut line, and union, exact-order and group contracts need the joint placings of many teams from one tournament simulation. Administrative shocks (deductions, voided seasons) and the definition of the competition-season complete the chain.

stages.name: Team strength and its uncertainty
stages.description: A title or top-N probability starts from each contender's current attack/defence strength, with opponent and venue adjustment and a preseason prior when the season is young. The posterior width matters as much as the mean: two teams with equal means but different uncertainty have different title odds because the maximum of several uncertain totals favours the wider one.
stages.distribution: Posterior distribution of latent strength per team (approx normal on log goal rate); drift over the season via a random walk.

stages.name: Remaining-fixture simulation and table race
stages.description: Points accumulate through 3-outcome matches whose probabilities come from the goal model; the table is a sampled joint outcome across all teams, so title or top-N probabilities are obtained by counting sampled tables. Fixture difficulty and the home/away order of the remaining games differ by team and are the main deterministic asymmetry among contenders.
stages.distribution: Count of table outcomes from a Monte Carlo sum of draws/win/loss lotteries per team; title is argmax of the points vector with tie rule.

stages.name: Competition format conversion
stages.description: Where the title is not the table leader (split seasons, liguilla playoffs, MLS Cup, World Cup knockouts, two-leg ties), a team's table position is converted to the title by a bracket with seeding, home advantage in legs and a penalty-shootout lottery, so the format-specific path probability, not strength alone, sets the price; a one-match final with extra time and penalties compresses strength differences toward 50%.
stages.distribution: Sequence of binary knockout events with win probability for the favourite to be estimated per format (roughly 0.55-0.75 is a hypothesis); product of path probabilities, dominated by bracket draw luck for the elite.

stages.name: Squad shocks, transfers and priority across competitions
stages.description: Over months, key injuries, winter transfer activity, a manager change and the weighting of the league against cups and European competition move strength; a team still alive in several competitions rotates more, lowering league points per game, and this trade-off differs by club ambition. Trophy-count contracts require the joint path across several competitions.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed multi-month strength shifts; correlated across competitions through a shared squad-fatigue state.

stages.name: Rank thresholds and the density at the cut line
stages.description: For top-N series the random variable is the team's final rank relative to N: it depends on the N-th highest points total against the team's own, so the number of rivals within a few points of the cut and the official tiebreak at equal points matter more than the team's average rank. KXUCLTOP and KXUCLTOP8 apply the same logic to the 36-team league phase, and KXEPLTOP4's qualification wording adds the chance that an extra slot reaches fifth place.
stages.distribution: Rank of a correlated points vector; P(top-N) is steep (near 0 or 1) for teams far from the cut and most uncertain for teams within about one match of points.

stages.name: Settlement and administrative events
stages.description: Contracts resolve on the final official table or competition result; points deductions, expulsions, cancelled seasons or retroactive title stripping change who is champion after the last whistle, and ambiguous Clausura/Apertura naming requires the exact competition-season definition in the market.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete administrative events (a few percent of league seasons across world football) layered on the sporting outcome.

stages.name: Team-set unions, exact orders and group outcomes from the joint tournament draw
stages.description: Many World Cup and UCL series are functions of the whole simulated tournament rather than one team's title: unions over a named set (group, confederation by qualification pathway, host nations, first-time winners, league of origin) sum disjoint title probabilities, while exact orders (top four via final and third-place match, a group's 1-4 order under FIFA tiebreaks) and 'any nation of a set wins its group' need the joint distribution of placings, because group-mates and bracket neighbours cannot both progress. Marginal title odds are insufficient; the correlation induced by the bracket and shared groups must be kept. Host-nation unions (KXWCHOSTWIN: any of USA, Mexico, Canada wins) need soc.home_advantage set on for each host's matches played in its own country and zero for neutral-venue matches, so the hosts' group and knockout probabilities carry the host edge before summing their disjoint title probabilities.
stages.distribution: Multinomial over permutations from a joint Monte Carlo of groups and bracket; exact-order outcomes have small probabilities (often below 2%) and are sensitive to tiebreak modelling.

stages.name: Single-match residuals inside the outright key
stages.description: Three series here are decided by one match: the World Cup third-place match (two beaten semi-finalists, motivation and rotation uncertain), the final's winning margin (KXWCWINMARGIN, TITLE_ONLY) and an AFC Champions League Two game. They need the match goal model, the margin distribution and, for knockout matches, the extra-time and shootout branch, not the season simulation.
stages.distribution: Three-way or margin distribution from two team intensities; extra-time and shootout branch adds near-coin-flip mass for knockout games.

talent_strength.note: Strength with uncertainty and a preseason/promoted-team prior for early-season prices.

opponent_matchup.note: Fixture asymmetry for leagues; bracket opponents for cups.

role_personnel.note: Depth of the 12th-18th players and key-player dependence.

availability_news.note: Season-long availability and window activity; no match-day lineup vintage is needed for outright markets.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager changes and in-season tactical evolution shift a contender's strength, and the true effect size of a sacking or appointment is not estimated in any input here; the existing catalog only flags it inside soc.transfers.

environment.note: Weather and altitude act on single matches and are absorbed by the team's home advantage in the goal model over a whole season; the one environmental exception, neutral-venue finals and tournament host-country effects, is handled by the bracket input, not a separate environment variable.

game_context_script.note: Table state and format determine what each match is worth.

pace_volume.note: Possession and shot volume matter only through the goal-model strengths for a season-long outcome; no volume statistic is a direct determinant of who wins a title or finishes top-N, so it carries no separate input.

efficiency_conversion.note: Luck-versus-skill split is performed inside the rating fit (xG-based goal model with shrinkage) so soc.ratings carries it; soc.xg is audited WEAK and is no longer cited as standalone cover.

distribution_variance.note: Joint placings from the tournament simulation and strength uncertainty give the tail and dependence shape of union and order contracts.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rotation and priority across competitions come from soc.cup_progression_load; soc.motivation is audited KEEP_CONTEXT (circular with the simulation) and is not cited as cover.

officiating_rules.note: Refereeing tendencies average out over a full season and have no systematic effect on title chances; sanctions and deductions are administrative and are covered under points_deductions and settlement.

settlement_contract.note: Tiebreak order, split-season definition, deductions and exact named competitions.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Season and tournament outcomes, one binary per team or per outcome: champion of a league, cup, conference or tournament ('is the 2026-27 Bundesliga champion'; split-season and playoff leagues per their own format text); top-N table finish ('is a top 6 finisher in the 2026-27 EPL season', 'finishes in the top 8 in the league phase'); group winner (FIFA tiebreaks); trophy counts and trebles over named competitions (KXSOCCERTROPHIES, KXARSENALCUPS 4+, KXSOCCERTREBLE); team-set unions ('a team from Group L wins', 'any host nation', 'a country that has never won', 'a team from Slovak Super Liga wins the Champions League'); exact finishing orders (KXWCFINISHINGORDER 1-4 via final and third-place match, KXWCGROUPORDER with FIFA tiebreaks); and the World Cup third-place match. KXEPLTOP4 settles on whether the club 'qualifies' (even if it then does not compete), not on rank alone. Resolution is the official final table or competition result; no outright text addresses retroactive sanctions.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Final official league table or tournament result published by the governing body (league, UEFA, CONMEBOL, FIFA); trophy counts rely on the named competitions' official results; whether later sanctions retroactively change the champion is not stated.
variants_and_edge_cases: Split-season leagues (Argentina Torneo Clausura, Paraguay APF Clausura, Uruguay, Liga MX liguilla, MLS Cup): 'champion' is the playoff or half-season winner, so table position converts to the title through a bracket or short tournament, not points alone.

Single-elimination cups and World Cup/Copa/Asian Cup outrights: one binary per team across several rounds with extra time and penalties (penalty shootout winner advances), so the settlement event is the final's winner, not 90-minute results.

Top-N series (KXEPLTOP, KXEPLTOP2, KXEPLTOP6, KXLALIGATOP4, KXSERIEATOP4, KXLIGUE1TOP4, KXBUNDESLIGATOP4, KXLIGAMXTOP, KXUCLTOP8, KXUCLTOP) settle on final rank, except KXEPLTOP4 whose secondary text makes it a qualification event; the tie order at the cut is the league's official tiebreak.

Union and order contracts: KXWCGROUPWINNER, KXUCLLEAGUE, KXWCCONTINENT, KXWCNOEURSA, KXWCHOSTWIN and KXWC1STTIMEWIN pay if any team of a named set wins (continent defined by qualification pathway, not geography); KXWCWINGROUP pays if any nation of a set wins its group; KXWCFINISHINGORDER and KXWCGROUPORDER need an exact permutation.

110 live series, 99 with rules text; 11 TITLE_ONLY (e.g. KXWCFINALMATCHUP, KXWCWINMARGIN, KXUCL16, KXUCL8, KXUEL16TWEVIK, KXUSOPENCUP, KXEGYPL). Points deductions, voided seasons and retroactive title stripping are not addressed in any outright text.

Single-match residuals: KXWC3RDPLACE is the third-place match winner (presumably including extra time and penalties; not stated), KXWCWINMARGIN (TITLE_ONLY) is plausibly the final's winning margin, and KXAFCCL2GAME is a match-result title; stage s8 covers them.

Ecuador LigaPro (KXECULP) carries regular-season points into a hexagonal decided on total points, Peru (KXPERLIGA1) uses Apertura/Clausura and playoff stages, and Venezuela (KXVENFUTVE) a final between half-season winners, so 'champion' differs by league beyond the Argentine/Paraguayan/Uruguayan cases; KXSOCCERTROPHIES also counts a Supercopa de Espana mini-tournament. The Manchester City-type retroactive-sanction case is the reviewer's judgement, not rules text (see retroactive_sanctions).

relegation_qualification_advancement.label: Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement
relegation_qualification_advancement.target: Bottom-N finish, qualification slot, promotion, or advancement from a group/knockout tie.
relegation_qualification_advancement.mechanism: These markets are threshold events near the table's cut line, where small rating differences, tiebreak order, points deductions, and motivation (dead rubbers) matter most. Tournament advancement also uses group permutations, tie-break rules, and knockout extra time/penalty components; advancement is not the same as 90-minute result. Slot allocation (cup winners freeing places, coefficient places) changes qualification thresholds.

inputs.why: Season/tournament simulation - the channel through which it moves the Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement price.
Leverage in fixtures near the cut.
Tiebreaks and slot allocation.
Administrative sanctions near the cut.
Group permutations and simultaneous matches.
Aggregate state and extra-time rules.
Advancement beyond 90 minutes.
Uncertainty near the cut - the channel through which it moves the Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement price.
Direct-rival fixtures - the channel through which it moves the Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement price.
Key absences late in season - the channel through which it moves the Relegation, qualification, promotion and advancement price.
National-team duty for tournament-style competitions.
Defines qualification and advancement wording.
Narrative-level stakes beyond leverage.
Shootout skill for knockout advancement.
Postponed fixtures change the cut-off schedule.
Late squad news in decisive matches.
Makes the qualification threshold a random variable rather than a constant, which the table simulation alone omits.
Last-place contracts are minimum order statistics and are not equal to relegation odds.
Provides the structured tree the existing inputs (aggregate state, ET model, shootout skill) only describe separately.

Prices stage-reach counts, maxima and $1/N dead heats over sets of teams (furthest-advancing confederation nation, debutant and host counts, non-top-10 semi-finalist) from the per-draw stage-reached vector; the same simulation already serves competition_winner_and_top_n.
Converts the table simulation into promotion probability for KXEFLPROMO and KXLALIGA2PROMO, whose YES includes the play-off route.

interactions.hypothesis: Late-season matches where one side has nothing to play for reduce that side's strength, shifting the cut-off teams' probabilities beyond static ratings.
Advancement = 90-minute win + draw x (ET win + shootout); the required-goals state changes each term differently.
A deduction can move a team across the cut and alter tiebreak order, non-additively.

For qualification-settled series (KXUCLQUAL requires a main-tournament place per its text): a club finishing just outside the domestic Champions League places has a qualification probability that is a step function of whether a cup winner or coefficient slot frees an extra place, moving the cut line by one rank; rank-only series (last place, relegation) are unaffected.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare qualification probabilities with and without the cup-spillover branch in past seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Second-leg goal and draw rates depend on the first-leg lead: a two-goal leader plays deep, lowering both teams' rates, while a one-goal trailing team pushes; the advancement probability conditional on first-leg margin is nonlinear.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin second legs by first-leg margin and compare draw rates and goals.

interactions.hypothesis: Last-place probability is convex in rating uncertainty because the minimum of several tightly clustered totals is more sensitive to variance than the mean; widening the posterior increases odds for the second-worst team more than it reduces the worst team's.
interactions.how_to_test: Scale the posterior sd by 0.5-1.5 and track P(last) of the bottom 3.

interactions.hypothesis: Direct clashes among survival rivals create paths where points tie; the tiebreak order then decides, so schedule effects interact with tiebreak only in narrow finishing scenarios.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute frequency of tie-resolved placements in simulations by league.

interactions.hypothesis: A pending deduction or a final-day simultaneous kickoff changes the competitive regime: the deducted team goes from fighting for survival to a dead-rubber, shifting rotation and draw rates for its rivals. (speculative: for a deducted team still fighting relegation the effect may be the opposite; treated as a hypothesis to be tested only on observed deductions)
interactions.how_to_test: Event study on matches following deduction announcements.

interactions.hypothesis: When two nations of the same set share a group, at most one can win it and their knockout paths diverge, which lowers the expected count reaching the knockouts and raises the chance that the set's furthest stage is decided by one team; independence over-prices 'all hosts qualify' or 'exactly N debutants' outcomes when set members are drawn together.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare count-over-set probabilities from the joint simulation with an independent-marginals product for past World Cups.

interactions.hypothesis: Relegation-zone clubs on a winless run have the highest dismissal hazard; a dismissal switches their rating regime for the remaining fixtures, so P(relegated) is a mixture over change paths and survival odds of a struggling club are not simply its current rating projected forward.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of bottom-six points per game after in-season changes versus matched non-changing clubs, then compare relegation calibration with and without the dismissal branch.

interactions.hypothesis: Promotion probability is piecewise in final rank: near-certain in automatic places, then a drop to the bracket win probability for 3rd-4th (semi only), and a further drop for 5th-8th in the 2026-27 EFL format because of the extra single-leg eliminator; in Segunda the higher-seed tie-break flattens the drop between 3rd and 6th less than penalties would.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare historical promotion rates by final rank to the bracket-composed prediction, separately for EFL (pre and post 2026-27) and Segunda.

nonlinearities.shape: Roughly linear in games remaining (variance), collapsing to tiebreak-only in the last two rounds (not a saturating shape)
nonlinearities.why: Schedule asymmetry adds variance proportional to the number of games left and nearly vanishes in the final two rounds when only points and tiebreak matter.

nonlinearities.shape: Right-skewed minimum order statistic
nonlinearities.why: The distribution of the lowest total has a skewed shape, and linear rating-gap predictors understate the probability of surprises.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by aggregate margin: 0, 1, 2+
nonlinearities.why: Aggregate leads change rates sharply at one goal and saturate beyond two as leaders sit deep.

mechanism_review.summary: Placement and advancement events are threshold events on random objects. For tables, each team's final points come from simulated remaining fixtures with uncertain strengths; last place is the minimum of closely spaced totals, relegation or top-N is a rank threshold whose cut line itself depends on cup winners, play-offs and sanctions. For ties, advancement is a sequential tree: first-leg state, second-leg goals shaped by aggregate lead, extra time with fatigue, and a near-coin-flip shootout. Group qualification adds tiebreak order and best-third rankings. Injuries, manager changes and administrative rulings are the shocks, and settlement depends on the competition's own regulations and tie rules.

stages.name: Team strength with uncertainty
stages.description: Both sides of a bubble race and both sides of a tie begin with opponent-adjusted strength and its posterior width; for bottom-of-table and last-place events the weakest teams are separated by small rating differences, so uncertainty width and short-memory form (new manager, injuries) dominate rankings among the bottom five.
stages.distribution: Posterior of latent strength with sd to be estimated (about 0.1 log goals is a placeholder); bottom-N membership is an order statistic of closely spaced values.

stages.name: Table state and the schedule left to play
stages.description: Remaining fixtures determine how points can still be earned: points gap to the cut line, number of matches remaining, strength and venue of the opposition (including direct clashes between rivals for survival or a slot), all of which determine a team's distribution of final points relative to the line. Bottom-six clubs dismiss managers often, so the remaining-fixture simulation draws in-season dismissals from soc.manager_dismissal_hazard (driven by simulated winless runs and points below expectation) and applies the re-blended post-change rating from soc.transfers; the new-manager bounce magnitude stays at zero until estimated, since much of it is mean reversion.
stages.distribution: Sum of remaining match lotteries (0/1/3); variance of gap relative to cut line scales with matches remaining.

stages.name: Where the cut line sits
stages.description: For relegation, promotion and qualification the line is not fixed: relegation can be shifted by play-offs (Bundesliga 16th place) or deductions, promotion runs partly through a play-off mini-tournament, and Champions League qualification depends on coefficient slots and on cup winners already holding a place. KXUCLQUAL settles on a main-tournament place, so spillover and qualifying rounds move its effective threshold; last-place and relegation series settle on rank only. Promotion and relegation play-offs are an explicit bracket (soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket): P(promoted) = P(automatic rank) + sum over play-off ranks of P(rank) x P(win bracket | rank). KXEFLPROMO is for 2026-27, the first season of the six-team Championship play-off (3rd-8th: single-leg eliminators 5v8 and 6v7 at the higher-placed club, two-legged semi-finals against 3rd and 4th, Wembley final); KXLALIGA2PROMO uses 3v6 and 4v5 two-legged semis and a two-legged final where a level aggregate after extra time goes to the better-placed club with no shootout.
stages.distribution: Discrete random threshold determined by cup winners and administrative rulings; effect is 0 or 1 place shifts with probabilities to be estimated (10-30% is a placeholder) in the cup-spillover case.

stages.name: Tie formats: legs, extra time and penalties
stages.description: An advancement market is the product of a first-leg state, a second-leg match, and then if needed extra time and penalties; the first-leg score, the venue of the second leg, and the team's priorities in the next league match drive risk-taking, and shootouts are close to coin flips. Away goals no longer decide UEFA ties but may in some national cups. KXUCLMOV maps the same tree onto three outcomes (advance in regular time, after extra time, via shootout), so the branch probabilities themselves are traded.
stages.distribution: Sequential probability tree; aggregate lead changes the match goal rate and draw probability; shootout win near 50% with small skill edge.

stages.name: Group-stage qualification and cross-group ranking
stages.description: Group qualification (World Cup, Nations League, Champions League league phase) depends on points, goal difference, head-to-head and in expanded formats on ranking third-placed teams across groups; the order of tiebreaks and the final-day simultaneous matches create strong dependencies between teams. KXUCLRO16 (top 8 or win the knockout play-off) and KXUCLBOTTOM (36th place) need the 36-team league-phase simulation over eight unbalanced fixtures rather than a group table.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution across teams and groups; tie-breaks create discrete jumps in qualification.

stages.name: Squad shocks and administrative events
stages.description: Injuries, international absences and suspensions shift strength during the run-in; sanctions (points deductions, licensing, administration) move teams across the line administratively, with probability mass concentrated at lower-profile leagues.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed strength shocks and rare discrete administrative events.

stages.name: Stage reached by sets of teams in a bracket tournament
stages.description: World Cup and UCL stage-reach series ask how far one team or a set of teams goes: the furthest stage by any nation of a qualification pathway, which host or which confederation nation goes furthest (dead heat if several share the stage), exactly N debutants reaching the knockouts, all hosts qualifying, or a non-top-10 nation reaching the semi-finals. These are functions of the joint stage-reached vector: bracket placement makes teams of the same group or half negatively dependent, so counts and maxima over a set cannot be built from independent marginals, and tie probabilities at a stage must be kept for the $1/N payouts. Host series (KXWCHOSTKO: all three hosts reach the knockout stage; KXWCHOSTSTAGE) apply soc.home_advantage to each host's group matches in its own country; KXWCHOSTKO is an intersection over hosts in different groups, so it is the product of near-independent group-qualification probabilities, each lifted by the host edge.
stages.distribution: Joint categorical vector of stages reached per team; counts over a set are dependent-Bernoulli sums, maxima have heavy mass at the round of 32 and round of 16.

talent_strength.note: Strength distribution with posterior width, needed particularly for tightly spaced bottom teams.

opponent_matchup.note: Direct clashes between rivals and group opponents.

role_personnel.note: Key-player availability across the run-in.

availability_news.note: Availability news; matters for ties more than for season-long placement.

coaching_scheme.note: In-season dismissal hazard for relegation-threatened clubs and the post-change rating re-blend; bounce size empirical.

environment.note: Weather, altitude and pitch affect single matches and their influence on season placement averages out; for ties, neutral-site venues are encoded in the aggregate-state and home-advantage logic rather than as a separate environmental input.

game_context_script.note: Aggregate and table state set risk posture and win probabilities.

pace_volume.note: Volume stats such as possession or shots matter only via the goal-model strengths feeding the simulation; no independent volume variable determines a table position or tie advancement, so no pace input is attached.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shootout conversion and extra-time finishing.

distribution_variance.note: Order-statistic and tail structure of the table, especially at the bottom.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Dead-rubber and priority rotation effects come from soc.rotation_index (predicted rotation) and break effects; soc.stakes_leverage and soc.motivation are simulation outputs (WEAK/duplicate) and are not cited as cover.

officiating_rules.note: Administrative sanctions, abandonment and voided matches.

settlement_contract.note: Tiebreaks, slot allocation and the contract wording.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Table series settle on the final official table: last place (single bottom rank), relegation ('is relegated from'), promotion ('is promoted from the EFL Championship', play-off route included), and UCL league-phase bottom. Tie series settle YES when the named side 'advance[s] past' its opponent in the named tie and round (finals add 'and lift the cup'; KXMLSADVANCE and KXINTERCUPADVANCE state 'including extra time and penalties'); legs and away-goals treatment are inherited from the competition. Qualification and stage-reach series (KXUCLQUAL, KXWCQUAL, KXUCLRO16/RO8/RO4/FINALIST, KXUCL16xxx, KXWCROUND, KXWCGROUPQUAL) settle on qualifying for the named stage even if the team then does not compete. KXUCLMOV splits a final into Regular Time / Extra Time / Penalty Shootout advancement. World Cup aggregate series settle on stage reached by sets of teams (furthest advancing nation of a confederation with a $1/N dead heat, stage of elimination with a withdrawal rule, counts of debutants or hosts reaching the knockouts).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Final official league table (governing body) for placement markets; official tie result including extra time and penalties for advancement markets; the competition's published regulations for tiebreaks and slot allocation.
variants_and_edge_cases: Last-place and relegation have different cut lines: 'last place' needs the single lowest points total and its tiebreak (La Liga/Serie A head-to-head first, Premier League goal difference first), while relegation is bottom-N and also affected by relegation play-offs in some leagues (Bundesliga 16th-place play-off, Ligue 1).

Qualification series settle on qualifying, not competing (KXUCLROUND, KXUCLRO16, KXWCROUND: 'if they qualify but do not end up competing, the market will still resolve to Yes'); KXUCLQUAL requires a main-tournament place, so slot spillover and qualifying rounds are part of the event.

Advancement series pool single-leg cups, two-leg Libertadores/Sudamericana ties, play-offs and World Cup group qualification (best-third-place rule); the number of legs, ET/penalties and away-goals treatment are competition-specific and not in the sampled text.

176 live series, 91 with rules text; 85 TITLE_ONLY (mostly league and cup 'Advance' series, KXBRASILEIRORELEGATION, KXWCHOSTSTAGE). Final-tie series add 'and lift the cup'; a sanction-driven table change after the last match is not addressed.

World Cup aggregate series: KXWCSTAGE (furthest stage by any team of a confederation pathway), KXWCSTAGEOFELIM (stage of elimination; a withdrawing team is assigned the next stage), KXWCFURTHESTADVANCING ($1/N dead heat), KXWCREGIONKO ('exactly N' debutants reach the knockouts), KXWCHOSTKO (all hosts), KXWC3RDPLACEQUAL, KXWCFIFATOP10 (any non-top-10 nation reaches the semi-finals).

Single-match items filed here: KXWCADVANCE text is 'wins the 3rd Place ... game' (window not stated), KXMLSADVANCE and KXINTERCUPADVANCE include extra time and penalties with a two-week postponement clause.

player_season_leader_and_awards.label: Player season leaders, totals and awards
player_season_leader_and_awards.target: Season-end player counting stats (goals, assists) leadership or totals relative to a strike.
player_season_leader_and_awards.mechanism: Player counting-stat markets combine the current tally with expected remaining minutes, per-90 production, penalty duty and the race against competitors. Production regresses toward xG-implied levels, and minutes carry injury/rotation risk. Joint simulation across candidates handles ties and tie-break rules; award markets add voting and team-success components.

inputs.why: Current tally and remaining fixtures.
Shot volume and quality per 90.
Expected minutes distribution.
Penalty share - the channel through which it moves the Player season leaders, totals and awards price.
Regress finishing over-performance.
Injury hazard - the channel through which it moves the Player season leaders, totals and awards price.
Opponent strength affects scoring chances.
Aerial/set-piece scoring role.
Voting narrative for award-linked markets.
Season production trend - the channel through which it moves the Player season leaders, totals and awards price.
Counted competitions and tie-break rules.
Shot volume per 90 for the candidate.
Team chance creation limits individual output.
Starting role in confirmed lineups.
Injury and role news - the channel through which it moves the Player season leaders, totals and awards price.
Separates team volume from role share, the quantity that changes when squads change.
Gives tails (long-term injury) that a mean minutes input misses.
Without it the same player goal tally is labelled differently across leader markets.
Sets the exposure that multiplies per-match scoring for every World Cup tally series.

interactions.hypothesis: Production is rate x minutes; minutes uncertainty dominates for fragile players.
Current leaders with large positive finishing delta should be shrunk toward xG-implied tallies.
A penalty taker's expected remaining goals include penalty xG, which can swing close races.

Expected goals is the factorisation team volume x share x minutes survival; the interaction of interest is that zero-inflated minutes make the exceedance probability of a rung lower than a mean-based Poisson suggests only when the mean is at or above the rung, and higher when the mean is well below it (the skewed minutes distribution widens both tails).
interactions.how_to_test: Compare probability of crossing the strike from simulation with mean-only prediction.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability of finishing first depends on tie rules: if ties split payouts, a candidate level with the leader has half the value, and if ties resolve on assists the playmaker striker gains; the gap-to-leader effect is conditional on the tie rule.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate leader markets under each tie rule and compare to observed settlements.

interactions.hypothesis: The expected future scoring rate is a shrunk mix of a hot finishing record and xG; the weight on realised goals decays with sample size, so equal over-performance is worth much less in a long remaining season.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest forward goals/90 on past npxG and past goals with an interaction in sample size.

interactions.hypothesis: Penalty duty adds roughly the team penalty rate times conversion (for example 0.15 team penalties per match x about 0.78 = about 0.1 goals per match) for the designated taker only; the gain is a product of the taker flag and the team penalty rate, not a threshold, and varies with referee and VAR habits.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress goals on designated-taker flag and team penalty rate.

interactions.hypothesis: Tournament tallies are per-match intensity times a random match count, and the two are positively correlated because a team advances partly through its striker's goals; ignoring this correlation under-prices high totals (record, 11+ goals) and over-prices middling ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated tally distributions with and without joint goal-and-progression simulation against past World Cup top-scorer totals.

nonlinearities.shape: Left-skewed, zero-inflated minutes distribution
nonlinearities.why: Minutes are bimodal at injury (0) and full-minutes outcomes; linear expectations misprice exceedance probabilities for round-number rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: Sigmoid in gap to leader scaled by sqrt(remaining expected goals)
nonlinearities.why: Probability of overtaking depends on gap relative to the sd of remaining goals; the 2-goal and 5-goal breakpoints are placeholders to be estimated from the race simulation.

nonlinearities.shape: Shrinkage weight rising with sample size
nonlinearities.why: Predictive weight on observed over-performance grows with shots taken, roughly n/(n+k) with k to be estimated (about 100 shots is a placeholder).

mechanism_review.summary: For a season total or a leader market the outcome is the realised tally at the deadline: expected goals equals matches times minutes survival times team chance volume times the player's share times finishing, with penalty duty adding a discrete block. Minutes are a survival process with a zero-inflated left tail; finishing luck must be shrunk; teammates and managers change the share mid-season. A leader market is the maximum of many correlated tallies, so variance and tie rules matter as much as means. World Cup goal series run over at most about eight tournament matches, so they are short count processes; leader rules settle on official regular-season statistics with a dead heat when no tiebreak is declared and No for a player who never plays, while the EPL stat ladder counting scope is not visible. For World Cup series the number of matches played is itself random through the team's bracket path, and streak, record and combined series need match-by-match joint simulation.

stages.name: Availability and minutes over the remaining season
stages.description: A player's tally can only grow while he plays; the remaining-season minutes distribution is determined by the injury hazard (with history of recurrence), suspensions, rotation and the risk of leaving the competition (winter transfer, loan), so expected minutes is a survival-type quantity. A starter with 85% of minutes in the first 12 games can lose a quarter of the remaining season to a single injury.
stages.distribution: Survival and recurrence process; minutes are zero-inflated with a mass at 0 (injury) and a bulk near 80-90 per start; heavy left tail.

stages.name: Per-match goal or assist intensity
stages.description: Per 90 the player scores according to shot volume, shot quality and finishing, plus penalty duty; role in the team (focal striker vs shared) determines the share of team xG, and teammate arrivals or departures change that share. Per-match intensity is combined with the opponent's defence and the team's expected goals for that fixture. Assist races (EPL, UCL) replace shot share by chance-creation share, set-piece delivery duty and teammates' finishing, which add noise beyond the passer's own skill.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like per-match counts; strong dependence on set pieces and penalties; season totals are overdispersed relative to a Poisson with the mean xG.

stages.name: Luck versus skill in current tally
stages.description: The running total includes finishing over- or under-performance relative to xG which should be regressed toward the player's multi-season baseline; a striker at 12 goals from 7 xG is a regression candidate while another at 7 from 12 xG is not. The shrinkage fraction is large over a half season.
stages.distribution: Poisson noise plus persistent skill; finishing skill persists weakly (persistence share to be estimated; 20-30% is a placeholder).

stages.name: Race dynamics across candidates
stages.description: Leader markets are decided by the maximum across many correlated candidates: teammates compete for the same chances, candidates share fixtures, and ties and tiebreaks matter; the probability a candidate is first depends on the gap to the leader and on how many rivals are within reach, not on his own mean alone.
stages.distribution: Order-statistic outcome from a vector of correlated overdispersed counts; the maximum rewards variance (high-volume strikers with injury risk).

stages.name: Tournament exposure set by the team's progress
stages.description: In World Cup series a player's tally is bounded by how many matches his nation plays: three group games, then up to five knockout games including the third-place match. The distribution of matches played comes from the team's group and bracket simulation, so a striker on a likely semi-finalist has roughly twice the exposure of an equal striker on a likely group exit; extra-time minutes add exposure in drawn knockouts. Per-match scoring intensity is multiplied by this random number of matches.
stages.distribution: Discrete number of matches (3-8) from the bracket simulation, mixed with per-match negative-binomial goals; the mixture is strongly right-skewed for elite teams.

stages.name: Settlement scope, dead heat and DNP
stages.description: The contract reads the official league total for the regular season (or all EPL games for the stat ladder, World Cup tournament games for career goals): goals for two clubs within the league are combined, a candidate with no appearances resolves No, and a tie with no official tiebreak pays a dead-heat share; parsing scope and dead-heat rules per series avoids label errors in training data.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from official statistics; scope ambiguity is the only randomness.

stages.name: Path-dependent and combined tournament tallies
stages.description: Some World Cup series depend on the order or combination of goals: a streak of consecutive matches entered with a goal (carried over from 2022), the round in which a career record is first broken outright, whether any player passes 13 goals, and the sum of three named strikers. These need match-by-match simulation of each player's goals jointly with his team's path, keeping correlation between teammates and the record state, rather than end-of-tournament marginal totals.
stages.distribution: Sequential Bernoulli/negative-binomial per match; streak and record events are rare tail events with probabilities often below 5%, and trio sums are overdispersed through shared team paths.

talent_strength.note: Per-90 scoring rates with opponent context; leaders are the top of a talent distribution.

opponent_matchup.note: Fixture difficulty and set-piece opportunity for each candidate.

role_personnel.note: Role, penalty duty, share of team shots, minutes.

availability_news.note: Injury hazard and news flow; long horizon so status vintage matters less than hazard.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager changes alter a striker's role and service, and a tactical shift (system change, new playmaker) can change goals per 90 by 20-30% in the middle of a season; no input quantifies this and press-conference news does not capture it.

environment.note: Weather and pitch effects on a single player's goal count are small and average out over dozens of matches; their impact is already in the per-90 rate, so no separate environmental input is required for a season total.

game_context_script.note: Current tally, matches remaining and the position relative to the leader.

pace_volume.note: Team chance volume (team xG) and the player's share of it set the number of scoring opportunities; raw shots (WEAK) are not used as cover.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing over/under-performance and xG context.

distribution_variance.note: Order-statistic race simulations and dispersion of totals.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Congestion and rotation across competitions act through expected minutes and the minutes-survival curve; the WEAK soc.lineups_pit is not used as cover.

officiating_rules.note: Referee identity affects penalties awarded to a given team only slightly over a season and averages out; it matters at the match level for first-event contracts, not for season-long leader totals, so no officiating input is attached here.

settlement_contract.note: Counting scope, tie rules, own-goal and disallowed-goal handling.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Twenty player-tally series, all with rules text. League leaders: YES when the player has the highest regular-season total of goals (Bundesliga, La Liga, Serie A, Ligue 1, Liga MX Apertura, MLS) or assists (KXEPLLEADER, and KXUCLLEADER for the UCL tournament) per official league statistics; goals for several clubs in the league combine, a player who plays no games resolves No, and a tie with no official tiebreak is a dead heat (KXLEADERUCLGOALS: $1/N rounded down). KXEPLSEASONSTAT: N+ goals across all games of the EPL season. World Cup series: the anytime-goal, goal-count, trio, country-top-scorer and streak texts include regulation, stoppage and extra time; those and the Golden Boot total and record texts exclude shootout goals; the career, goal-leader and Mbappe-record texts state no window. Series cover scoring at all (no entry = No), N+ goals including the third-place match, Golden Boot leader with FIFA tiebreaks (most assists, then fewest minutes), country top scorer ($1/N dead heat, 'No Goalscorer' leg), Golden Boot winner's total 15+, a named trio's combined 22+, a 9+ match scoring streak across 2022 and 2026 in matches entered, any player beating 13 goals, Mbappe becoming sole all-time leader in a named round, and career 40+ World Cup goals. Own goals are excluded explicitly in the career, Golden Boot total, streak and record texts (and are not credited to the scorer elsewhere).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official league statistics (goals/assists, regular season or tournament) as documented by the league or UEFA; FIFA official tournament records and Golden Boot tiebreaks for World Cup series; own goals and shootout goals excluded.
variants_and_edge_cases: Leader markets: dead heat if tied and the league declares no single leader ($1/N in KXLEADERUCLGOALS), goals for several clubs within the league combined, a candidate who plays no games resolves No; Liga MX and MLS use the Apertura/regular season only.
Assist leaders (KXEPLLEADER, KXUCLLEADER) depend on the provider's assist attribution, a noisier and more definition-sensitive count than goals.

World Cup series run over three to eight matches per team: the number of matches a player can play depends on his team's progress, the third-place match counts for goal counts and career totals, extra time counts and shootouts do not.

Path-dependent World Cup series: KXWCGOALSTREAK (consecutive matches entered with a goal across 2022 and 2026), KXWCMBAPPEGOALLEADER (the round in which he first becomes sole record holder, with a 'does not break record' leg), KXWCRECORD (any player above 13), KXWCGOALCOMBO (sum of a named trio).

KXEPLSEASONSTAT 'across all games during the 2026-27 EPL season' leaves the counting scope (league only vs all competitions) to interpretation; KXWCPLAYERGOALS resolves No (not void) if the player never enters.

first_to_score_event.label: First team to score
first_to_score_event.target: Which team scores first (or none) in the match.
first_to_score_event.mechanism: First-to-score is a race between two inhomogeneous Poisson processes with a null outcome for 0-0. The team with higher early hazard (press intensity, set-piece threat, penalty probability) is favoured beyond share of lambda, and the null outcome mass depends on low-score dependence. Rules for own goals and abandoned matches determine settlement.

inputs.why: Minute-level hazard of each team.
Relative strength - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Probability of no goal - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Early dead-ball threat - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Press intensity front-loads chances.
Lineup effect - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Penalty as first-goal source - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Home share of first goals - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Own-goal, null-outcome and abandonment handling.
Team xG sets hazard ratio - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Starting XI - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Early shot volume - the channel through which it moves the First team to score price.
Directly sets the gate P(draw at 90) of the method path tree.
Calibrates every node of the Method path tree against history rather than an assumed 50%.
Turns a lump first-goal hazard into route-specific intensities that respond to referee and set-piece news.
Provides the actual drivers for league MOV series, whose outcome set cannot be the knockout path tree; shared in definition with handicap_and_exact_score margin inputs.

interactions.hypothesis: Consistency between hazard integral and the 0-0 cell is a check on the goal model.
High-press sides score earlier so hazards peak early rather than being proportional to full-match lambda.
Dead-ball and penalty events provide step increments in hazard not captured by open-play xG.

The knockout draw rate depends on the aggregate: a team leading by two from the first leg sits deep and cuts match goals, while a trailing team must attack, so the cagey factor is a function of the aggregate state and not a constant.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin second-leg matches by aggregate margin and compare draw rates against a first-leg baseline.

interactions.hypothesis: Shootout skill only matters when the match reaches penalties, so its weight in the Method price is the product of P(draw at 90) and P(ET draw); in a lopsided tie that product is under 6% and skill is negligible. This is a structural identity (the node weight equals the product of the two draw probabilities), used to gate where shootout inputs matter rather than as a learned interaction.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(pens win) predictions for ties with high vs low P(reach pens).

interactions.hypothesis: The first-goal minute and route are jointly distributed: set pieces concentrate after minute 30 while penalties are timed by referee decisions, so the intensity decomposition changes the win-the-race probability and the minute distribution together.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the first-goal CDF by route and compare with a pooled hazard in held-out matches.

interactions.hypothesis: Home advantage multiplies the intensity ratio, so in a neutral-venue final it disappears and the favourite's first-scorer odds fall by an amount to be estimated from neutral-venue finals relative to the same pairing at home.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit first-scorer indicator with home and neutral flags.

interactions.hypothesis: A depleted favourite (missing starters) has a lower win-in-90 but a smaller drop in ET win, because ET advantage depends on bench depth and fitness more than on the starting XI; the effect on the tree is node-dependent. (hypothesis: no evidence is cited that ET advantage depends more on bench depth than on the starting XI)
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate node probabilities with an interaction for lineup strength.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave first-goal CDF with right-skewed minute
nonlinearities.why: The probability a goal arrives by minute t is 1-exp(-integral hazard), so equal differences in hazard matter more early.

nonlinearities.shape: Compressed around 0.5
nonlinearities.why: Shootout skill shifts P(pens win) by a few points only; the response is bounded by the binomial noise of five kicks.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by stage and leg
nonlinearities.why: Cagey adjustments differ sharply between first leg, second leg and single-leg final; a linear multiplier misprices the tails.

mechanism_review.summary: Two distinct mechanisms live under this key. A Method of Victory/Finish contract is a path tree over regulation, extra time and penalties: the regulation result gates everything, knockout-specific cautiousness inflates the draw gate, extra time is a low-scoring tired period of 30 minutes, and a shootout is close to a coin flip with small first-kicker and goalkeeper edges. A First-Team-To-Score contract is a competing-risk race between two time-varying scoring intensities with a no-goal outcome, where early goals have a distinctive set-piece and penalty mix. Both settle from official match records, the FTTS settlement (entire-game window, own-goal credit, a listed No Goal outcome) is verified from 23 texts, while none of the 37 Method series has rules text. The Method path tree (s2) is a consolidated copy of unreg:knockout_method_of_victory, whose rules-verified MOV/MOF template covers the knockout series; it applies only to knockout series with a possible extra time; the six domestic-league MOV series are handled by the conditional margin stage s7 until their rules are read.

stages.name: Ninety-minute result distribution
stages.description: Method of victory starts with the regulation outcome: home win, draw, away win, from the goal model with team strength, home advantage and lineups. Only matches level after 90 minutes proceed to the extra paths, so P(draw at 90) is the gate that determines the entire non-regulation mass.
stages.distribution: Three-outcome distribution with draw probability about 25-30% in league play and 28-35% in cup knockouts.

stages.name: Knockout Method-of-Victory/Finish path tree (consolidated onto unreg:knockout_method_of_victory)
stages.description: The Method series still filed here (title-only, no markets listed) share Kalshi's MOV/MOF template verified on KXUCLMOF, KXUELMOV, KXWCMOF and KXWCMOV, which the reconciliation filed to unreg:knockout_method_of_victory: Regular Time (90 plus stoppage), Extra Time, Penalty Shootout. They are priced with that record's path tree and the same inputs, not a separate copy: knockout draw inflation and leg state, the extra-time phase rate and late risk appetite, then the shootout. This duplicates the knockout record on purpose; the two must not diverge.
stages.distribution: Three-branch path tree: P(regulation decisive), P(ET decisive)=P(level at 90)xP(ET goal decides), P(shootout); shootout near 0.5 per side.

stages.name: First-goal timing and route (for first-team-to-score variants)
stages.description: For first-to-score the relevant process is the competing-risk race between the two sides' scoring intensities in minutes, with a P(no goal) at P(0-0). Early goals come disproportionately from set pieces and penalties; the stronger attacker wins the race with probability lambda_a/(lambda_a+lambda_b) at first-order, adjusted by timing hazards and the opening-period cautiousness of each side. In knockout ties of competitions that play extra time the FTTS texts count the entire game, so the race window can extend to 120 minutes and P(no goal) must be computed over that window; extra-time hazard uses the lower tired-play intensity from the extra-time stage. Verified window (FTTS rules text): the race runs over the entire game including any extra time, the shootout excluded; P(team A first) = lambda_A/(lambda_A+lambda_B) x (1 - exp(-(lambda_A+lambda_B) x T)) with T the expected exposure (90+stoppage, plus extra time with P(level at 90) in knockouts), and both teams resolve No on 0-0.
stages.distribution: Competing exponential hazards with time-varying intensity; first-goal minute is right-skewed with median about minute 25-30; P(no goal) about 7-9% in leagues, higher in cup ties.

stages.name: Settlement mapping
stages.description: The method contract maps the observed path (regulation, extra time, penalties) into one of its outcomes, and the first-scorer contract maps the goal log; competition-specific rules (golden goal absent today, away goals abolished in UEFA competitions, aggregate rules) determine whether an ET occurs at all.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from official match record; competition rules vary and change over time.

stages.name: League Method-of-Victory series: margin-of-victory reading (conditional)
stages.description: If the six domestic-league KX*MOV series (La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Brasileiro, Liga MX) settle on a goal-margin bucket rather than regulation/extra-time/penalties, the outcome is the regulation goal difference, generated by the same two team intensities as the 90-minute result but read through a margin partition; no extra-time or shootout stage applies and the knockout cagey factor is irrelevant. This stage is conditional on the rules text, which is not sampled.
stages.distribution: Discrete signed goal difference with mass concentrated on -1, 0 and +1, slightly over-dispersed relative to Skellam through score-state effects.
