contract_review.settlement_definition: Three contract families share this key. First Team to Score (32 KX*FTTS series, 23 with rules text): one binary per team, YES when that team 'records the first goal during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)'; an own goal counts for the team awarded it; a shootout is outside the window. A separate 'No Goal' outcome is listed ('If no team records the first goal during the entire game', KXWCFTTS, KXGERSCFTTS, KXENGCSFTTS), so the three outcomes partition the match. Method of Victory (23 KX*MOV) and Method of Finish (14 KX*MOF) series are all TITLE_ONLY: outcome labels, league-fixture treatment and aggregate-tie handling are unknown (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS). No FTTS text has a postponement or abandonment clause.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official match report goal events with scorer team and minute (own goals credited to the team awarded), including extra-time periods, for FTTS; not verified for the Method series (presumably official result including extra time and shootout).
variants_and_edge_cases: First Team to Score (23 of 32 series with rules text, identical wording across leagues, UEFA competitions, cups, super cups and the World Cup): window is the entire game including any extra time; own goals count for the team awarded; a goalless game resolves the listed 'No Goal' outcome YES and both team markets No.

League FTTS fixtures cannot reach extra time, so their window is 90 minutes plus stoppage. Extra time exists only where the competition plays it: Coppa Italia, DFB Pokal, Copa del Rey, FA Cup proper rounds, World Cup and UCL/UEL/UECL knockout second legs; under current rules the EFL Cup (before the final), Leagues Cup, Community Shield, DFL-Supercup and UEFA Super Cup go straight to penalties after a 90-minute draw, so the 'any extra time periods' clause is inert there. Where extra time exists it lowers P(no goal) relative to a regulation-only window.

No FTTS text contains a postponement or abandonment clause (the 48-hour fair-price rule appears only in sibling game/half texts), so settlement of a match abandoned after the first goal, or postponed, is not visible.

Method of Victory/Finish contracts (KX*MOV, KX*MOF) are TITLE_ONLY; the outcomes are plausibly win in regulation / in extra time / on penalties for knockouts, but six MOV series are league fixtures (KXLALIGAMOV, KXSERIEAMOV, KXBUNDESLIGAMOV, KXLIGUE1MOV, KXBRASILEIROMOV, KXLIGAMXMOV) where extra time cannot occur and the outcome set is unknown (stage s7 is a conditional placeholder).

Draw at 90 minutes in two-leg ties may end the tie without extra time (aggregate leader advances) so the MOV/MOF path tree is competition-specific; no sampled text says how single-leg vs two-leg is treated.
KXWCFTTS has rules text with the entire-game window and the no-goal leg; KXWCTTSF (World Cup Team To Score First) has none and is assumed identical.

The Kalshi MOV/MOF template is verified on KXUCLMOF, KXUELMOV, KXWCMOF and KXWCMOV (now filed to unreg:knockout_method_of_victory): 'Regular Time' includes stoppage and excludes extra time and the shootout; MOF settles on either team, MOV on the named team; cancellation or rescheduling beyond two weeks resolves to a fair price. The 37 Method series left here have no listed markets and are assumed to follow it.

team_points_and_margin.label: Team season points and points margin
team_points_and_margin.target: A team's final points total (or gap between two teams) relative to a strike.
team_points_and_margin.mechanism: Team points are a sum of match results; the mean follows expected points from ratings and schedule, and the variance depends on draw rates, rating uncertainty and correlation across matches. Margin markets between two teams need their joint distribution, including direct meetings.

interactions.hypothesis: A draw-prone team has a different variance for the same expected points.
Rating uncertainty matters more with many fixtures left, and schedule matters more with few.
Margin markets must incorporate pending deductions affecting one team only.

A pending deduction on the leader or the runner-up shifts the first-minus-second gap by the deduction size, so a margin near 15 can cross the strike in either direction without any match being played; the effect is zero for clubs outside the top two.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate margins with and without announced deductions and compare against realised margins in seasons with sanctions.

interactions.hypothesis: The margin depends on whether the leader and runner-up still have to meet: a remaining direct meeting is a six-point swing that raises margin variance, while once both meetings are played the two totals evolve more independently through different schedules.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare margin distribution width in simulations before and after the last direct meeting.

interactions.hypothesis: Points thresholds far above a club's expected total are convex in rating uncertainty: wider posterior strength fattens the upper tail, so 75+ for a club expected at 65 rises sharply with uncertainty while near-median thresholds barely move.
interactions.how_to_test: Calibrate threshold probabilities by distance from expected total with and without posterior-draw simulation.

interactions.hypothesis: For three group wins the third game switches regime: a team already qualified after two wins may rotate, lowering its win probability, while a team needing a win plays full strength; this conditional dependence lowers P(3 wins) below the naive product.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare third-game win rates of World Cup and Euro teams already qualified vs not, controlling for rating gap.

interactions.hypothesis: A key injury during a congested stretch lowers expected points over many fixtures at once; below a squad-depth threshold the loss compounds with rotation, shifting the season total and, for contenders, the margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points-per-game residuals on key-player absence interacted with congestion.

interactions.hypothesis: A club below its expected points has a raised dismissal hazard; a dismissal switches the rating regime for all remaining matches, so the season-points distribution is a mixture that is wider and left-skewed for struggling clubs, and a contender's change moves both its points threshold and the first-minus-second margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare season-points calibration (PIT histograms) for clubs that changed manager in-season, with and without the simulated dismissal branch.

nonlinearities.shape: Right-skewed survival function in the strike
nonlinearities.why: P(margin>=m) decays slowly for a dominant champion and fast otherwise, so a single 15-point strike sits on very different parts of the curve by league and season.

nonlinearities.shape: Sigmoid in threshold minus expected total
nonlinearities.why: Threshold probabilities follow a CDF of an approximately normal total with sd 6-8 points, so they are near 0/1 beyond about two sd and steep near the mean.

mechanism_review.summary: Three contract types share this key. Team Points thresholds are the final season points total of one club: banked points plus a sum of remaining 0/1/3 outcomes whose probabilities come from ratings, venue and draw propensity, widened by shared rating uncertainty and shifted by deductions. Champion Winning Margin is the first-minus-second order statistic over all clubs' totals, a right-tail event at the 15-point strike that depends on the leader's dominance and the weakness of the best rival. The World Cup series requires three group wins, a product of match win probabilities with a third-game incentive effect. Rotation and injuries create regime shifts, and settlement reads official standings with explicit zero-margin and deduction rules.

stages.name: Per-match win and draw probabilities
stages.description: Every series is built from match-level outcome probabilities: each remaining league fixture (and each of the three World Cup group games) gets P(win), P(draw) and P(loss) from opponent-adjusted strengths and venue. Points thresholds weight a draw as one point, the three-group-wins series counts only wins, and the margin series needs these probabilities for every contender, so the draw split matters differently in each variant.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per match with p between 0.25 (away at a top side) and 0.85 (home against a weak side); sequence-dependent through shared strength uncertainty.

stages.name: Remaining schedule and its order
stages.description: The remaining league schedule fixes how many points are still available and against whom: a mid-table club with a soft run-in has a higher points ceiling than one facing the top six, and the champion-margin series depends on both the leader's and the runner-up's remaining schedules, including their direct meeting. For World Cup group series the three fixtures and their order (opening game vs dead rubber) are known at listing.
stages.distribution: Deterministic fixture list; random only through postponements and cup-induced rescheduling.

stages.name: First-minus-second order statistic for the champion margin
stages.description: For the Winning Margin series the outcome is the gap between the highest and second-highest final totals among all clubs, not the gap between two named clubs: a 15+ margin requires the champion's total to be high and the best rival's to be low at the same time. The relevant inputs are the joint distribution of the top few totals, their correlation through direct meetings and common opponents, and current banked points; a single dominant club makes the margin right-skewed.
stages.distribution: Order statistic of correlated points totals; margin sd about 6-8 points over a full season with strong right skew when one club is dominant; P(margin>=15) is a tail probability.

stages.name: Rotation, injuries and fatigue across the stretch
stages.description: Congestion from European and cup fixtures causes league rotation and lowers expected points per match, and a long injury to a key player lowers the whole remaining points path; for World Cup groups a team already qualified after two wins may rotate in the third game. These regimes move the season totals of contenders unevenly, which matters for both thresholds and the margin.
stages.distribution: Regime shifts in p_t by rotation and injury states; effect size 0.03-0.10 per-match p.

stages.name: Settlement and contract scope
stages.description: Points thresholds read the official standings (points awarded, deductions included); the margin series reads the final table with level points giving 0 (Serie A: 0 after a title play-off); the World Cup series counts three group-stage wins only. Abandoned or voided matches change totals through awarded results, which no text addresses explicitly.
stages.distribution: Deterministic from official records; ambiguity in scope definitions.

stages.name: Season points total for the Team Points thresholds
stages.description: For the Team Points series the final total is points already banked plus 3 per win and 1 per draw over the remaining league fixtures; each fixture's win and draw probabilities come from opponent-adjusted ratings, venue and draw propensity, and the sum is wider than a binomial because rating uncertainty is shared across all remaining fixtures. Points in the official standings also absorb any administrative deduction, which shifts the whole distribution. In-season managerial change is drawn inside the points simulation from soc.manager_dismissal_hazard and, when it occurs, the remaining matches use the soc.transfers re-blended rating, which widens the points distribution of under-performing clubs and, for contenders, the champion margin; the shift size is set to zero until the event study.
stages.distribution: Sum of about 24-28 categorical outcomes (0/1/3) with shared rating error; sd of the remaining-points total roughly 6-8 for a mid-table club; a deduction is a discrete left shift.

stages.name: Three group wins in a World Cup group (KXWCGSUNDEFEATED)
stages.description: The World Cup group series pays only if the team wins all three group games, so P(YES) is roughly the product of three match win probabilities, adjusted for dependence through shared rating error and for the third-game incentive: a team that has already won twice is usually through and may rotate, while one needing a win plays at full strength. Draw-prone low-scoring tournament football makes this a low-probability event for all but the strongest sides against weak groups.
stages.distribution: Product of three dependent Bernoullis; P(3 wins) from about 0.02 for weak teams to about 0.35-0.45 for a heavy favourite in a weak group.

talent_strength.note: Team strength and posterior width determine every p_t and their correlation.

opponent_matchup.note: Remaining opponents per club and direct meetings between the top two.

role_personnel.note: Key-player availability across the stretch.

availability_news.note: Availability news for the matches in the next weeks; vintage matters less over a multi-month window.

coaching_scheme.note: In-season dismissal hazard and the post-change re-blended rating inside the points simulation; shift size empirical.

environment.note: Venue and weather act through each match's win/draw probabilities (home advantage is in the match model); season totals and the margin add no separate environmental mechanism.

game_context_script.note: Banked points and gaps at the as-of date, and World Cup group state before the third game.

pace_volume.note: Volume statistics matter only through team ratings; points totals, margins and group wins are functions of match outcomes, not of possession or shot counts.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and saving luck in banked results is regressed through xG-based ratings, so the remaining-fixture probabilities are not inflated by an over-performing start.

distribution_variance.note: Order-statistic tail of the margin and the width of the season points distribution.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Predicted rotation and cumulative minutes load across the December and spring fixture pile (soc.rotation_index, soc.congestion_load, both catalog inputs) plus the schedule list; soc.motivation (audited WEAK) is no longer cited.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating tendencies affect single matches (penalties, cards) and average out over a season or a three-game group; no systematic officiating mechanism changes points totals or margins.

settlement_contract.note: Standings points with deductions, zero-margin rule, three-wins definition.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Eleven live series, all with rules text. Team Points (EPL, La Liga, Serie A, Ligue 1, Bundesliga): YES when the club 'reaches at least N points' (floor N-0.5), resolved on the points awarded in the official season standings, so deductions count. Champion Winning Margin (same five leagues): YES when the champion finishes 15 or more points (greater_or_equal) above second in the final official table; level points give margin 0 regardless of tiebreaker, and in Serie A a title play-off after level points also gives 0. KXWCGSUNDEFEATED, despite its 'Undefeated' title, settles YES only if the named team 'wins 3 matches in the group stage' of the 2026 World Cup (a draw fails it). No postponement or abandonment clause appears in any text.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final season standings of the named league (points awarded after deductions) for Team Points and Winning Margin; official FIFA group-stage results for KXWCGSUNDEFEATED.
variants_and_edge_cases: Team Points thresholds are N+ on banked points plus 3W+D over the remaining 24-28 league fixtures (as of November 2026; 34-match Bundesliga), read from the official standings so an administrative deduction shifts the whole distribution.

Margin series use one strike of 15+ points per league: the event needs a dominant champion and a weak runner-up, so it is a right-tail event of the first-minus-second order statistic; Serie A's zero-margin rule refers to a play-off after level points.
KXWCGSUNDEFEATED title says 'Undefeated' but the rules text requires 3 wins; the third group game may be a dead rubber for a team already through, lowering its win probability through rotation.
No text covers postponed matches that are never played or voided seasons; Team Points relies on the standings 'points awarded', which would include awarded (forfeit) results.

soccer_special_and_host.label: Soccer specials, hosts and governance markets
soccer_special_and_host.target: A named official announcement or event (host selection, appointment, special) within the contract window.
soccer_special_and_host.mechanism: These markets are decided by committees, clubs and negotiations. The useful structure is the decision calendar, credible-source leaks and base rates for rumour conversion, and especially the exact contract definition of 'official'. No stable statistical model exists; the catalog treats them as hypothesis-driven event-timing problems.

interactions.hypothesis: Only a formal confirmation inside the window counts, so base rates must be conditioned on deadline and wording.
Jumps with signed flow indicate informed leak; jumps without flow look like stale repricing.
Transfer fee/club finance constraints condition how fast rumours can convert.

Inside the last 12 months of a contract and with a window open before the deadline, the hazard jumps; with no window before the contract's date, the probability of a transfer is only from emergency/free-agent routes, so the window availability gates the contract-state effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the hazard model with an interaction between months to expiry and a window-open indicator.

interactions.hypothesis: Without credible news the prior drifts slowly; after a top-tier confirmation the probability jumps near certainty irrespective of the base rate, so the information regime replaces the base-rate regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of resolved outcomes after each source tier's reports.

interactions.hypothesis: A dismissal changes the transfer outlook for the club's stars (new manager's priorities) and vice versa; manager exits often precede window activity, so one hazard is conditional on the other state. (speculative cross-lag, not supported by the sampled contract texts; treat as a hypothesis for event-study testing)
interactions.how_to_test: Cross-lagged analysis of manager change and star departures within 60 days.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability of a final decision before the deadline is piecewise in stage: near zero before hearing, rises after ruling, and appeal windows add a second step; the number of titles stripped depends on appeal outcomes. Note that soc.points_deductions measures league points deductions only; a titles-stripped legal outcome (KXMANCITYTITLES) is a different procedural result and is driven by soc.governance_procedure_stage, not by this input.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute conditional probabilities per stage from past cases.

interactions.hypothesis: A star with a short contract at a club that has just lost its manager and sold others has a hazard far above the product of separate effects, because the club's bargaining position and the player's incentive both shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress departure on interactions of contract months and club transition indicators.

nonlinearities.shape: Steeply convex in months to expiry below 12
nonlinearities.why: Hazard of leaving rises sharply as expiry approaches because the club must sell or lose the player for free, so the function is not linear in months.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail in time-to-event
nonlinearities.why: Governance and transfer timings have fat tails; the survival function is not exponential and a constant hazard overstates short-window probabilities.

nonlinearities.shape: Spike in daily hazard at the deadline
nonlinearities.why: Daily hazard is highly non-uniform: a disproportionate share of window deals complete in the final days, so cumulative probability by date is convex until the deadline.

mechanism_review.summary: An off-field soccer contract is a rare-event hazard resolved by an official announcement inside a window. The prior comes from a reference class (club state, player or manager profile, body and process type); the actor's fundamentals (contract end and release clause, results versus expectation, legal stage) tilt the hazard; the calendar (window deadlines, committee dates, effective dates) decides whether the event can occur before the contract's end; and information arrives as tiered reports whose reliability sets how far probability should jump. Multi-outcome sets (next club, co-hosts) need 'no change' and non-exclusive handling, and loans, sign-and-loan and effective-date wording must be read per series. Scope: transfers, managers, office-holders, governance, participation and host/format announcements; the only sporting-skill series is the MLS skills challenge (stage s7).

stages.name: Reference-class base rate in the window
stages.description: Each event type has a base rate that depends on its reference class: a top-club star leaving in a given calendar year, a manager at a given league position being dismissed within a season, a host selection by a given body; the window length, the starting state of the actor (tenure, contract, league position) and the structural calendar anchor the prior before any news.
stages.distribution: Rare-event hazard with prior from event counts per class; a few percent per month for a star player's departure, much higher for a bottom-table manager.

stages.name: Actor fundamentals and incentives
stages.description: A transfer requires a willing player, a willing seller and a buyer that can afford the fee and wages: contract expiry date, release clause, club finances, squad needs and the player's stated intentions determine feasibility; managers face board tolerance linked to results, owners and succession options; sanctions depend on evidence and legal process.
stages.distribution: Discrete-time hazard conditional on contract and club state; strongly nonlinear in months to contract end.

stages.name: Calendar and timing structure
stages.description: Transfers cluster at window deadlines (a large share of window deals complete in the final days; the exact share is unsourced here), managerial dismissals follow poor-result runs and international breaks, and governance decisions follow committee dates and appeal periods. A contract whose window ends before a calendar decision date will resolve No whatever the merits.
stages.distribution: Event times clustered at deadlines; heavy-tailed delay distributions for regulatory processes.

stages.name: Information flow and credibility
stages.description: News arrives in tiers: club/federation statements, established journalists' 'here we go' confirmations, rumours from aggregators; the likelihood ratio of each tier and the lag from leak to official confirmation determine how fast a probability should move, and a false report is common at lower tiers.
stages.distribution: Jump process in log odds with reliability-dependent jump sizes; confirmation lag of hours to weeks.

stages.name: Governance and legal process
stages.description: Host selections and sanction decisions are decided by named bodies with procedural stages (bid evaluation, hearings, ruling, appeal) and politics; the events are lumpy, with long periods of nothing and sudden announcements; the stripping of a specific count of titles is a multi-valued legal outcome. Team-participation and format series (Iran competing, DR Congo in the playoffs, a 64-team 2030 field, relocation of US matches) are the same kind of governance outcome: a body's decision, a withdrawal or a disqualification inside the window.
stages.distribution: Staged process with random stage durations and lumpy outcomes; multi-valued legal outcome (0, 1, 2, ... titles).

stages.name: Settlement mapping and multi-outcome bookkeeping
stages.description: Settlement uses effective dates and official announcements; the 'next club' and host sets must include 'no change' and multiple co-host cases; loans count in some contracts and not in others, so label construction requires reading each series' wording.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from announcement records; ambiguity is in definitions.

stages.name: All-Star skills challenge winner (KXMLSSKILLS)
stages.description: The MLS All-Star Skills Challenge is a short exhibition of shooting, passing and crossing drills scored per round; the winner is determined by drill scores among a handful of selected players or teams, not by match play. Outcomes depend on the event format, which players are entered, and specific technical skills (long passing accuracy, shooting under time), with high noise from few attempts per drill.
stages.distribution: Multinomial over a small field with near-uniform priors adjusted by drill-specific skill; few attempts make outcomes highly random.

environment.note: Weather, venue and pitch have no bearing on a transfer, appointment or governance decision; the only environment is the institutional context handled under the calendar and governance inputs.

game_context_script.note: Timing structure of windows and procedures.

pace_volume.note: There is no volume or opportunity count in an announcement event; the analogue (number of news items) is information flow, covered by the announcement-signals input, so a pace input is meaningless.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate or efficiency process exists for a one-off announcement; the nearest analogue, the conversion of leaks to confirmations, is part of the source-credibility measurement rather than a separate efficiency input.

distribution_variance.note: Rare-event distribution and jump-process news updates.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Window deadlines, results runs and international breaks.

officiating_rules.note: Rules and procedures of governing bodies; sanctions framework.

settlement_contract.note: Effective date vs announcement, loan handling, co-hosts and deadlines.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Off-field event contracts that resolve on an official or credibly confirmed fact inside a window: a named player transferring out of a club before a date (KXLAMINEYAMAL, KXCLUBCHANGEMBAPPE: permanent transfers, loans of any duration and contract termination/expiry all count), the player's next club (a multi-outcome set; in KXJOINCLUB/KXJOINLEAGUE/KXMLSJOIN a sign-and-loan counts for the signing club and staying, re-signing or extending resolves the current club's outcome Yes, while in KXJOINRONALDO/KXJOINDAVID still being under contract on the end date resolves a separate 'no change' outcome 'if it exists'), a manager leaving by effective date (KXPOCHETTINOOUT: resolves on the effective date of departure, not announcement), a host country being announced (KXCOPAAMERICAHOST: every announced co-host resolves Yes), or a governing-body sanction stripping a count of titles (KXMANCITYTITLES: 'at least 8', as officially announced before 1 Jan 2028). Further verified families: next permanent manager (KXNEXTMANAGERMANU: interim or caretaker managers do not count unless later appointed permanently), office-holder exit (KXFIFALEAVE: temporary leave or suspension is not leaving; death resolves at the last fair price), team participation (KXWCIRAN 'competes in', KXWCCONGO 'competes in the Intercontinental Playoffs', No if disqualified), tournament format (KXWCTEAMS: a 64-team field confirmed by Source Agencies), match relocation (KXFIFAUSPULLGAME, whose sampled primary text still carries an unfilled '||date||' placeholder; the title says before Jun 11, 2026), and signings that stay Yes even if later voided (KXJOINMESSI).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official club, federation or governing-body announcement (club websites, FIFA/UEFA/CONMEBOL communications), with credible news agencies as source agencies where named; effective dates as stated in the announcement.
variants_and_edge_cases: Sign-and-loan, contract-expiry release and loans of any duration are explicitly handled in the sampled transfer texts (KXJOINCLUB: 'signing club resolves to Yes'; KXLAMINEYAMAL: 'loans out ... for any duration', contract release incl. expiration); a free-agent signing counts like a fee, and a player still at his club on the end date resolves a separate 'no change' outcome (KXJOINRONALDO). Transfers within the same ownership group are not addressed in any sampled text and are CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Governance events (host announcement, sanctions, bans) depend on committee calendars and appeal processes with fat-tailed timing; the stated window can end before a decision, which resolves No by default.

Manager markets resolve on effective dates (KXMANAGERSOUT, KXPOCHETTINOOUT, KXMANAGEROUTDATE with an 11:59:59 pm ET cutoff); next-permanent-manager markets exclude interim and caretaker appointments unless made permanent (KXNEXTMANAGERMANU).

36 of 47 series have rules text; TITLE_ONLY: KXNEXTMANAGERJUV, KXNEXTMANAGERMIL, KXMANCITYSANCTION, KXMANCITYBAN, KXMANAGEROUT, KXJOINMBAPPE, KXJOINSALAH, KXSOCCERINTLRETIRE, KXSOCCERLEAVE, KXUEFAISRAELBAN and KXMLSSKILLS; the Source Agencies list for host and format announcements is not shown.

Participation and format series: KXWCIRAN (competes in the 2026 World Cup), KXWCCONGO (competes in the Intercontinental Playoffs; No on FIFA disqualification), KXWCTEAMS (64-team 2030 field confirmed), KXFIFAUSPULL/KXFIFAUSPULLGAME (US involvement suspended / at least one match relocated); KXSUPERBALLONDOR settles on whether any Super Ballon d'Or is awarded before 2030; KXMLSSKILLS (skills challenge winner) is TITLE_ONLY.

KXMANCITYTITLES reads 'If the English Premier League imposes a sanction stripping at least 8 title(s) across Premier League, FA Cup, or League Cup'; whether a stripping imposed by the FA, EFL, UEFA or CAS rather than the Premier League itself counts is not stated.

KXFIFALEAVE: death in office resolves at the last fair price at the Exchange's discretion; KXSOCCERRETIRE must be retirement from all professional play effective immediately or before the next season; KXJOINMESSI stays Yes if the signing is later voided.

competition_head_to_head.label: Head-to-head competition markets
competition_head_to_head.target: Which of two teams/players finishes ahead on a defined metric.
competition_head_to_head.mechanism: A head-to-head market compares two entities' outcomes in the same competition. Their results are dependent through direct meetings and common uncertainty, so a joint simulation gives P(A ahead of B) rather than comparing marginals. Tie rules and wording decide equality outcomes.

inputs.why: Joint dependence - the channel through which it moves the Head-to-head competition markets price.
Joint simulation - the channel through which it moves the Head-to-head competition markets price.
Shared and independent uncertainty.
Differential fixtures - the channel through which it moves the Head-to-head competition markets price.

Underlying strength for the pair.
Late-season incentives - the channel through which it moves the Head-to-head competition markets price.
The race outcome is a function of the gap relative to what remains, so this is the primary state variable.
Directly sets negative correlation between the two points totals.
Provides the cross-team shock correlation the pairwise comparison is sensitive to.
Prices exact equality of two players' tournament goals or goal contributions. The same joint draws give the two player legs (A>B, B>A) as well as the Tie leg.
Only usable input for the influencer penalty duel.
KXWCTEAMH2H (including its same-stage leg) and KXWCBESTHOST ($1/N dead heat) are functions of the joint stage-reached vector of the compared teams, which group and bracket structure make dependent.

interactions.hypothesis: Direct meetings create negative dependence; common schedule creates positive dependence.
Frequent point ties make the tiebreak rule decisive.
Injuries hurt thin squads more; differential effect determines the pair.

P(leader holds) follows a normal tail in gap divided by sqrt(remaining fixtures times variance per match times (1 - rho)); correlation lowers the denominator, so the same gap gives a higher hold probability when the teams' results are positively correlated.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit hold probability on gap/sqrt(n_left) with and without a correlation term; compare Brier.

interactions.hypothesis: A remaining direct meeting is worth six points of swing; when the gap is at most three points it makes the meeting a decider, when the gap exceeds six it becomes irrelevant, so the effect of the meeting is conditional on the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast outcomes by presence of a remaining meeting and gap bucket (0-3, 4-6, 7+).

interactions.hypothesis: A shared European schedule hurts a thin squad far more than a deep one, so the relative strength shift is proportional to overlap times (1 - depth quality), generating gap changes of of unestimated size in the congested window (a hypothesis, not a measured effect).
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points-per-game change over congested windows on depth and overlap.

interactions.hypothesis: Only on paths with equal final points does goal difference or head-to-head matter, so the tie rule has weight near the zero-point gap and none far from it; the effect is piecewise and depends on the league's order.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate final tables with each tiebreak order and see how often the order changes the 'ahead' label.

interactions.hypothesis: Uncertainty in each team's strength persists over all remaining fixtures (it is not averaged away), so the strength part of the gap sd grows linearly in games remaining while only the match-noise part grows with sqrt (variance quadratic vs linear), especially when one team has a harder schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated gap variance with fixed versus sampled strengths and backtest interval coverage, separating the n^2 strength term from the n match-noise term.

interactions.hypothesis: If both players' teams are likely to exit early, the two tallies concentrate on 0-1 goals and equality is likely; if one team goes deep its player's tally spreads out and equality falls, so the bracket paths drive P(equal) more than the scoring rates.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose simulated P(equal) by the pair of stages reached and compare with an independent-exposure model.

interactions.hypothesis: For KXWCTEAMH2H the two teams' stage outcomes are independent only if their bracket paths cannot cross before the final; when they share a group or bracket half, one's progress removes the other's, shifting mass away from 'same stage' at late rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare same-stage frequencies for pairs in the same vs different bracket halves in simulations and past tournaments.

interactions.hypothesis: Finish-ahead contracts depend on two clubs' rest-of-season points; a club underperforming its rating has a raised dismissal hazard, and a dismissal switches its rating regime for the remaining fixtures, so the pairwise order probability is a mixture over change/no-change paths, mattering most when the two clubs are close and many matches remain.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare finish-order calibration with and without the simulated dismissal branch on seasons with in-season changes among paired clubs.

nonlinearities.shape: Sigmoid in gap divided by sqrt(games left)
nonlinearities.why: Win probability of the race follows a normal-CDF shape: flat when the gap is small relative to the remaining variance and approaching 0 or 1 once the gap exceeds about 2 sd.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance grows quadratically (sd linearly) with horizon through the persistent latent strength term, plus a linear-in-games match-noise variance
nonlinearities.why: With a persistent latent strength the sd of that component is linear in games remaining (variance quadratic) while the match-noise component has sd proportional to sqrt(games); ignoring the persistent term understates tails early in the season.

mechanism_review.summary: A head-to-head season finish is a race between two cumulative points totals. State at the as-of date (points, goal difference, games in hand, deductions) is the starting condition; each team's remaining fixtures generate points through a goal model with its own opponents, venues and rest; the two totals are coupled negatively through direct meetings and positively through shared shocks and common opponents, which sets the variance of the gap. Strength itself is uncertain and drifts with injuries, transfers and congestion. The resolution is the final table, with a tiebreaker branch on equal points and a possible post-hoc deduction. Four mechanisms share the key: s1-s5 cover the table-finish contract (KXEPLH2HFINISH); s6 covers KXEPLH2H, which settles on the two regular-season league meetings (a two-match result model); s7 covers the World Cup stage comparisons (KXWCTEAMH2H, KXWCBESTHOST) through the joint stage-reached distribution of the teams compared; s8 covers the three-way player tally comparisons (KXWCMESSIMBAPPE, KXWCMESSIRONALDO); s9 covers the PrizePicks penalty duel (KXPPPKSO).

stages.name: Current table state and games in hand
stages.description: The starting point is the exact points, goal difference, goals scored and fixtures played for both teams on the as-of date, including postponed matches and deductions. The gap relative to the number of fixtures remaining sets how much variance must be overcome: a 6-point lead with 10 games left is very different from the same lead with 3 left.
stages.distribution: Deterministic state with integer points; drives a discrete race outcome whose variance scales with remaining fixtures.

stages.name: Remaining-fixture points distributions
stages.description: Each team's remaining matches generate points via a calibrated goal model with opponent strength, venue and rest; the two teams face different schedules, so the expected points difference depends on schedule asymmetry, not only on current ratings. Rating uncertainty widens the spread of the points-gap distribution beyond independent match noise.
stages.distribution: Sum of independent three-outcome match lotteries per team (points 0/1/3) plus a shared latent strength uncertainty; approx normal for the gap with sd per match to be estimated (a three-outcome points lottery gives roughly 1.2-1.4 points per match for typical probabilities).

stages.name: Cross-team dependence of outcomes
stages.description: The two teams' results are not independent: direct meetings are zero-sum (a win for one is a loss for the other), common opponents produce correlated results, and shared shocks (same European fixtures, similar injury waves) correlate depth. The correlation of the final points of the two teams sets the variance of their difference, and so the probability the leader holds.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution of two points totals with negative correlation from direct fixtures and positive correlation from shared opponents/shocks; difference variance can be well below the independent sum.

stages.name: Squad shocks over the remaining horizon
stages.description: Over a multi-month horizon injuries, suspensions, transfer windows and manager changes shift one team's strength relative to the other; squad depth determines how much a typical injury wave costs. Competing in cups and Europe adds minutes load and rotation that reduces league-priority quality. A manager change inside the remaining horizon is simulated rather than ignored: each simulated week draws a dismissal from soc.manager_dismissal_hazard given the club's simulated results, and after a change the club's rating is re-blended by soc.transfers (prior weight k/(k+m) over m matches under the new manager); the size of the post-change shift is left to the event study.
stages.distribution: Random strength drift over weeks; heavy right tail for key-player long-term injuries; depth modulates the tail.

stages.name: Tie resolution and settlement
stages.description: A tie on points moves the outcome to the competition's tiebreaker (goal difference, goals scored or head-to-head), so the end-of-season goal-difference gap and direct-match results matter in the narrow set of paths where points are level; deductions and the official final table fix the settlement.
stages.distribution: Discrete tie branch (P(equal points) is an unsourced hypothesis of order 5-10% for evenly matched teams, to be measured from simulated and historical tables) resolved by a continuous goal-difference comparison.

stages.name: Direct-meeting result combinations (KXEPLH2H)
stages.description: For the Results series the event is the pair of outcomes of the two scheduled league meetings between the clubs. Each meeting has its own home/draw/away probabilities from opponent-adjusted attack and defence ratings, the venue of that leg and the draw mass from low-score dependence; the joint outcome (for example one win and one draw for the named club) is the product of the two leg distributions conditional on any leg already played, plus a small positive correlation from shared rating error. Lineups matter close to each leg.
stages.distribution: Discrete 3x3 joint over two match outcomes; each leg roughly 0.25-0.30 draw mass; legs nearly independent given ratings, a played leg collapses one margin.

stages.name: World Cup stage comparison between two named teams or among hosts
stages.description: KXWCTEAMH2H and KXWCBESTHOST compare stages reached: each team's stage distribution comes from the group and bracket simulation, but the comparison needs the joint distribution, because two teams in the same group or bracket half cannot both go deep and may eliminate each other directly. The same-stage outcome is large for weak pairs (both out in the group or round of 32), and the host comparison must keep the $1/N tie mass.
stages.distribution: Joint categorical over seven stages for two or three teams; P(same stage) often 0.25-0.45 for comparable mid-tier nations.

stages.name: Comparison of two players' tournament tallies (more / fewer / exactly equal)
stages.description: For the Messi-Mbappe goals and Messi-Ronaldo goal-contribution series the outcome is which player finishes the 2026 World Cup with the higher tally, with a separate Tie leg for identical tallies. Each tally is the player's per-match scoring (and assist) intensity times his matches played, which depends on availability and his team's progress; P(Tie) is the sum over k of P(A=k)P(B=k) adjusted for dependence and is dominated by low counts and early exits, while the player legs split the remaining mass by relative intensity and expected matches.
stages.distribution: Joint of two overdispersed count pmfs; P(Tie) typically 0.15-0.30, highest when both players have low expected tallies; player legs share the rest.

stages.name: Amateur 1v1 penalty duel (KXPPPKSO)
stages.description: The PrizePicks shootout alternates the two contestants as kicker and keeper over five kicks each on a small 10x6 ft net, then sudden death. The win probability depends on each person's conversion as kicker against the other as keeper; with a small net, keeper reach matters more than in professional shootouts. No historical record exists, so the price rests on weak priors from the contestants' content and is close to a coin flip.
stages.distribution: Two binomial sequences of five kicks with unknown per-kick rates (perhaps 0.5-0.8), then geometric sudden death; outcome near 50/50 under symmetric priors.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted team ratings with posterior uncertainty feed both teams' remaining-fixture points.

opponent_matchup.note: Each team's remaining opponents and the direct meetings set the schedule asymmetry.

role_personnel.note: Key-player dependence and replacement quality decide how injuries move the strength gap.

availability_news.note: Injuries and suspensions to key players across the remaining horizon shift the gap; no timestamps for lineup vintage needed for season-long contracts.

coaching_scheme.note: In-window dismissal hazard and the post-change rating re-blend; the size of the new-manager shift remains an empirical question.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and weather act through single matches and average out over 8-20 remaining fixtures; home advantage is already embedded in the match-level goal model, so no separate environment input is justified for a season-end comparison of two teams.

game_context_script.note: Current gap and games-in-hand define the race state; the remaining-matches count determines variance.

pace_volume.note: Possession and tempo volume affect match goal totals but a head-to-head table finish is decided on points, not on counts, so volume enters only through the team rating that feeds the goal model rather than as a standalone input.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and xG separate luck from skill in the points earned so far, which the rating must regress. For KXPPPKSO the per-kick conversion and save priors of the two contestants are the whole efficiency question.

distribution_variance.note: Joint distribution of the two final points totals (table finish), the joint stage-reached vector (World Cup comparisons) and the joint tally distribution (player comparisons).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Fixture congestion and stakes leverage differ between teams; late-season dead rubbers change effort.

officiating_rules.note: Match-level referee tendencies average out across the many remaining fixtures and have no systematic effect on which of two teams finishes ahead; an official ban or deduction ruling is handled under settlement and tie rules instead.

settlement_contract.note: Tiebreak order, deductions and which table is official.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Seven live series, all with rules text, in four mechanisms. KXEPLH2HFINISH: YES when the named club is placed above the other in the final EPL table after all official tiebreakers, deductions and adjustments. KXEPLH2H: outcome markets on the combined results of the two regular-season league meetings (e.g. 'wins one and draws one'). World Cup stage comparisons: KXWCTEAMH2H has outcomes for each team going further and 'Eliminated same stage' (a semi-final loser stays at Semifinals whatever the third-place result); KXWCBESTHOST pays the furthest-advancing host nation, $1/N if several tie. Player comparisons: KXWCMESSIMBAPPE (goals) and KXWCMESSIRONALDO (goals+assists) are titled 'Will X or Y have more ...'; the sampled leg in each is 'Tie', which pays if the two players' 2026 World Cup tallies are exactly equal ('Only goals scored during the 2026 World Cup are considered'); the player legs (one player strictly more) are implied by the title but their text was not sampled. KXPPPKSO: a PrizePicks 1v1 penalty shootout between two influencers, five kicks each on a non-regulation 10x6 ft net, then sudden death.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Final official EPL table (KXEPLH2HFINISH); official results of the two league meetings (KXEPLH2H); FIFA official stage results and player statistics (World Cup series); the PrizePicks event result (KXPPPKSO).
variants_and_edge_cases: If two teams finish level on points the outcome depends on the competition's tiebreak order (goal difference vs head-to-head vs play-off), so P(ahead) must include a tie-resolution branch whose rule differs by league (the order differs by league and is unsourced here; it must be read from the competition regulations).

A pending points deduction or administrative sanction can reorder the final table after the last match; a head-to-head contract may settle on the official final table at a stated date rather than on-pitch results.

KXEPLH2H settles on the two regular-season league meetings only; once the first meeting is played the contract reduces to one match result, and a meeting postponed beyond the season end is not addressed.
KXWCTEAMH2H stages are Group, R32, R16, QF, SF, lose final, win final; third-place results are ignored, and when the two teams can meet in the bracket their outcomes are directly coupled.

Player comparison series (KXWCMESSIMBAPPE, KXWCMESSIRONALDO) are three-way (X more, Y more, Tie); the Tie leg has large mass at low equal counts (both 0 or both 1), so availability and team exits matter as much as scoring rates. The texts do not name the source for goal or assist attribution.
KXPPPKSO is an influencer exhibition with a non-regulation net and no published performance history; it has no postponement or no-show clause in its text.

Non-standard finish formats (Ecuador LigaPro hexagonal with carried-over points, Peru/Uruguay/Venezuela playoffs, MLS conferences) make "finish ahead" ambiguous between aggregate table, stage table and playoff result; none are verified.

player_award.label: Player awards (voted)
player_award.target: Winner of a named individual award decided by a panel or vote.
player_award.mechanism: Awards combine production statistics, team success and narrative through a voting process. Probability is a ranking function over candidates with joint dependence on team trophies and on availability through the vote date; the awarding body's criteria and timing define which signals matter.

inputs.why: Voting criteria and narrative.
Season production - the channel through which it moves the Player awards (voted) price.
Underlying chance production - the channel through which it moves the Player awards (voted) price.
Counting-stat race - the channel through which it moves the Player awards (voted) price.
Team trophy probabilities - the channel through which it moves the Player awards (voted) price.
Availability - the channel through which it moves the Player awards (voted) price.
Injury risk before vote - the channel through which it moves the Player awards (voted) price.
Stats vs underlying skill - the channel through which it moves the Player awards (voted) price.
Eligibility window and voting body.
Bookmaker award prices - the channel through which it moves the Player awards (voted) price.
Shot volume influences perceived production.
Panel awards are decided by vote shares; narrative and team success set the distribution.
Isolates the dominant coefficient of the voting model and lets the model switch regimes by year.
Provides winner and tie probabilities and the 1/n split payoff that the contract specifies.
The decisive late-moving information for voted awards; absent from the existing list.
Adds the predictability of taste before the target award.
Prices World Cup Ball awards and the Golden Boot + Golden Ball combo.

interactions.hypothesis: Awards are conditional on team trophies so joint simulation is needed.
Voters see goals not xG so luck-inflated stats still win votes.
Late-season injuries remove candidates before the vote date.

A player's vote share multiplies trophy weight by individual narrative: a Champions League winner with the key goal gets disproportionately more votes than the winner's teammate, so team success and individual role multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare an additive-utility softmax with and without a trophy x decisive-contribution product term by likelihood ratio and leave-one-year-out log score; if the product term adds nothing, the effect is additive.

interactions.hypothesis: In tournament years a single international winner can concentrate first-place votes, so the vote-share spread among top candidates is wider and the aggregation noise matters less than in non-tournament years when several club-trophy winners split the vote (hypothesis).
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the margin between first and second by tournament-year status and test whether the fitted softmax temperature differs by regime.

interactions.hypothesis: Before a credible leak the market is in a model-driven regime; after it, probability jumps to near certainty regardless of the model, so the model prior is replaced by the reliability of the source. This is a reliability-weighted Bayesian update, listed as an interaction only in the sense that the update weight depends on the source tier; it is not a separate structural channel.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of price/probability around leak timestamps.

interactions.hypothesis: Precursor award results matter more when the Champions League final has been played and is undecided for the leader, because the leaders are already narrowed; before the final they are weaker evidence.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast predictiveness of precursor awards by timing relative to major final.

interactions.hypothesis: The Golden Ball and the Golden Boot both load on a forward whose team reaches the final, so they co-occur far more often than independence implies; a combo priced as the product of marginals is too low for the favourite and too high for scorers on teams likely to exit early.
interactions.how_to_test: Count historical editions where the Golden Ball winner also topped scoring and compare with the product of marginal frequencies.

nonlinearities.shape: Softmax saturation: vote share concentrated in top two candidates
nonlinearities.why: Utility differences translate to win probability through a softmax, so a gap of one utility unit moves the leader from 50% to 73% while the tail candidates stay near zero.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function at tournament-final result
nonlinearities.why: Winning the Champions League or the World Cup produces a discrete jump in utility rather than a gradual change.

mechanism_review.summary: A voted award is decided by ballots, not by on-pitch counting, so the mechanism is a vote-share model. The candidate pool is narrowed to a few players by team trophies in the eligibility window (the Champions League and tournament results carry the highest weight, with weights varying by year); within a team-success tier, individual output and media narrative separate candidates. Ballots from a finite panel aggregate with noise and possible national bias, so close races are near coin flips and ties can occur and pay 1/n. Credible leaks before the ceremony are the dominant late information, and the contract settles on the official announcement with a no-award clause.

stages.name: Eligibility, season window and candidate pool
stages.description: The award covers a defined season window and the shortlist (30 nominees for the Ballon d'Or) removes most players; the realistic contenders are 3-6 players whose teams won the main trophies in the window. A player's candidacy is determined by season-level team success and visible individual output, not by statistics accumulated before the window opens.
stages.distribution: Small discrete candidate set; probability mass heavily concentrated (top 3 hold 80-90% of the price) with a long tail of outsiders.

stages.name: Team success coupling and tournament weighting
stages.description: Voters are strongly influenced by trophies: a Champions League winner with a decisive final performance or a World Cup/Euros winner takes the lead, and the weight of each trophy varies with the year (international tournament year versus none). The player's share of team success (goals, assists and decisive moments in knockout rounds) converts team outcomes into candidate vote share.
stages.distribution: Conditional-logit style: vote share is a softmax of a utility that is dominated by team trophies; heavy-tailed shifts when a final is won or lost.

stages.name: Individual production and narrative
stages.description: Within a team-success tier, goals and assists, big-match output and the media narrative separate candidates: a 'story' (injury comeback, record-breaking season) adds votes beyond counting stats. Production is measured over the season window, but only part of it is in voters' memory, with more weight on the final months.
stages.distribution: Smooth, right-skewed utility differences; narrative factors are unobserved and partially proxied by media share and previous awards (PFA/UEFA awards).

stages.name: Voter panel aggregation and bias
stages.description: Each voter ranks a top-N list and the points sum determines the winner; with a few dozen to a hundred voters, the margin between top candidates, voter nationality and regional bias (home-country voting), and the scoring scale determine the final ordering and the chance of a tie. Close races (within 5-10 points) are essentially noisy draws.
stages.distribution: Sum of discrete voter ballots; vote-total noise sd of about 3-6 points for 100 voters; ties rare but nonzero.

stages.name: Announcement information and leaks
stages.description: The winner is determined before the ceremony and can leak; pre-ceremony reporting (credible outlets, club statements, attendance of players) updates the probability sharply, and the contract settles on the official announcement. Injuries, minutes and remaining production are live inputs only while the eligibility window is open and become inert once it closes; the pricing horizon of the sibling award series is unknown (pricing_horizon_unknown).
stages.distribution: Jump process: probability moves to near 0/1 on credible news; otherwise slow drift.

stages.name: World Cup awards: selected Balls and the counted Golden Boot
stages.description: World Cup Balls are chosen by FIFA after the final, with heavy weight on players from the finalists and on knockout-round performances, while the Golden Boot is mechanical (by FIFA practice most goals, then assists, then fewest minutes; the combo text itself states no criterion). The combo series needs both to land on one player, which happens mainly when a finalist's forward also tops the scoring, so the joint probability is far above the product of marginals for elite forwards on strong teams and near zero for others. Team progress through the bracket drives both legs.
stages.distribution: Selection: softmax over a handful of finalists' players; Golden Boot: maximum of tournament goal counts with tiebreak; combo is a strongly positively dependent joint event.

talent_strength.note: Candidate quality and team trophy outcomes drive the vote utility.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent matchup in a voted award: candidates are compared by voters across the whole season and not head to head in a match, so matchup variables of the game archetypes have no role here beyond the finals that feed team success.

role_personnel.note: Role (forward/midfielder) shapes how production converts to votes; minutes matter for the season window.

availability_news.note: Before the window closes injuries and expected minutes change remaining contribution chances; after it, leaked announcements matter.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching and tactical scheme enter only through team trophies and a forward's volume, which the team-success input already captures; no voter looks at tactics, so no separate coaching input is warranted for a voted award.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel have no bearing on a ballot cast by journalists after the season; their effect is already inside the underlying season outcomes the voters see, so there is no environmental input for this contract.

game_context_script.note: Final and knockout events weigh more heavily in voters' memory.

pace_volume.note: Volume statistics such as shots or touches are not the voters' criterion beyond the goals and assists they produce; keeping them would give a false sense of precision in a subjective vote.

efficiency_conversion.note: Goal conversion is only a partial signal because voters respond to totals regardless of luck.

distribution_variance.note: Vote-share distribution and aggregation noise determine the tail and ties.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Tournament year, stakes of trophies, and narrative.

officiating_rules.note: Match officials do not affect a vote; rules and eligibility windows of the award are contract matters and are handled under settlement, not as an officiating input.

settlement_contract.note: Co-winner split, no-award clause, season eligibility window.

contract_review.settlement_definition: One binary per candidate. Winner series (KXBALLONDOR men's 2027, KXBALLONDORAWARD women's 2026, KXPFAPOY): YES when the named player wins the named award for the stated season. KXBALLONDORAWARD and KXPFAPOY add that co-winners split $1 by the number of tied recipients unless a separate Tie/Co-Winners market is listed, and that if no award is given every candidate resolves No; the sampled KXBALLONDOR (men's 2027) text has only the one-sentence primary rule, with no tie or no-award clause. Rank series (KXBALLONDORRANK): YES when the player is in the stated top N of the official final ranking, ties resolved by the publisher's method, otherwise all tied share the highest rank and tied contracts pay $1/(number tied) rounded down. Resolution is the awarding body's official announcement. World Cup awards: KXWCAWARD pays the named Golden/Silver/Bronze Ball (or similar) recipient as recognised by FIFA, and if co-winners are announced a separate 'Tie/Co-Winners' market resolves Yes and every individual market No; KXWCAWARDCOMBO pays if the named player wins both the Golden Boot and the Golden Ball; its text states neither the Golden Boot criterion nor any shared-award rule. KXEPLPOY is TITLE_ONLY.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official announcement and published final ranking of the awarding body (France Football/Ballon d'Or organisers, PFA, Premier League, FIFA) as published on its website and at the ceremony.
variants_and_edge_cases: Seven live series: men's and women's Ballon d'Or winner, Ballon d'Or top-N ranking, PFA and EPL player of the year, World Cup awards (single and Golden Boot + Golden Ball combo); six have rules text, KXEPLPOY is TITLE_ONLY.

Rank series settle on the official final ranking: 'Tied rankings shall be resolved using the publisher's official tie-breaking methodology', otherwise tied entities share the highest rank and tied contracts pay $1/(number tied) rounded down, so a candidate near the 10th place cut carries tie risk.

The voting body, number of voters, scoring scale (journalist points scale of believed 15-12-10-8-7-6-5-4-3-1 for the top ten, unverified) and the eligibility window are not in the market text; they determine the joint distribution of vote shares and the tie probability.
Awards revealed by leak before the ceremony change the information state; the contract settles on the official announcement, creating timing risk if different sources publish contradictory winners.

Horizon: KXBALLONDOR (2027 men's award) is listed in November 2026, before the eligibility season ends, so availability and remaining production matter; the finalized KXBALLONDORAWARD market is the post-window case.

Scope: women's award inputs need women's-league data, which is much thinner; PFA is voted by players and restricted to the Premier League season; World Cup Balls follow FIFA's selection (technical study group plus public/media input, composition unverified) and the Golden Boot is a goal count with tiebreaks (stage s6).

Tie handling differs by series: KXBALLONDORAWARD and KXPFAPOY split $1/n among co-winners unless a Tie market exists; KXBALLONDOR states no tie rule; KXBALLONDORRANK splits tied ranks $1/n rounded down; KXWCAWARD resolves a Tie/Co-Winners market and zeros individuals; KXWCAWARDCOMBO has no clause for a shared Golden Boot or Golden Ball.

player_goal_assist_props.label: Soccer player goals, assists, hat tricks and score-or-assist
player_goal_assist_props.target: A named player scores (or assists) at least once, or a count threshold, in a match; regulation per contract rules.
player_goal_assist_props.mechanism: Player scoring is team expected goals times the player's share of chances times minutes, adjusted for penalty duty and opponent defensive weaknesses. Lineup confirmation about an hour before kickoff is the decisive information: the same player's probability changes by multiples if he is dropped or moves position. Over-dispersion and correlation with team goals matter for hat tricks and multi-leg combinations.

inputs.why: Per-90 xG and xA with minutes shrinkage is the base scoring rate.
Share of team shots by role and set-piece duty converts team expected goals into player expected goals.
Confirmed starters and positions about an hour before kickoff decide whether the player plays and where.
Expected minutes and substitution risk scale every count.
Penalty duty adds roughly 0.76 expected goals per penalty awarded, concentrated in one player.
Team and referee penalty-award rates set how often penalty duty matters.
Opponent- and venue-adjusted team xG sets the team's goal expectation.
Opponent's conceded zones match the player's shot zones.
Opposing goalkeeper quality shifts conversion.
Finishing over-performance regresses, so use xG not goals.
Predicted rotation changes starter probability before lineups are published.
Embedded refund rule is peculiar to this contract and changes the correct probability for every non-starter.
Needed because assist props are driven by creators and set-piece takers, not by xG/90.
Provides coherent probabilities for the first-goal and first-goal-win contracts.
Prices the team-first and country-first-in-tournament goalscorer series.

interactions.hypothesis: A penalty taker's goal probability rises when the referee awards penalties at a high rate.
Formation changes redistribute shot share among forwards and wingers.
A positional move changes which conceded zone the player faces.

A substitute's minutes fall mostly in game states where his team is trailing or protecting a lead, so the team lambda during his minutes differs from the full-match lambda; his expected goals are not per-90 rate x minutes x full-match team lambda but a state-conditional minute-weighted rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted versus realised goals for substitutes split by score state at entry and by team rating gap.

interactions.hypothesis: The player's goal chance depends on whether the zones and shot types he occupies (box central, headers) match what the opponent concedes: the same shot share yields more expected goals against a defence that concedes box-central chances than one that concedes wide shots.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit player xG per shot on his zone profile interacted with the opponent concession profile by zone.

interactions.hypothesis: The taker's extra probability exists only if a penalty is awarded (about 0.15 per team per match, 0.3 for both teams combined, higher with referees and teams that win penalties); the effect is a discrete bump, conditional on the taker being on the pitch.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare taker scoring rate in matches with penalties vs without.

interactions.hypothesis: For first goalscorer a substitute's chance is conditional on entering before the first goal, which depends on rotation and the timing of the first goal: if the first goal comes early, subs are excluded, so the fair-price void changes the effective denominators.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(on pitch at first goal) by role and minute distribution of first goals.

interactions.hypothesis: Assist probability scales with team goals and with the set-piece taker's share; in a high-xG match the taker's chance grows roughly linearly while a non-taker's grows more slowly, so team volume interacts with role.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit assists on team xG interacted with set-piece-taker flag.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating 1-exp(-lambda) from team volume to player P(1+)
nonlinearities.why: Player goal probability saturates: a doubling of lambda from 0.3 to 0.6 raises P(1+) from about 0.26 to about 0.45 (a rise of about 0.19) rather than doubling.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in minutes with substitution at 60-70
nonlinearities.why: Expected goals are roughly linear in minutes but entry minute distribution is bimodal (starters vs substitutes), so mean minutes misprices both groups.

nonlinearities.shape: Shrinkage weight rising with shots
nonlinearities.why: Weight on realised finishing grows with the sample of shots, n/(n+k) with k around 100.

mechanism_review.summary: A player goal or assist prop is a thinned, allocated team event. The player must be on the pitch (starter, substitute, or unused, where an unused player settles at fair price); given minutes, his probability is one minus exp(-lambda) with lambda equal to the team's expected goals in this fixture times his share of team chances times conversion, plus penalty duty; assists are the same logic through creation share and the set-piece taker role, bounded by team goals and the teammates' finishing; score-or-assist is a union with within-player dependence. First goalscorer is a competing-risk race for the first goal with a categorical allocation and substitution timing, and the combo adds the dependence between scoring first and winning. Extra time counts, and own-goal and fair-price rules vary by series.

stages.name: Availability and entry into the game
stages.description: Whether the named player starts, enters as a substitute, or does not play at all determines his minutes distribution: starters average 80-90 minutes, substitutes 15-30. Because an active player who never enters settles at fair price, the relevant quantity for that group is the output conditional on playing, weighted by when he enters (an early sub is almost a starter) and by late lineup information on starting status; players outside the matchday squad are a separate case the texts do not state. For club first-goalscorer texts entry after the opener voids to fair price, while World Cup first-goal texts resolve such a substitute on his goals.
stages.distribution: Three-point mixture: starter (about 85 minutes), substitute (about 20 minutes), unused; substitution times right-skewed.

stages.name: Team goal volume in this fixture
stages.description: The player's team has an expected goal total set by its opponent-adjusted attack against this opponent's defence and keeper; a player's chance is a share of that, so the same striker has a 55% scoring chance in a 3.0-xG home game and 25% in a 0.9-xG away game. Tempo and game state influence the team's volume.
stages.distribution: Team goals as an overdispersed count; the player's count conditional on team count is binomial-like with allocation by share.

stages.name: Player's share and conversion
stages.description: Share of team shots and chances, shot quality (location, header vs foot), finishing relative to xG and role in set pieces and penalties determine the player's goal rate per 90; penalty duty adds roughly 0.1 goals per match for the taker (about 0.15 team penalties per match x about 0.78 conversion; about 0.3 penalties per match is the two-team total), and set-piece aerial threats add a lumpy component. Finishing must be regressed.
stages.distribution: Per-90 rate with heavy shrinkage (finishing persistence about 20-30%); zero-heavy count (P(0)>55% for forwards).

stages.name: Assist and chance-creation structure
stages.description: Assists depend on the player's creation (key passes, crosses, set-piece delivery) and on the finishing of the teammates who receive the chances; the set-piece taker (corners and free kicks) holds a disproportionate share of assists; an assist requires a goal to be scored, so assist probability is bounded by team goals and the player's share of creation.
stages.distribution: Compound process: team goals times player's share of assist credit; assists are rarer than goals (about 0.08 per 90 for creators), with large provider-definition noise.

stages.name: First-goal race and combo structure
stages.description: First goalscorer is a joint event: the team scores first (a competing-risk race), the scorer is the specific player (a share of first-goal routes weighted toward set pieces and penalties early), and for substitutes he must be on the pitch. The combo 'scores first and team wins' adds the positive dependence between scoring first and winning (the first scorer wins roughly 70% of the time and win-or-draw is nearer 85-90%; both are unsourced hypotheses, and in the combo the win includes any officially recognised tiebreak).
stages.distribution: Competing-risk race then categorical allocation; P(no goal) about 8%; conditional dependence between first goal and result.

stages.name: Settlement mapping
stages.description: Settlement maps official event logs to each player-level contract with specific DNP/fair-price, extra-time and own-goal rules; labelling errors arise from treating a fair-price settlement as a loss and from using different first-goal definitions in the combo and the team-level market.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from event feed; ambiguity in provider definitions.

stages.name: Team-conditional and tournament-span first scorer
stages.description: Two variants change the first-goal race: the first goal for a named team in a match is a race only among that team's players, so it equals the player's share of his team's expected goals adjusted for entry time and penalty duty, plus the team's no-goal probability; the first goal for a country over the whole World Cup chains this race across matches until the country first scores, so exposure is the number of matches until the first goal, which depends on group opponents and the team's goal rate.
stages.distribution: Within-team multinomial over players with a no-goal leg; for the tournament version a geometric-like number of matches until the first goal, mixed over lineups per match.

talent_strength.note: Team strength and player-level scoring talent.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent's chances conceded by zone and position, keeper quality.

role_personnel.note: Role in chance creation, set pieces and penalties.

availability_news.note: Starting status and entry; confirmed lineups about an hour before kickoff.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach substitution timing and rotation habits.

environment.note: Weather and venue change team goal rates by a few percent, which the team lambda already carries; no player-specific environmental input has evidence, so none is added for goal/assist props.

game_context_script.note: Competing-risk race for the first goal and its link to the result.

pace_volume.note: Shots and touches in the box per 90.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing over/under-performance regressed to the player's baseline.

distribution_variance.note: Zero-heavy count and union events (goal or assist).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Dead-rubber, congestion and cup-priority effects on whether a star plays 90 minutes or is substituted early depend on stakes, but no pregame stakes input is attached to this archetype and the effect on a player's minutes is only partly in rotation_index.

officiating_rules.note: Referee penalty tendency determines penalty opportunities for the taker.

settlement_contract.note: Fair-price DNP rule, extra-time inclusion, first-goal definitions.
