contract_review.settlement_definition: Per-player binaries over the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods): 'Goalscorer' = records at least 1 goal (floor 0.5, greater), 'Assists' = at least 1 assist, 'Score or Assist' = a goal or an assist, 'First Goalscorer' = the player records the first goal (plus a 'No Goal' outcome), and the 'First Goal Win' combo = the named player scores the first non-own goal AND his team wins (including any officially recognized tiebreaking procedure). If a player is active but never enters the game (the wording says only 'active'; the outcome for a player who is injured, rested or not in the matchday squad is not stated) the market settles to the (last) fair market price before game start rather than to No; once a player enters, settlement is on his goals/assists. For the club and Nations League first-goalscorer texts, a first goal scored before the player enters as a substitute also settles to fair price; KXWCFIRSTGOAL and KXWCTEAMFIRSTGOAL have no such clause ('Once a player enters the game, the market settles based on the player's goals scored'), so a substitute entering after the opener resolves on his goals. World Cup and Super Cup variants add: N+ goal rungs (KXUEFASCGOAL 'at least 2 goals'); first goalscorer where an own-goal opener passes to 'the next non-own-goal scored' (KXWCFIRSTGOAL); the first goal for a named team in the match (KXWCTEAMFIRSTGOAL, own goals skipped likewise); and the first goalscorer for a country over the whole 2026 World Cup (KXWCTEAM1STGOAL), which spans several matches, excludes own goals and shootouts and has a 'No Goalscorer' leg; its text is cut at 'All players who do not score the first qualifying goal will r', so the non-scorer outcome (presumably No) is not fully visible.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official match data feed event log (goals with scorer, assists, substitutions) from the provider used by Kalshi (not named in the texts); own goals are skipped to the next non-own goal in KXINTLFRIENDLYFGW, KXWCFIRSTGOAL, KXWCTEAMFIRSTGOAL and KXWCTEAM1STGOAL, while the club first-goal texts are cut before any own-goal clause.
variants_and_edge_cases: DNP/bench rule: unlike many sports props, a player who never enters settles to fair price (stated 'before game start' vs 'last fair market price before game start' in different series), so the market contains an embedded refund and pre-game liquidity matters; once a player enters for one minute the contract resolves on his actual output.

First goalscorer: the 'No Goal' outcome resolves YES when no player scores; KXWCFIRSTGOAL and KXWCTEAMFIRSTGOAL skip own goals to the next non-own goal, while the EPL first-goal text is cut before its own-goal clause; KXINTLFRIENDLYFGW also uses the first non-own goal.

Assist attribution depends on the data provider (Opta-style definitions: the final pass leading directly to a goal, counting deflected passes in some cases; set-piece assists and penalty-won are not assists); own goals have no assist; this determines assists and score-or-assist labels.

Strikes are N+ for count thresholds (floor 0.5 means at least one) with also 2+ goals/hat-trick style rungs possible; extra time is included, so cup matches add exposure; abandonment mid-match with goals scored is not described.

33 live series, all with rules text; 8 World Cup and UEFA Super Cup series were re-filed here, including the tournament-span KXWCTEAM1STGOAL, which is not a single-match prop (its non-scorer clause is cut off in the sampled text). The World Cup first-goal texts lack the club texts' substitute-after-opener fair-price clause.

player_shots_saves_props.label: Soccer player shots, shots on target and goalkeeper saves
player_shots_saves_props.target: A player's shot or shot-on-target count, or a goalkeeper's saves, relative to a threshold.
player_shots_saves_props.mechanism: Shot counts are team shot volume times the player's share times minutes, shaped by game state (trailing teams shoot more) and the opponent's block and press profile. Goalkeeper saves are the opponent's shots on target times the keeper's save probability, which is noisy and must be shrunk. Both are over-dispersed counts and depend on the confirmed lineup.

inputs.why: Team shots and SOT for and against set the volume to be shared.
Player share by role converts team volume to player volume.
Confirmed lineup fixes who plays and in which role.
Expected minutes and substitution risk scale every shot and save count.
Expected SOT faced is the keeper-saves volume.
Keeper quality (PSxG minus goals allowed) shrunk toward average.
Pressing and tempo change shot volume.
Trailing teams shoot more; leading teams concede more shots.
Opponent block and zone profile changes shot conversion to SOT.
Formation changes who takes shots.
Allows a pregame forecast that reflects the favourite or underdog role of the player's team.

Extends soc.keeper_workload (whose catalog measurement already multiplies expected SOT by a shrunk PSxG-based save probability): it adds only the goals-conceded subtraction and a compound-count variance, and is not independent of it.
Label consistency is a prerequisite for calibration given no rules text exists.

interactions.hypothesis: Shot volume is convex in expected deficit: heavy underdogs concede many shots while taking few, changing both player and keeper counts.
Keeper saves depend on volume times shrunk skill; volume dominates unless skill is extreme.
A teammate's absence raises shot share in a position-specific way.

A striker's expected shots are team volume times share times a state multiplier; an underdog's striker has a lower base volume but a large trailing-state boost, and the three factors multiply, so the expected count is not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit player shots with interaction of team win probability and role in a Poisson regression.

interactions.hypothesis: At fixed conversion saves are monotone increasing in shots on target faced; a non-monotone pattern across opponents arises only if shot quality (and so conversion) rises with opponent attack faster than SOT volume, which is a hypothesis; opponent zone concession shifts both volume and quality at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare saves against SOT and PSxG deciles, then split by opponent zone-concession profile to see whether quality outruns volume.

interactions.hypothesis: A substitute or early-substituted striker accumulates his minutes mostly in trailing or protecting states, so his shot rate during those minutes is the state-specific rate, not the full-match average; the product of minutes and state multiplier differs from minutes x average rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised shots for substitutes and early-hooked starters with a model using full-match rate versus a state-weighted rate by score state at entry.

interactions.hypothesis: A winger's shots depend on the opposing full-back and the system: against a back five the wide player takes fewer shots and more crosses, so the matchup effect is conditional on the opponent's formation.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact shot rate with opposing formation indicator by position.

nonlinearities.shape: Non-monotone in opponent shot quality
nonlinearities.why: Saves are SOT minus goals: at fixed conversion they are monotone in SOT, and they decline in opponent quality only if conversion rises faster than SOT volume (hypothesis to test), so the shape is not asserted to be non-monotone.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in the goal deficit
nonlinearities.why: Trailing by one lifts shots by an amount to be estimated (20-30% is a placeholder) but trailing by three adds little since players shoot from low-quality positions with fatigue.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in entry minute for substitutes
nonlinearities.why: Shot count is near-linear in minutes for starters but a substitute entering after 75 minutes has a sharply smaller expected count.

mechanism_review.summary: HYPOTHETICAL TEMPLATE (no live series, no rules text; nothing here is evidence that Kalshi lists shots or saves props). A player shot count thins the team's shot volume: minutes on the pitch (starter, early substitution), the team's expected shots against this defence, the player's share by role and set-piece duty, and a score-state multiplier since trailing teams shoot more. Shots on target add an accuracy layer. A goalkeeper's saves are a difference: opponent shots on target minus goals conceded, so the count depends on opponent SOT volume, shot quality and the actual goals, and it is non-monotone in opponent quality. Definitions of shots and saves depend on the data provider, and no live series exists to fix settlement.

stages.name: Playing time and role
stages.description: A shot count scales with minutes on the pitch and with the player's role: central forwards and wide attackers take 2-4 shots per 90 while defenders take under one; starting status, expected minutes and whether the player is subbed off in a game that is decided shift the count; for a goalkeeper the role is binary (starter or not), which makes minutes almost deterministic.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated by non-participation; for outfield players minutes distribution right-skewed; keeper minutes nearly constant at 90.

stages.name: Team shot volume in the fixture
stages.description: The team's total shots in this match come from its opponent-adjusted attacking volume, tempo and game plan against this defence; strong teams against low blocks produce 18+ shots, while counter-attacking teams produce fewer but better ones; the player's expected shots are the team volume times his share of shots, and shots on target multiplies by accuracy.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial team counts with mean and sd to be estimated per league (12 and 4 are illustrative placeholders); player counts thin the team count with a binomial-like allocation, giving heavy overdispersion.

stages.name: Game-state response of shot volume
stages.description: The trailing team shoots more and from lower-quality positions, while the leader's volume declines; in blowouts the winner's volume often falls late while the loser's rises. So the player's shot count depends on whether his team leads, and the keeper's saves depend on the trailing opponent's late volume, making the final count a function of the match's score path.
stages.distribution: Time-varying intensity with state multipliers of placeholders of +20% to +40% to be estimated for the trailer; joint distribution of goals and shots (negative correlation within team).

stages.name: Shot conversion to on-target and to goals (keeper side)
stages.description: Shots on target depend on shot quality and the shooter's accuracy; a keeper's saves are SOT faced minus goals conceded, so strong shot quality (high PSxG) turns SOT into goals rather than saves, and the keeper's own shot-stopping quality shifts saves by a few tenths per match. Penalties add a rare high-conversion event.
stages.distribution: Binomial thinning of shots into on-target (illustrative 33%) and then into goals (illustrative 30% of SOT); saves mean and sd to be estimated (about 3 and 1.7 are illustrative).

stages.name: Formation, personnel matchups and settlement definitions
stages.description: Which opposing defenders and tactical system face the shooter (central or wide, high line or deep block) affects his shot opportunities; the settlement counts depend on the provider's definitions of shots, blocked shots and saves, on extra time inclusion and on the participation rule.
stages.distribution: Matchup multipliers about 0.8-1.25; definition ambiguity is a deterministic offset (blocked shots count or not).

contract_review.settlement_definition: HYPOTHETICAL TEMPLATE, NOT A LISTED CONTRACT: No live Kalshi series maps to this archetype in the ledger, so there is no contract text to read. The catalog target is a player's shot or shot-on-target count, or a goalkeeper's saves, relative to an N+ threshold over a match. Settlement details (which shots count, whether blocked shots and headers are included, whether penalties count in shots and saves, regulation-only versus entire game with extra time, the DNP/substitute rule, the data provider's definitions) cannot be stated and are recorded as unresolved rather than inferred from the neighbouring goal/assist props, whose texts do say 'entire game' with fair-price DNP settlement.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not verified; presumably an official data-feed event log (shots, shots on target, saves per player) from the league's data provider used by Kalshi.
variants_and_edge_cases: Shot definition: provider counts differ on blocked shots (an Opta 'shot' includes blocked, a 'shot on target' excludes them), on headers and on penalties; a shots threshold of 3+ for a striker is a different event under each, so the data provider must be identified before any calibration.

Goalkeeper saves count only shots on target that did not become goals, so saves = shots on target faced minus goals conceded (and own-goal and penalty details), making the contract a function of the opponent's SOT volume and of the goals actually conceded; a 4-0 loss can still have 4 saves while a 1-0 win can have 6.

DNP/substitute handling, extra time inclusion and abandoned matches are unknown; if the family follows neighbouring goal/assist props it would be entire-game with fair-price settlement for non-participants, but that is an assumption.
The catalog lists both players and keepers in one archetype although their drivers differ (player share of team shots versus opponent volume), so any live series would probably need separate keys.

corners_and_cards_team_events.label: Soccer corners, cards and fouls
corners_and_cards_team_events.target: Count of corners, cards or fouls in a match relative to a threshold.
corners_and_cards_team_events.mechanism: Corners follow territorial pressure, wing play and blocked shots; cards and fouls follow referee tendencies, derby intensity, tackle volume and score state. Both are over-dispersed counts that correlate with possession and game state. The referee appointment is announced days ahead and is the single most informative card input.

inputs.why: Team corners for and against per 90, opponent-adjusted, are the base rate.
Team and player foul and card rates are the base of card markets.
Referee card and penalty tendencies are the largest known card driver and are published in advance.
Pressing intensity creates fouls and turnovers.
Wide formations generate corners and crosses.
Derbies raise fouls and cards.
High-stakes matches raise cards.
Trailing teams earn corners; late leads add time-wasting cards.
Set-piece attack versus defence shifts corner-to-goal conversion.
VAR reviews add stoppage and cards.
Added time lengthens the window for corners and cards.
Moves from historic corner counts to a causal expectation based on how attacks end.
Provides the dynamic structure behind team-corner thresholds that static team averages cannot.
Captures matchup in how teams attack, which total corner counts depend on.
Settlement-definition input needed to label training data consistently.

interactions.hypothesis: A card-happy referee in a derby compounds the baseline.
Corners cluster in the trailing team's spell, so the mean is conditional on the expected score path.
High-press teams commit tactical fouls that referees punish unevenly.

A favourite's team corners depend on whether it scores early: an early goal drops its expected count while the underdog's rises, so the favourite's team-corner threshold has a negative interaction with goal timing; the match total changes less.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare favourite corner counts split by whether it scored before minute 30.

interactions.hypothesis: A wide-attacking team facing a low block that clears crosses over the byline yields a multiplicative boost to corners: width volume times opponent concession rate, not their sum.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit corners on product of attack width and opponent concession index.

interactions.hypothesis: Corners per attack saturate at very high possession against deep blocks because shot quality, not volume, becomes the limit, but total corners still rise with territorial dominance as s1 states; the saturation concerns the marginal corner per extra attack and is a hypothesis, not a decline in counts.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot corners vs shots volume by possession decile.

interactions.hypothesis: Late stoppage minutes are played in a score state that is already imbalanced, so added time multiplies the trailing side's elevated corner rate: a long second-half added time in a one-goal game adds more expected corners than the same minutes in a level game.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare corners per minute in the 90+ period by score margin and fit an added-minutes x margin term.

nonlinearities.shape: Negative-binomial overdispersion; variance excess over Poisson to be estimated (1.2-1.4 times the mean is a placeholder)
nonlinearities.why: Counts are overdispersed by game-state heterogeneity, so Poisson-based rung probabilities are too narrow at both tails.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by margin: +1 goal raises trailer, saturates beyond 2
nonlinearities.why: Corner multipliers grow when trailing by one and saturate at two goals as the trailing team gives up or the leader parks.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in cross volume
nonlinearities.why: More crosses add corners at a decreasing rate as defensive clearances become less likely to go over the byline.

mechanism_review.summary: A corner-count contract counts corner kicks taken over the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time). Corners are a by-product of attacks that end blocked, deflected or parried: team expected corners scale with attacking volume and the share of attacks ending in blocked shots and crosses, and the opponent's defensive style (low block, clearance direction) multiplies it. Game state redistributes corners between the teams: the trailing side gains late, the leader concedes, so the favourite's team count depends on whether it scores early. Exposure (added time, VAR, extra time) and the 'taken versus awarded' definition adjust the count. Cards and fouls have no live contract in the ledger.

stages.name: Attacking pressure and territory
stages.description: Corners are generated when the attacking team's shots, crosses and passes are blocked or deflected over the byline, so each team's expected corners scale with its volume of attacks in the final third and the share of attacks that end in blocked shots; territorially dominant teams against deep blocks generate the highest counts, while transitional teams generate few.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative binomial) with mean about 5 per team; dispersion from variation in how attacks end.

stages.name: Opponent defending style
stages.description: A low block that blocks shots and crosses concedes many corners, a high line concedes few corners but more shots; the relevant measure is corners conceded per attack (block rate and clearance direction), not shots conceded; defenders' clearing habits and goalkeeper behaviour (tipping over the bar) are part of this.
stages.distribution: Team-level rate multiplier with sd across teams to be estimated (15% is a placeholder); interacts multiplicatively with the attacker's volume.

stages.name: Game state redistributes corners
stages.description: The trailing team pushes forward in the second half and wins more corners, while the leader defends deep and concedes them; late-game state raises the trailer's corners after the 60th minute by an amount to be estimated (30-40% is an unsourced placeholder). So the favourite's team corners are high only if it dominates without scoring early; an early lead lowers the favourite's count.
stages.distribution: Time-inhomogeneous intensity with score-state multipliers; negative association between early goals and the leader's subsequent corners.

stages.name: Match exposure: stoppage, VAR and extra time
stages.description: Exposure minutes (45+ each half, VAR delays, 30 minutes of ET in cups) scale the count; referees' added-time habits differ; a red card changes both teams' corner rates; and taken versus awarded definition removes a few percent of awarded corners. For World Cup knockout games and UCL knockout second legs the extra-time branch (probability of a draw at 90 times about 30 extra minutes of corner rate, often elevated by fatigue and chasing) is part of the count.
stages.distribution: Exposure is a small discrete variable; extra time adds corners when played (2-3 and 30% of knockout ties are unsourced placeholders).

stages.name: Rivalry, stakes and settlement
stages.description: High-stakes or derby matches increase tempo and aggression; settlement requires the count taken in the entire game from the match feed and mapping of N+ rungs; ladder consistency across rungs is a constraint.
stages.distribution: Mild shifts in mean (derby shift of unmeasured size); deterministic settlement.

contract_review.settlement_definition: All ten live series are corner counts: combined ('France and England combined record at least 9+ corners') or single-team ('France records at least 8+ corners') N+ thresholds (floor_strike N, greater_or_equal) over the entire game including regulation, stoppage and any extra time. The EPL and La Liga texts count only corner kicks actually taken; the UCL, World Cup and UEFA Super Cup texts do not mention it. World Cup corner series resolve to a fair price if the game is cancelled or rescheduled more than two weeks away; the club texts carry no postponement clause. No card or foul series is listed.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Match data provider's corner-kick events (Opta-style events as used by Kalshi's sports data feed), counting corners taken in the entire game; the exact provider is not stated in the sampled text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Threshold construction: 'N+' with floor_strike N (greater_or_equal, e.g. 9+ total, 6+ team), a nested ladder of integer rungs; counts are discrete with mean about 10 total (sd 3-3.5) so adjacent rungs differ by 6-9 percentage points.

Extra time is included in every corner text. World Cup knockout games (KXWCCORNERS, KXWCTCORNERS) and UCL knockout second legs can go to 30 minutes of extra time after a draw, adding corner exposure; the UEFA Super Cup (KXUEFASCCORNERS, KXUEFASCTCORNERS) has, under UEFA regulations since 2023, gone straight to penalties after a 90-minute draw, so the text's extra-time inclusion is normally inert there (to be confirmed against the current regulations).
'Actually taken' language appears in the EPL and La Liga texts but not in the UCL, World Cup or UEFA Super Cup texts, so awarded-but-not-taken corners may be treated differently by series.
Cards and fouls have no live series here (the catalog's cards inputs have no contract to be verified against); referee-dependent card contracts, if listed, would need their own rules.

EPL and La Liga series (four) can never reach extra time; UCL series cover league-phase games (no extra time) and later knockout second legs (extra time possible); World Cup knockout games can reach extra time; the Super Cup normally cannot. Exposure must be conditioned on the game's format and P(draw at 90) where extra time exists.

tournament_aggregate_event_props.label: Tournament aggregate and match-event count props
contract_types: World Cup Every Team to Score a Goal
World Cup Matches to go to Penalties
Goalie Penalty Goal in World Cup
World Cup Group Winners to be Eliminated in Round of 32
World Cup Winner to Trail in a Match
World Cup Goal in Every Game
tournament_aggregate_event_props.target: A count, sum or extreme of goals or match events aggregated across many matches in a tournament, relative to a strike or condition.
tournament_aggregate_event_props.mechanism: Twenty-two settled 2026 World Cup series, each a different statistic of the same 104 matches (72 group, 32 knockout incl. third place): a tournament goal sum; named-team goal ladders over the group stage or the full run (3 to 8 matches); extremes across teams or groups with $1/N dead heats; per-round shootout counts and the longest shootout in rounds; the highest-scoring knockout match and the fastest goal; group-table patterns and group winners lost in the Round of 32; a cross-match race to concede first by ET timestamp; whether the champion ever trails; and player or rare-event aggregates (hat tricks, club goal pools, a player scoring in every knockout round, direct free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals). Outcomes come from team strengths against the actual draw and simulated bracket, the international goal environment, shootout kick dynamics, player shares of team goals, and contract scope flags.

inputs.why: Per-team scored/conceded rates against the drawn opponents and the simulated knockout path settle the named-team ladders, Goals Allowed and the most/fewest extremes.
Group plus 32-team bracket simulation supplies matches played per team, champion identity and knockout pairings used by most series.
International attack/defence strength is the base of every match rate and of champion and pairing probabilities.
Goals per match level times 104 matches sets the Total Goals strike (308+ needs about 2.96 per match).
Shared tournament effects widen the totals distribution beyond independent matches.
Match-level goal count distribution is the building block for sums and maxima of match totals.
Tail of single-match totals drives the knockout Highest Scoring Game strike.
Mismatch mix of fixtures moves group goal totals, blanks, hat tricks and high-scoring games.
Per-round shootout counts (exactly N / N+ in R32, R16, QF) and group winners lost in the R32 come from round-level bracket simulation.
Per-tie probability of level after 120 minutes feeds every shootout-count series.
Knockout goal-rate and draw-rate multiplier changes shootout counts and the KO highest-score maximum.
Round count of each shootout settles Longest Penalty Shootout and when goalkeepers kick.
Team shootout skill slightly shifts shootout length and goalkeeper-kicker exposure.
Opening-goal timing per match sets the Fastest Goal minimum and early concession hazards.
Kickoff ET timestamps plus per-minute concession hazards settle the four-team Concede First race.
P(champion never trails) needs champion identity times conditional trailing along its path.
Recovery after conceding feeds the champion-never-trails calculation.
Excess blank rates of the weakest attacks dominate Every Team to Score.
Joint W/D/L patterns inside a group settle Group Points (all four teams on 4 points).
Draw frequency in balanced group fixtures is required for the all-on-4-points pattern.
Player-level goal distributions settle Hat Trick count, Club Goals maximum and Goal in Every Game.
Per-match base rates for direct free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals settle the rare-event series.
Player npxG/90 and shot share drive hat-trick and every-round scorer probabilities.
Expected minutes of key forwards cap team and player goal ladders.
Star-forward absence moves named-team goal ladders and player-pool aggregates.
Designated free-kick and corner takers drive direct free-kick and olimpico rates.
Qualification state before matchday 3 drives rotation and attacking intent in named-team ladders.
Dead-rubber versus must-score leverage moves weak teams' blank probabilities in round three.
Longer added time raises goals per match for Total Goals and team ladders.
Penalty award rate adds goals and feeds goal-environment estimates.
VAR penalties and disallowed goals shift the per-match goal level.
Heat and Mexico City/Guadalajara altitude act on a subset of venues and raise or lower rates.
Per-series flags: group vs full tournament, ET in or out, shootouts out, own-goal attribution, third-place game in.
Exact wording per series fixes strike construction (N+, exactly N, $1/N dead heats) and scope.

interactions.hypothesis: A full-tournament team ladder is a random sum: goals per match times a random number of matches, so advancement depth and attack strength compound and the upper rungs are convex in strength.
A shared tournament effect shifts every match together, so Total Goals has fatter tails than an independent sum of 104 matches.
The longest shootout is a maximum over a random number of shootouts, so per-round shootout counts and sudden-death continuation must be simulated jointly.
Never-trailing is evaluated on the eventual champion only, so it mixes over champion identity and conditioning on winning lowers trailing rates.

The chance of a very high-scoring match rises convexly with the strength gap, so a knockout bracket that keeps a few heavy mismatches in the R32 lifts the KO Highest Scoring Game rungs more than the same average gap spread evenly.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the KO maximum from real simulated pairings versus pairings with equal mean gap but compressed spread.

interactions.hypothesis: A tournament-level random effect makes Total Goals a mixture, so the 104-match sum has fatter upper and lower tails than independent matches; rungs far from the mean such as 308+ are most affected.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate tournament random-effect variance across World Cups and continental finals and compare 308+ probability with and without it.

interactions.hypothesis: The longest shootout exists only if at least one tie reaches penalties and long ones need sudden death; with about four or five shootouts per tournament the maximum and the chance a goalkeeper kicks are driven jointly by count and length.
interactions.how_to_test: Joint simulation of shootout counts per round and lengths versus a model using a fixed average count.

interactions.hypothesis: A full-tournament team ladder equals goals per match times matches played; stronger teams score more per match and play more matches, so high rungs (e.g. 22+ for France) respond multiplicatively to strength while group-stage ladders do not.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare full-tournament team-goal distributions from the joint simulation with a fixed-match-count approximation for favourites versus minnows.

interactions.hypothesis: Champions that trail must come back, so conditioning on the title selects paths with few or recovered deficits; the never-trailed probability is far above the product of unconditional per-match trailing rates for a favourite.
interactions.how_to_test: On World Cups 1986-2022 compare champions' never-trailed frequency with the unconditional per-match never-trailed rate of the same teams.

interactions.hypothesis: In the Concede First race, a team whose first match ends before another team kicks off wins outright if it concedes at all, so the race is a threshold on kickoff order: earlier calendar position dominates defensive strength unless the early team keeps a clean sheet.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate with real kickoff timestamps versus all four teams kicking off simultaneously and compare the race probabilities.

interactions.hypothesis: A weak team still without a goal entering matchday 3 with qualification hope chases harder; one already eliminated may not, so the Every Team to Score conjunction is sensitive to round-three incentives of the few binding teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare blank rates in matchday-3 World Cup group matches by stakes bucket against matchdays 1-2.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear mean effect on the sum but convex effect on far tail rungs
nonlinearities.why: Total Goals moves linearly with the per-match level, but the probability of clearing a high rung such as 308+ changes much faster than the mean because it sits in the tail of a mixture.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at five or fewer rounds, then geometric decay with ratio p^2+(1-p)^2
nonlinearities.why: With kick conversion p about 0.70 each sudden-death round continues with probability about 0.58, so P(9+ rounds) per shootout is near 0.05 and the longest-shootout ladder falls steeply.

nonlinearities.shape: Product over 48 teams dominated by the weakest few
nonlinearities.why: Every Team to Score is a product of per-team scoring probabilities over three group matches, so one or two weak attacks with excess zero rates set most of the probability.

nonlinearities.shape: Minimum over 104 matches: fastest-goal rungs saturate near certainty for late minutes
nonlinearities.why: With about 100 matches, even a modest per-match chance of a goal by minute 8 makes the 8th-minute rung likely and earlier rungs drop sharply, so the response is concave in the hazard.

mechanism_review.summary: All 22 series are statistics of the same 104 matches but read different parts of them. Sums: Total Goals adds every match incl. ET; named-team ladders add one team's matches over the group stage (three games, no ET) or the full run (three to eight games incl. ET), so attack strength against the actual drawn opponents and advancement depth dominate. Extremes: the most goals allowed by a team, the fewest goals by a group, the highest-scoring knockout match, the fastest goal, the longest shootout and the biggest club goal pool are maxima or minima whose probabilities depend on tails and on how many candidates compete. Counts: shootouts per knockout round, group winners lost in the R32, hat tricks and rare goal types. Patterns and paths: a cyclic 4-4-4-4 group table, a four-team race to concede by wall-clock time, and the champion never trailing. A shared tournament factor correlates matches, and per-series scope flags (ET, shootouts, own-goal direction, $1/N dead heats) change the random variable.

stages.name: Tournament goal level for the all-team total
stages.description: Total Goals sums 104 match totals including extra time and own goals. World Cup goals per match ran about 2.6 to 2.7 through 2022 and the 48-team field adds weaker teams, while the long-added-time directive adds minutes. The 308+ sampled rung needs about 2.96 per match, so the level, its shared tournament shock and directive effects decide the series rather than any one team.
stages.distribution: Sum of overdispersed match counts plus a tournament random effect; approximately normal in the middle with fatter tails than an independent sum.

stages.name: Named-team and per-group goal sums and their extremes
stages.description: Team Goals (group stage) and Tournament Goals (full run incl. ET) are one country's goals against its three drawn opponents plus any knockout opponents; Goals Allowed asks for a group-stage clean sheet with own goals charged to the erring team; Group Stage Goals takes the team conceding the most and the group scoring the fewest, both paying $1/N on ties; Every Team to Score is a conjunction effectively decided by the weakest attacks' three group games. Star availability and matchday-3 rotation move the sums.
stages.distribution: Per-team sums are compound Poisson-gamma counts over a random number of matches (3-8); extremes across 48 teams or 12 groups are discrete order statistics with frequent ties.

stages.name: Knockout rounds: shootout counts, upsets and shootout length
stages.description: Matches to go to Penalties counts ties level after 120 minutes within a named round (16, 8 or 4 ties), at roughly a quarter of World Cup knockout ties historically and higher for balanced pairings; Group Winners Eliminated counts group winners losing R32 ties against runners-up or third-placed teams; Longest Penalty Shootout is the maximum round count across all shootouts; Goalie Penalty Goal needs a goalkeeper to kick, usually only after ten outfield kickers in sudden death.
stages.distribution: Per-round counts are sums of dependent Bernoullis with pairing-specific probabilities; shootout length is five rounds or fewer with about 27% reaching sudden death and then a geometric tail with ratio near 0.58.

stages.name: Single-match extremes: highest knockout score and fastest goal
stages.description: Highest Scoring Game (sampled 26KO event) is the maximum total over 32 knockout matches including extra time, shootout kicks excluded and own goals counted, so it depends on mismatched KO pairings, cagey knockout play and ET goals added to level ties. Fastest Goal is the minimum over 104 matches of the first-goal official minute; with roughly 100 matches an 8th-minute-or-earlier goal is likely, so the opening-period hazard drives it.
stages.distribution: Maximum of discrete match totals (extreme of a Poisson mixture) and minimum of censored first-goal times; both are steep functions of the per-match tail.

stages.name: Cross-match race and champion path properties
stages.description: Concede First is the earliest ET timestamp at which Mexico, Spain, Argentina or Ghana concede, so the kickoff calendar (Mexico played the opening match) and each team's concession hazard against its specific opponents decide it, with $1/N if none concede. Winner to Trail follows the eventual champion across seven or eight matches: probability is a mixture over champion identity of never being behind, and conditioning on winning reduces trailing.
stages.distribution: Race outcome is a categorical over four teams dominated by schedule order; never-trailing is a path Bernoulli whose mixture is concentrated on a few favourites.

stages.name: Group-table patterns
stages.description: Group Points pays if any of the twelve groups ends with every team on four points, which needs each team to win one, draw one and lose one. This is a joint pattern of six results that is most likely in balanced groups with high draw rates, and matchday-3 situations where a draw suits both sides add mass; it cannot be read from teams' marginal points.
stages.distribution: Rare joint event per group (low single-digit percent at most for balanced groups); union over twelve nearly independent groups.

stages.name: Player and rare goal-type aggregates
stages.description: Hat Trick counts players with three or more goals in a match (ET included), concentrated in mismatch group games; Club Goals takes the maximum over clubs of goals by players under contract, driven by clubs with many forwards at deep-running nations; Goal in Every Game needs a finalist's player to score in R32, R16, QF, SF and Final. Free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals are rare goal types with type-specific base rates and taker effects.
stages.distribution: Player goals are thinned team counts; hat-trick and rare-event counts are near-Poisson with small means; the club maximum is an order statistic over correlated pools.

stages.name: Per-series scope and payout rules
stages.description: The verified texts change the random variable per series: group-stage series exclude ET by construction, full-tournament and knockout series include it, shootout kicks never count as goals except in Goalie Penalty Goal, own goals go to the beneficiary in team ladders but to the erring team in Goals Allowed and Concede First, three series pay $1/N on ties and Longest Shootout settles all No without a shootout.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the text; reading a flag wrongly shifts team ladders by a goal or flips extreme-market payouts.

contract_review.settlement_definition: All 22 live series have settled (status finalized) rules text. YES conditions: KXWCTOTALGOAL all teams' goals over the full tournament incl. ET, own goals counted, third-place game included, N+ strikes (sample 308+); KXWCTEAMGOALS one named team's goals in the GROUP STAGE (regulation+stoppage), N+; KXWCTEAMTOTALGOALS one named team's goals over the FULL tournament incl. ET, N+; own goals credited to the benefitting country; KXWCGOALSALLOWED named team concedes zero in the group stage, own goals charged to the erring team; KXWCGSGOALS named team allows the most group-stage goals and KXWCGROUPGOALS named group scores the fewest group-stage goals, both with Yes $1/N dead heats; KXWCEVERYTEAMGOAL every team scores at least once; KXWCGAMEGOALS highest knockout match total incl. ET, shootout goals excluded, own goals counted; KXWCFASTESTGOAL earliest goal by official FIFA match minute across all matches; KXWCKOPENALTIES exactly N shootouts in a named round (sample: Quarterfinals); KXWCLONGESTPEN longest shootout measured in rounds, all No if no shootout; KXWCGOALIEPEN any goalkeeper scores in a knockout shootout; KXWCGROUPWINELIM at least N group winners lose in the R32; KXWCGROUPPTS any group with every team on 4 points; KXWCCONCEDE1ST first of Mexico, Spain, Argentina, Ghana to concede by ET timestamp, shootouts excluded, $1/N if none concede; KXWCWINNERTRAIL champion never trails in any match; KXWCHATTRICK at least N hat tricks incl. ET, excl. shootouts; KXWCCLUBGOALS maximum over clubs of goals by players under contract, N+; KXWCGOALEVERYGAME a player scores in each of R32, R16, QF, SF and Final (third place excluded); KXWCFREEKICKGOAL, KXWCOLIMPICO, KXWCGOALIEGOAL any such goal (goalkeeper open-play goal incl. ET, no shootout or own goals). Source of truth: official FIFA match records (only the fastest-goal text names FIFA explicitly).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official FIFA match records (KXWCFASTESTGOAL names 'the official match minute as reported by FIFA'); the other sampled texts do not name a source, so FIFA match reports are assumed as source of truth.
variants_and_edge_cases: Period scope differs inside the archetype: group-stage series (Team Goals, Goals Allowed, Group Stage Goals, Group Points) cannot include ET; full-tournament and knockout series (Total Goals, Tournament Goals, Highest Scoring Game KO, Hat Trick, Goalie Goal) include ET; no series counts shootout kicks as goals except Goalie Penalty Goal, which is only shootout kicks.

Own-goal attribution flips by series: credited to the beneficiary for Team Goals, Tournament Goals and Every Team to Score, charged to the erring team for Goals Allowed and Concede First, and counted in match totals for Total Goals and Highest Scoring Game.

Dead heats pay Yes $1/N rounded down to the cent for Group Stage Goals (most allowed), Group Stage Goals by group (fewest) and Concede First when none of the four concede; other series have no tie rule because they are N+ or exact counts.

Highest Scoring Game: only the 26KO event (incl. ET) is in the sampled rules; the independent reviewer reports a separate 26GS group-stage event '(including regulation and stoppage time)', not present in the pack (see unresolved gs_highest_game_wording_unverified).

Longest Penalty Shootout is counted in rounds of paired kicks; a shootout ending after the first team's kick in a round (possible inside the first five) leaves the final round partial, and the text does not say whether it counts.

Club Goals attributes goals to the club 'currently under contract'; loanees, free agents and players moving during the tournament are not addressed. Goal in Every Game excludes the third-place match, so only the two finalists' players can be YES.
Winner to Trail does not say whether conceding first in a shootout or trailing on aggregate in a shootout counts; goals only are mentioned, so shootouts are presumably excluded.

KXWCCLUBGOALS secondary text contains a template sentence about 'Own goals scored by USA's players' that has no meaning for a club-pool maximum; own goals are presumably not credited to any club, but the text does not say so.

tournament_bracket_composition.label: Tournament matchup composition and host venue
tournament_bracket_composition.target: Whether a named pair of teams is confirmed as the matchup in any match, a named round or a final (settled at qualification), or whether any tournament game is played in a named host country/state.
tournament_bracket_composition.mechanism: Pair-matchup contracts settle the moment both named teams qualify for the same match: in any World Cup match (group co-membership is fixed by the draw, otherwise the pair must converge in a knockout slot), in a named World Cup round (Semifinal, USA Quarterfinal with a 'No Team' outcome), or in the Champions League final after the league phase, two-leg knockout rounds and a fixed bracket. Probabilities come from the joint group, best-third and knockout simulation pushed through the official slot graph. The location series is different: it settles on whether a scheduled game is actually played in Mexico or Massachusetts before 20 July 2026, a host-venue relocation and cancellation risk unrelated to results.

inputs.why: Joint probability the two named teams occupy the same match (any round, a named round or the final) is the settled quantity for four of five series.
Maps group positions and best-third combinations to knockout slots and rounds, the structure every World Cup pairing uses.
Joint cross-group finishing distribution including the best-third ranking feeds slot occupancy.
Group and knockout simulation produces the joint paths from which pair meetings are counted.
International and club strength ratings set each match probability that fills the bracket.
Group tie-breaks and best-third criteria decide slots near the cut.
Single-leg World Cup ties and two-leg Champions League ties, incl. ET and shootouts, decide who advances.
Champions League league-phase rank distribution determines which clubs enter the knockout bracket and where.
UEFA rank-to-bracket-line mapping fixes which side of the Champions League bracket each finisher is on, so whether two clubs can only meet in the final.
Aggregate state between legs updates Champions League advancement during the knockout rounds.
Opponent strength along a team's World Cup path sets its reach probability per round.
Remaining group permutations during the group stage move slot probabilities.
Long-term absences of key players adjust team strength for advancement.
Risk that scheduled host-city games are moved or cancelled settles the location series.
Abandonment or postponement of the specific scheduled games in a host region can leave a location unplayed.
Exact wording fixes any-match vs named-round vs final, settlement at qualification, the No Team outcome and the location granularity.

interactions.hypothesis: Whether two teams from different groups can meet in a given round depends on the best-third combination that qualifies, so pair-meeting probability needs the joint cross-group distribution pushed through the slot graph.
Two Champions League clubs on the same bracket side can only meet before the final, so P(final pairing) is near zero for same-side finishes and multiplicative across rounds for opposite sides.
A host location settles No only if every scheduled game there is moved or not played, so the location probability is a near-certain base state with a small joint failure regime.

Whether two teams from different groups can meet in the R32 or R16 depends on which other groups supply qualifying third-placed teams, so pair-meeting probabilities from independent group marginals pushed through the graph misstate cross-group pairings.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare pair-meeting probabilities from the joint simulation with those from independent group marginals mapped through the annex.

interactions.hypothesis: Teams level on points flip group position at a hard tie-break threshold (head-to-head before overall goal difference per secondary reports), moving a team onto a different bracket side and changing which pairings are possible.
interactions.how_to_test: Re-simulate with head-to-head and overall goal difference swapped and count pairs whose meeting probability changes by more than 1 point.

interactions.hypothesis: A late-round meeting requires both teams to win every feeding tie, so per-round advancement probabilities multiply along two paths; modest per-round edges compound into large differences in Semifinal pairing odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated Semifinal pairing probabilities with the product of single-team reach probabilities for same-side and opposite-side pairs.

interactions.hypothesis: In the Champions League, two clubs whose league-phase ranks put them on the same bracket side can meet before the final but never in it, so the final-pairing probability is zero for those rank combinations and positive only for opposite sides.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate simulated final pairings by league-phase rank combination and confirm zero mass for same-side combinations.

interactions.hypothesis: With several scheduled games per region, individual abandonments almost never empty a region; NO needs a region-level relocation regime, so the location probability is a mixture of a near-certain base state and a rare switch driven by dated news.
interactions.how_to_test: Review relocations in major tournaments since 1990 and compare per-match abandonment rates with region-level relocation events.

nonlinearities.shape: Step change at the best-eight third-place cut
nonlinearities.why: Only eight of twelve third-placed teams advance, so a small goal-difference change moves a team from exit to a specific R32 slot and switches which pairs it can meet.

nonlinearities.shape: Zero, one or a product depending on bracket geometry
nonlinearities.why: Same-group pairs meet with certainty under any-match wording, same-side pairs can meet only before the final, and opposite-side pairs only late; the probability is discontinuous in bracket position rather than smooth in strength.

nonlinearities.shape: Near-zero baseline with a jump on credible relocation news
nonlinearities.why: Region-wide relocation is a discrete official decision, so the NO probability stays near zero until dated announcements move it in steps.

mechanism_review.summary: Four of the five series ask whether a named pair of teams is confirmed in the same match, and they settle the moment both qualify. For the World Cup the probability is the sum over rounds of joint slot occupancy: same-group pairs meet with certainty under the any-match wording, other pairs need group finishes and best-third combinations that route them to a common R32 to Final slot and then wins in every feeding single-leg tie. Named-round variants (Semifinal; USA in a Quarterfinal with a No Team outcome) restrict the sum to one round. The Champions League final pairing follows a different structure: league-phase rank, two-leg playoff and knockout ties, and a fixed bracket that only lets opposite-side clubs meet in the final. The location series is unrelated to results: it settles on whether any scheduled game is actually played in Mexico or Massachusetts before 20 July, a host-operations risk.

stages.name: World Cup slot graph and settlement scope
stages.description: The regulations fix which group positions feed which R32 slot, the annex lookup for the eight best third-placed teams across 495 combinations, and the tree from R32 to the final and third-place match. Each pairing contract reads this graph with its own scope: any match, the Semifinal only, or USA's Quarterfinal, all settled at qualification rather than at kickoff.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping; the only uncertainty is transcription error or an amendment, which would change which pairs can meet in a round.

stages.name: World Cup group finishing and best-third cut
stages.description: Twelve groups of four play three rounds; finishing order follows the tie-break sequence and the eight best of twelve third-placed teams qualify. Which groups supply those eight decides their R32 slots, so a team's possible opponents depend on results in other groups. Strength ratings must come from years of international results, and matchday-3 permutations matter while groups are live.
stages.distribution: Joint discrete distribution over 12 group orderings plus a cross-group third-place ranking with frequent ties on points resolved by goal difference.

stages.name: World Cup knockout convergence of a named pair
stages.description: Two teams in different groups meet only if both win every tie feeding a common slot; settlement happens once the second team qualifies for that match. P(meet) sums over the rounds where their potential paths cross; for the Semifinal variant only one round counts, and for USA Opponent the outcome is a categorical over QF opponents plus No Team. Path difficulty and ET/shootout resolution of single-leg ties enter.
stages.distribution: Sum over rounds of joint products of dependent Bernoulli advancements; strongly correlated because the two paths share potential opponents.

stages.name: Champions League final pairing
stages.description: The 2026 Champions League final pairing comes from the 36-club league phase (ranks 1-8 straight to the R16, 9-24 into a two-leg playoff), then two-leg R16, quarterfinal and semifinal ties on a seeded bracket fixed by rank. Two clubs on the same bracket side cannot both reach the final, so the pairing probability is the product of each side's path probabilities given ranks, updated with aggregate state between legs.
stages.distribution: Mixture over league-phase ranks of products of two-leg advancement probabilities; zero mass for same-side combinations.

stages.name: Host-region game actually played
stages.description: Game Location settles on whether any 2026 World Cup game is played in Mexico or Massachusetts before 20 July. Each region has several scheduled matches, so NO requires a region-wide failure: political or security relocation from a host city, a stadium becoming unavailable, or every scheduled match being abandoned. Team identity and bracket results are irrelevant; dated news about relocation is the only moving signal.
stages.distribution: Near-certain YES base state with a small, news-driven regime-switch probability of region-wide relocation.

coaching_scheme.note: Tactics affect pairings only through match probabilities already in team ratings; no series settles on a coaching decision, and rotation effects sit under group-stage scenarios.

game_context_script.note: ET, shootouts and two-leg aggregate states decide who advances.

pace_volume.note: Outcomes are pair occupancy of a slot or a venue being used, not counts of events, so no opportunity-volume input applies to any of the five series.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and shootout conversion affect advancement only through match and tie probabilities already produced by ratings and the advancement tree; no contract counts a per-opportunity rate.

settlement_contract.note: Any-match vs round vs final scope, settlement at qualification, No Team outcome, location deadline.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Five live series, all with settled rules text. KXWCTEAMSINGAME: YES if the named pair 'is confirmed to be the matchup in any match' of the 2026 World Cup (any round incl. group stage and, by the any-match wording, the third-place game), resolving 'immediately upon qualification, not when the game is actually played'. KXWCMATCHUP: same, restricted to 'the Semifinal' (ticker suffix SEMI2 suggests a specific semifinal slot). KXWCUSAOPPONENT: USA vs a named team in any Quarterfinal; if USA does not reach the Quarterfinals the 'No Team' outcome resolves Yes. KXTEAMSINUCL: the named pair are the two finalists of the 2026 Champions League Final; forfeit or disqualification after qualifying still resolves Yes and reaching a series stage counts. KXWCLOCATION: YES if 'a 2026 FIFA World Cup game is played in Mexico before Jul 20, 2026' (country or US state granularity), independent of which teams play. None of the sampled texts names a settlement source; FIFA/UEFA official announcements are assumed.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled texts. Assumed FIFA and UEFA official bracket/fixture announcements for pairings and FIFA match records for location; the independent reviewer reports that Kalshi lists FIFA, ESPN, Fox Sports and the New York Times for location, which the pack does not show (unresolved location_settlement_source).
variants_and_edge_cases: Scope varies across series: any match (Teams in Game), a named round (Semifinal; USA in a Quarterfinal) and a single final (Champions League); a pair from the same World Cup group meets with certainty in the group stage under the any-match wording.

Settlement is at qualification for all pairing series, so a later forfeit, injury crisis or postponement does not change the outcome; the location series instead requires the game to be played before 20 July 2026.
KXWCUSAOPPONENT is structured: exactly one of the named opponents or 'No Team' resolves Yes, so probabilities must sum to one across outcomes.
KXWCMATCHUP ticker 26SEMI2 suggests the second semifinal slot specifically while the text says 'the Semifinal'; a pair meeting in the other semifinal may settle differently.
The KXTEAMSINUCL secondary text is truncated after 'Mathematical possib', so the treatment of mathematically clinched qualification before the deciding match is not visible.
KXWCLOCATION does not define 'played' for a match that kicks off and is abandoned, nor whether a relocated match within the same country still counts.

knockout_method_of_victory.label: Knockout tie method of victory/finish
knockout_method_of_victory.target: Whether a knockout tie (or a named team's win) is decided in regulation, extra time, or a penalty shootout.
knockout_method_of_victory.mechanism: A single-match knockout final is decided in one of three ordered phases. Regulation (90 minutes plus stoppage) ends the tie when the score is unequal; otherwise 30 minutes of extra time are played, and a level score after 120 minutes goes to a penalty shootout. Method of Finish asks which phase ends the tie; Method of Victory asks which phase a named team wins in. The probability mass is generated by the regulation-draw probability (driven by the strength gap, the low total goal rate typical of finals and late risk aversion), the extra-time scoring rate under fatigue and extra substitutions, and a near-coin-flip shootout.

inputs.why: Opponent-adjusted attack/defence for both finalists sets the regulation goal rates and the strength gap.
Long-memory rating stabilises small international or cup-form samples before a one-off final.
Low-score dependence inflates 0-0 and 1-1, which is exactly the regulation-level cell.
Structural owner of the competition/stage goal and draw multiplier, including the average late-caution effect; soc.late_level_risk_appetite only adds the residual beyond it.

Calibration target only: empirical regulation/ET/penalty frequencies by competition are used to check and recentre the structural chain (ratings -> cagey factor -> ET rate -> shootout), never as an additional driver of draw mass.
Combines the phase probabilities into P(win in ET) and P(win on penalties) per team.
Splits the shootout branch between the teams for Method of Victory; small effect after shrinkage.
Confirmed XI changes the regulation gap and the bench left for extra time.
Bench quality matters more in a 120-minute match than in a 90-minute one.
Absences known days ahead move the strength gap and the substitute pool.
Goalkeeper quality affects both regulation concessions and shootout saves.

Near zero at a true neutral venue but applied at its normal value for a de facto home finalist (host nation in a World Cup final, a club final in its home city); partial crowd splits are handled by soc.neutral_final_venue_split.
Flags whether the contract is about the trophy/advancement or a match result and how stoppage time is treated.
Rules wording distinguishes either-team (MOF) from named-team (MOV) and sets the fair-price rule.
Share of level-at-90 outcomes settled before a shootout.
Residual late-minute caution at level scores beyond the cagey multiplier; inflates the Regular Time NO mass only by what the multiplier misses.
Neutral-venue crowd/travel tilt replaces league home advantage.
Days of rest, travel and minutes load of each finalist before the final differ (domestic cup final or league run-in) and feed extra-time fatigue and the ET-versus-penalties split.
Cumulative minutes of probable starters in the preceding 7/14/28 days proxies fatigue in the 90-120 window, the stage where extra time is decided.
Heat, humidity and altitude at kickoff lower late and extra-time intensity and are a channel between the ET leg and the shootout leg.
Stoppage-time length extends regulation (the Regular Time leg) and is the referee-dependent boundary between phases.

interactions.hypothesis: A small strength gap combined with a cagey final multiplies the regulation-draw probability, so the ET and penalty phases gain most when both conditions hold.
Extra-time goals come disproportionately from the side with fresher, better substitutes, so depth shifts both the ET-versus-penalties split and who wins in ET.
Heat and humidity lower extra-time intensity beyond the pro-rata discount, shifting mass from Extra Time to Penalty Shootout legs.

The level-at-90 probability depends on both the gap and the total rate; a cagey final lowers total goals, which raises the draw cell by more when the gap is small than when one side is a heavy favourite.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical finals, regress level-at-90 on gap bucket x competition goal multiplier and test the product term.

interactions.hypothesis: Extra-time goal intensity and its direction depend on which side keeps quality on the bench and substitutes left; a side with a strong bench raises ET decisiveness and its own ET-win share.
interactions.how_to_test: Among ET matches, compare ET goal share against the difference in bench value and subs remaining at 90 minutes.

interactions.hypothesis: Without home advantage the expected goal difference shrinks toward zero, so the diagonal cells that rho inflates carry more mass in finals than in league fixtures between the same sides.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast draw rates in neutral-venue finals with home/away matches of the same rating gap after the rho correction.

interactions.hypothesis: A goalkeeper strong at shot-stopping both lowers ET concessions and raises shootout win probability, so the ET and penalty MOV legs for that team are positively linked rather than independent.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate MOV legs with and without a shared keeper effect and compare to historical team-level ET and shootout win records.

interactions.hypothesis: Heat and humidity compound the fatigue of the 91-120 window: in hot kickoffs the ET goal rate falls below the pro-rata discount and the share of level-at-120 matches rises, moving mass from Extra Time to Penalty Shootout legs.
interactions.how_to_test: Among extra-time matches, regress ET goals per 30 minutes on kickoff temperature/humidity with competition fixed effects.

interactions.hypothesis: A side whose starters carry heavy recent minutes depends more on bench quality in extra time; unequal load plus unequal depth tilts who scores in the 91-120 window, not only whether anyone does.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical extra-time matches, compare ET goal share against the difference in starter minutes load across the sides, split by bench-value gap.

nonlinearities.shape: inverted-U (level probability peaks at zero strength gap)
nonlinearities.why: The regulation-draw probability is maximal for evenly matched finalists and falls on both sides as the gap grows, so MOF Regular Time NO is a concave function of the gap.

nonlinearities.shape: convex increase of level probability as total goal rate falls
nonlinearities.why: With total expected goals below about 2, the 0-0 and 1-1 cells grow faster than linearly, so a modest cagey multiplier moves the ET/penalty legs a lot.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating, heavily shrunk toward 0.5
nonlinearities.why: Even large observed skill differences translate into only a few points of shootout win probability because kick conversion noise dominates small samples.

mechanism_review.summary: The outcome is the phase that breaks the tie in a single match. First, the two finalists' attack and defence strengths, adjusted for opponent quality and neutral venue, give regulation goal rates; finals run below league rates and draw more often, so the regulation-level probability is typically around 25-35% when the sides are close. Second, low-score dependence and late conservatism at level scores fatten the 0-0/1-1 cells. Third, conditional on level at 90, extra time runs at a reduced, fatigue- and substitute-dependent rate, so roughly half or more of level matches stay level to 120. Fourth, the shootout is close to a coin flip with small skill and goalkeeper effects. MOV multiplies each phase probability by the team's share of that phase. Input hierarchy to avoid double counting draw mass: soc.knockout_cagey_factor plus Dixon-Coles are the structural draw model, soc.late_level_risk_appetite is only a residual, soc.extra_time_phase_scoring_rate and soc.extra_time_shootout_model combine the ET and shootout phases, and soc.method_path_tree_calibration is a calibration check on the result. Settlement wording decides stoppage-time allocation and the fair-price rule for cancellations.

stages.name: Regulation goal rates for a neutral-venue final
stages.description: Each finalist's expected goals in 90 minutes come from opponent-adjusted xG ratings shrunk to a long-memory rating, corrected for the confirmed XI and known absences. Home advantage is set to the small neutral-venue tilt from ticket share and travel rather than a league value. The knockout final multiplier lowers both rates, which matters because the level probability rises steeply as total goals fall.
stages.distribution: Bivariate goal counts with two Poisson-like rates; strength-gap uncertainty is approximately normal on the log-rate scale.

stages.name: Probability the final is level after 90 plus stoppage
stages.description: The regulation-level probability is the sum of diagonal cells of the score grid. Dixon-Coles dependence raises 0-0 and 1-1, the final-stage cagey factor raises draws further, and late risk aversion in the 75-90+ window at level scores reduces the decisive-goal hazard. This cell is the complement of MOF Regular Time YES and the shared base of all ET and penalty legs.
stages.distribution: A single probability near 0.2-0.4, concave in the strength gap (peaks when sides are equal) and decreasing in total goal rate.

stages.name: Extra-time resolution
stages.description: Given level at 90, 30 more minutes are played with an additional substitution allowance. Goal intensity is below a pro-rata share of the regulation rate because of fatigue and caution, and it tilts toward the side with the stronger bench and fewer cards. The phase decides how level-at-90 mass splits between Extra Time and Penalty Shootout legs and which team wins the Extra Time MOV leg.
stages.distribution: Goals in 30 minutes are low counts (mean roughly 0.5-0.8 combined); P(level at 120 | level at 90) is often 0.5-0.6.

stages.name: Penalty shootout
stages.description: Five alternating kicks per side then sudden death. Conversion is around 70-80% per kick, team skill differences are small and noisy, and first-kicker advantage is disputed in the literature. Goalkeeper save ability and the designated takers still on the pitch after 120 minutes are the only material inputs; heavy shrinkage toward 50% is required.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli winner with p close to 0.5; length is a stopping time but only the winner matters here.

stages.name: Contract phase mapping and settlement
stages.description: Regulation includes stoppage time, Extra Time ends before the shootout, and Penalty Shootout requires both earlier phases completed. MOF legs are either-team; MOV legs are team-specific. Trophy wording (UCL/UEL) versus advancement wording (World Cup) and a fair-price rule for cancellation beyond two weeks define the edge cases; no data source is named.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the phase and winner to six MOV or three MOF YES outcomes; fair-price settlements are rare continuous values.
