contract_review.settlement_definition: Binary markets per phase on one knockout final. MOF (KXUCLMOF, KXWCMOF) settles YES for the phase in which either team wins the trophy/advances; MOV (KXUELMOV, KXWCMOV) settles YES only if the named team wins in that phase. Regular/Regulation Time includes the 90 minutes plus all stoppage time and excludes extra time and the shootout; Extra Time is a win after extra time but before any shootout; Penalty Shootout is a win via shootout after regulation and extra time. Cancellation or rescheduling more than two weeks away resolves to a fair price. The source of truth is not named in the sampled text.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; presumably the official UEFA/FIFA match report as used by Kalshi's data provider.
variants_and_edge_cases: MOF (either team) vs MOV (named team): MOF Regular Time YES = P(regulation decisive); MOV splits each phase between the two teams, so six MOV legs sum to one and three MOF legs sum to one.

UCL/UEL wording uses 'wins the trophy'; World Cup wording uses 'advances'. For a final these coincide, but if the World Cup series is listed for earlier knockout rounds the 'advances' wording applies to a match with no trophy.
Stoppage time at the end of 90 minutes counts as Regular Time; a goal at 90+8 is regulation, while a goal at 91' of extra time is Extra Time.
An abandoned final replayed within two weeks presumably settles on the replay; beyond two weeks a fair price applies, and the fair-price method is truncated in the sampled text.
Two-legged ties are not represented in the sampled series (all are single-match finals); the same contract on a two-leg tie would need aggregate and away-goal logic.

match_combo_parlay.label: Soccer same-match combination (parlay)
match_combo_parlay.target: Two or more match events in one game must all occur (e.g. a named player scores first and his team advances).
match_combo_parlay.mechanism: A prepack settles YES only if every leg occurs in the same match. The legs share one score path: for the sampled contract the player must score the first goal of the match at any point up to the end of extra time, and his team must then advance, which includes winning on penalties. The joint probability is the probability the player's team scores first times the player's share of that first goal (driven by minutes on the pitch, shot share and penalty duty), times the probability that a team leading first goes on to advance, which is high in knockouts but not certain because extra time and shootouts remain.

inputs.why: Gives P(named player scores the match's first goal) with competing risks and substitution timing.
Pregame form: P(team scores first by minute t) from rating-based goal rates and a half-specific time profile, plus the goalless-120 mass; the in-play hazard is not available pregame and is not used.
Player's non-penalty shot quality and volume per 90 set his share of team goals.
Designated takers capture penalty first goals; a large share for a star taker.
Start, substitute and DNP probabilities determine whether the player can score first at all.
Advancement through regulation, extra time and shootout given the score state.
How often the side that conceded first equalises, which breaks the advancement leg.
Team strengths set both who scores first and who advances.
Confirmed lineups move team rates and confirm the player's start.
Opponent's concession by route (set piece, penalty, own goal) shifts the player's share and the own-goal risk.
Leg wording differs per prepack and must be parsed each time.
Calibration/validation target for the advancement leg: empirical P(advance | first-goal minute, gap) checks the structural tree; it is not an additional driver beyond soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.
Windows, own-goal and DNP treatment per leg.
Supplies the shootout and extra-time branch of the advancement leg once the first scorer's team has been equalised.
Competition/stage multiplier that lowers goal rates and sets the goalless-120 point mass, which kills the scorer leg.
Penalty awards (and designated-taker conversion) are a high-xG route to the first goal, credited almost entirely to the taker.
VAR-driven penalties and disallowed goals shift who scores first; folded into soc.penalty_rate as a tournament scalar.
Planned minutes and withdrawal minute for the named player, conditioned on tournament and age (a 39-year-old star has a capped, rest-managed minutes profile); scales the scorer leg directly.

interactions.hypothesis: If the player's first goals come early, his team has longer to lose the lead, so the conditional advancement leg is weaker than for late first goals.
A planned substitution of the player before the typical first-goal minute in a low-scoring match sharply cuts the scorer leg without changing the advancement leg.
The stronger the player's team, the smaller the uplift from scoring first because it would usually advance anyway; underdogs gain the most conditional uplift.

Both legs depend on the first-goal minute: an early goal by the player gives the opponent more time to equalise, a late one nearly secures advancement, so the joint probability is an integral over minute, not a product.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the joint with and without minute dependence and compare predicted joint frequencies with historical first-scorer-and-advance outcomes binned by first-goal minute.

interactions.hypothesis: If the player's expected withdrawal minute precedes the typical first-goal minute in a low-scoring match, his scorer share collapses; above that threshold the scorer leg is insensitive to small changes in substitution timing.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast realised first-scorer rates for players subbed before vs after 60' grouped by match total-goal expectation.

interactions.hypothesis: The dependence ratio P(advance | first goal) / P(advance) shrinks as the player's team becomes a stronger favourite, because its unconditional advancement is already near one; underdog stars show the largest uplift.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot the empirical ratio P(advance | scored first) / P(advance) against pre-match Elo gap in knockout matches.

interactions.hypothesis: A penalty first goal belongs to the designated taker only if he is still on the pitch: awarded before his withdrawal it is near-certain his; awarded after, it goes to another player, so the taker's route share is conditional on his on-pitch window.
interactions.how_to_test: Among first-goal penalties in tournaments, split by whether the designated taker was on the pitch and compare the taker share.

interactions.hypothesis: If the opponent equalises, advancement reverts to a near-even tie with extra time and penalties, so the response hazard matters only through the share of first-scorer paths that are later levelled.
interactions.how_to_test: Among knockout matches where the first scorer was equalised, measure the first scorer's eventual advancement rate against an even-tie baseline.

nonlinearities.shape: increasing S-curve in the minute of the first goal
nonlinearities.why: Advancement probability after scoring first rises slowly for early goals and steeply after about 70 minutes as the opponent runs out of time, then saturates near one.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: zero if DNP, linear in minutes on pitch otherwise
nonlinearities.why: The scorer leg requires being on the pitch; a DNP is a point mass at zero and partial minutes scale the share roughly in proportion to exposure.

mechanism_review.summary: The sampled combo is a conjunction of two dependent events on one score path. First, the match must produce at least one goal within 120 minutes and the player's team must score it; this depends on the two teams' goal hazards. Second, the player must be on the pitch and be the scorer of that goal, which depends on his start probability, substitution timing, share of team shots and xG, and penalty duty. Third, conditional on his team leading first at minute t, it must advance: the lead must be held or restored, and if equalised, the match is decided in extra time or a shootout. The joint probability is therefore not the product of the legs' marginals; it is the integral over the first-goal minute of the scorer hazard times the conditional advancement probability at that minute. Contract parsing determines which goals and which advancement routes count.

stages.name: Which team scores the first goal and when
stages.description: Team goal hazards (pregame form: rating-based rates with a half-specific time profile, not the in-play hazard) for Argentina and Switzerland, set from opponent-adjusted ratings and the confirmed XI, decide the probability that Argentina scores first, that Switzerland does, or that the match stays goalless for 120 minutes. The timing of the first goal is roughly exponential with a rate that rises slightly through each half; in a cagey knockout the goalless share is material.
stages.distribution: Competing risks over minutes with a point mass on no goal by 120 minutes (several percent in tight knockouts).

stages.name: Player's share of his team's first goal
stages.description: Conditional on Argentina scoring first at minute t, Messi must be on the pitch at t and be the scorer. His share comes from his non-penalty shot and xG share, his penalty duty (a first goal from the spot almost certainly belongs to the designated taker), direct free kicks, and the probability of an own goal by the opponent. A substitution plan for a veteran player reduces the share late in the match and in extra time.
stages.distribution: Time-varying share with a drop to zero after substitution; penalty route is a discrete jump in share; overall a small probability per match.

stages.name: Advancement conditional on leading first
stages.description: After scoring first, the team must advance (structure: the advancement tree with the trailing-side response hazard; the empirical lead-protection curve is only a calibration check, so equaliser risk is counted once). In knockouts a 1-0 lead converts often but the trailing side raises its attacking intensity, and an equaliser sends the match into a regulation-level state with extra time and penalties still available to either side. Earlier first goals leave more time for a response; stronger teams protect leads better.
stages.distribution: Conditional probability, typically high (around 0.75-0.9), decreasing in the time remaining and increasing in the strength gap.

stages.name: Joint integration of the legs
stages.description: The combo probability integrates, over the first-goal minute, the hazard that the named player scores first at that minute times the conditional advancement probability given the lead from that minute. The joint simulation is a modelling component and validation target, not an input; its output is never fed back as a feature. A minute-level simulation that tracks score, substitutions and phase is the natural tool; validating the joint indicator against historical matches shows how far the dependence moves the result from a product of marginals.
stages.distribution: Joint Bernoulli with strong positive dependence between legs; dependence ratio typically well above 1 for a player on the stronger side.

stages.name: Leg parsing and settlement
stages.description: Each prepack names its legs in rules_primary only. For the sampled one, the first-goal window explicitly includes extra time, advancement implicitly includes a shootout, and own goals, DNP and postponement are not addressed. Other prepacks in the series may combine different legs, so a per-event parse is required before any probability is computed.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from parsed flags; unparsed or ambiguous legs create discrete settlement risk.

talent_strength.note: Team strength drives both legs; player quality drives the scorer share.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent's concession routes and defensive strength.

role_personnel.note: Penalty and set-piece duty and attacking role.

availability_news.note: Whether the player starts and when he is likely to be withdrawn.

coaching_scheme.note: How the trailing side changes approach after conceding first.

environment.note: Venue, heat and travel affect both teams' goal rates through the team model; there is no environment channel specific to the leg dependence, and the sampled match is at a neutral North American venue for both sides.

game_context_script.note: Score state after the first goal and the ET/penalty escape route.

pace_volume.note: Goal intensity sets when the first goal arrives and the goalless share.

efficiency_conversion.note: Player finishing and penalty awards as routes to the first goal.

distribution_variance.note: Joint distribution of the legs comes from the minute-level simulation built on the scorer hazard and the advancement tree (a model component, not an input).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Tournament minutes management for a veteran (planned withdrawal minute, rest in dead rubbers) is carried by soc.player_minutes_expectation with tournament/age conditioning; its calibration is open in u2.

officiating_rules.note: Penalty awards and disallowed goals change who scores first.

settlement_contract.note: Leg windows, own goals, DNP.

contract_review.settlement_definition: The sampled prepack (KXWCPREPACK, Argentina vs Switzerland, World Cup knockout of Jul 11 2026) settles YES only if Lionel Messi scores the first goal of the entire game, counting regulation, stoppage and any extra time, AND Argentina advances. Advancement presumably includes a shootout win; a 0-0 after 120 minutes leaves no first goalscorer so the scorer leg fails. Treatment of own goals as the first goal, of Messi not playing, of postponement and the source of truth is not stated (rules_secondary is empty).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not stated in the sampled rules (rules_secondary empty); presumably official FIFA match report via Kalshi's provider.
variants_and_edge_cases: Goalless after 120 minutes: there is no first goal, so the scorer leg fails even if Argentina wins the shootout.
First goal an own goal by Switzerland: under the wording Messi did not score first, so the contract fails, but own-goal treatment is not stated explicitly.
Messi does not play or is substituted before scoring: no DNP/void clause is visible; a DNP likely makes the scorer leg false rather than void.
Other prepacks in the series may combine different legs (team totals, both teams to score, a different player) with different windows; each needs its own parse.
Only one series and one event were sampled, so the combo structure is verified only for this leg pair.

player_appearance_selection.label: Soccer player appearance, squad selection and availability
player_appearance_selection.target: Whether a named player (or pair) records playing time for a team in a match or window, or is named in a national team's final tournament squad (KXPLAYWC).
player_appearance_selection.mechanism: Appearance is a chain of gates rather than a performance: the player must be eligible (registered, under contract, eligible for the federation), fit on the match day, selected into the matchday squad, and then actually used by the coach, either from the start or as a substitute. Single-match contracts settle on official playing time in that game; window contracts are a union over every qualifying fixture before a deadline, with fitness persisting between matches; pair contracts require two players' on-pitch intervals to overlap. The probabilities are generated by injury recovery, contract and registration status, coach preference and rotation, and the number of qualifying fixtures.

inputs.why: Current injury and suspension state is the first gate for every appearance contract.
Hazard of a new injury over the window for players currently fit.
Expected role and minutes under the current coach set start and substitute probabilities.
Start/sub/DNP mixture maps directly onto 'enters the game and records playing time'.
Confirmed lineups and benches at T-60 nearly resolve single-match contracts.
Coach statements on fitness and selection arrive one to two days before matches.
Rotation in low-stakes fixtures removes regulars from the XI and sometimes from the matchday squad.
Dead-rubber and end-of-season matches change usage of stars and fringe players.
Expiring or expired contracts govern whether a player can play for a club in the window.
Card accumulation and red cards create suspensions that block appearances.
Game state drives late substitutions, which decide whether a bench player gets minutes.
Scope flags for which matches count (official only, friendlies, any NWSL team).
Wording differs per series: final squad vs entering the game vs simultaneous presence.
Return-date distribution for currently injured players.
Joint on-pitch overlap for pair contracts.
Number of chances inside the window.
Contract and registration gates.
Gate for national-team contracts: the player must be in the USA camp or 26-man World Cup squad; recent camps and minutes under the current coach set that probability.
Positional competition for camp and squad slots (striker pool for Balogun) decides call-up conditional on fitness.
Squad size, final-list deadline and replacement rules fix when a camp or squad place can still open.
Qualification state before a group finale (e.g. Argentina already through before Jordan) is the main rotation driver for the single-match KXWCPLAY contract.
System and role structure determine whether two midfielders (or a striker) fit together in the XI against a given opponent.
Transfers, loans and manager changes shift availability and registration state during the window.

interactions.hypothesis: A late return date matters only if few qualifying matches remain after it; with many fixtures the window probability is insensitive to a one-week delay.
Two midfielders competing for the same role overlap less in rotated fixtures, so the pair probability falls more than either marginal when rotation is high.
For an off-contract player both gates must open; fitness news is worthless until a registration path exists.

For an injured player the window probability is near zero if the return quantile falls after the last qualifying fixture and climbs steeply once it falls before; extra fixtures after return add little because fitness persists.
interactions.how_to_test: For past injured players with deadline contracts, compare appearance-by-deadline against (deadline - median return date) and the number of fixtures after the return date.

interactions.hypothesis: When both midfielders are first choice, overlap is almost certain whenever both are fit; in rotated end-of-season matches one is rested, and if they compete for one role the coach alternates them, so overlap probability drops more than the marginals suggest.
interactions.how_to_test: In the club's history, compare the overlap rate of the pair in high-rotation versus low-rotation matches conditional on both being available.

interactions.hypothesis: If registration opens late (a free agent signing near the end of the NWSL season or the deadline) few qualifying fixtures remain, so the window probability collapses once the opening date passes a threshold; early registration leaves it insensitive to a few days' delay.
interactions.how_to_test: For past signings, compare appearance-by-deadline against days between registration and deadline and the number of fixtures remaining then.

interactions.hypothesis: A bench player's entry probability changes regime with the score: large leads or deficits trigger more substitutions, while a tight knockout keeps the coach with his starters, cutting entry for veterans or fringe players.
interactions.how_to_test: Entry rates of benched players by score margin at minute 60 and match type.

interactions.hypothesis: A player carrying a minor knock is held out of low-stakes fixtures but risked in decisive ones, so availability depends on stakes, not only on medical state.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare return-match stakes for players returning from minor injuries versus a random-match baseline.

nonlinearities.shape: concave, saturating union probability
nonlinearities.why: Each extra fixture adds less because a player who is fit and favoured appears early; with strong persistence of fitness the curve flattens after two or three matches.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped cumulative availability in calendar time
nonlinearities.why: Return-time distributions have little mass in the first weeks, a steep middle and a long setback tail, so window probability moves sharply around the median return date.

mechanism_review.summary: Appearance outcomes are generated by sequential gates. Eligibility: the player must be registered for the team (contract signed, roster space, federation eligibility); for an out-of-contract player this can dominate. Fitness: a currently injured player's return date is a right-skewed distribution with setback risk, and fit players face a per-match hazard of new injury or suspension. Selection: given fitness, the coach decides matchday squad and XI from role, form, rotation and stakes. Usage: a bench player enters only if the coach substitutes him, which depends on score state and substitutions left. Single-match contracts are one pass through the gates; window contracts take the union over the qualifying fixtures with strong persistence of fitness and eligibility across matches; pair contracts need both players' on-pitch intervals to intersect, which depends on whether they are complements or rivals for one role.

stages.name: Eligibility and registration gate
stages.description: Before fitness or selection matter, the player must be eligible to appear for the named team: a current contract and league registration for club contracts (relevant to an NWSL player whose contract status is in question), and federation eligibility plus a call-up for national-team windows. For national-team contracts such as KXBALOGUNPLAY there is an additional selection gate before any match: the player must be in the camp or the final World Cup squad, a coach decision driven by call-up history, positional competition and squad deadlines. Transfer windows, roster limits and negotiation progress make this a discrete state with a time-varying hazard of opening. For KXPLAYWC this gate is the whole contract: YES is being named in the final World Cup squad, so call-up history, positional slot competition, fitness at the list deadline and the squad-list rules settle it without any match appearance.
stages.distribution: Binary state with a hazard of switching to eligible; often a mass of probability on 'never within the window'.

stages.name: Fitness on each qualifying match day
stages.description: For an injured player, the probability of being fit by each date comes from the return-to-play distribution of the injury type, which has a long right tail from setbacks. For a fit player, a per-match hazard of fresh injury or suspension from card accumulation applies. Fitness states persist across consecutive matches, so window outcomes are strongly autocorrelated rather than independent per fixture.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed return time (log-normal-like) with a setback mixture; daily availability series with high persistence.

stages.name: Coach selection into matchday squad and XI
stages.description: Given fitness, the coach chooses the matchday squad and starting XI. Core starters are near-certain; fringe players depend on form, tactical fit and rotation. End-of-season or dead-rubber club matches and pre-tournament friendlies raise rotation and give minutes to fringe players while resting stars. Press conferences and confirmed lineups at T-60 update this stage sharply.
stages.distribution: Start probability per match close to 0 or 1 for most players with a mid-range mass for rotation candidates.

stages.name: Entry from the bench and minutes recorded
stages.description: A player on the bench records playing time only if brought on; the probability depends on position, the coach's substitution habits, the score state (comfortable leads and heavy deficits produce more changes) and remaining substitutions. For single-match contracts like the Messi game this is the main residual uncertainty after the lineup is known.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli entry given bench with probability varying by game state; entry minute right-skewed toward 60-85'.

stages.name: Window union and pair overlap
stages.description: Window contracts aggregate over every qualifying fixture before the deadline, so the fixture count and type matter as much as the per-match probability. The pair contract needs the two Real Madrid midfielders' on-pitch intervals to overlap in at least one official match in late May, which depends on their joint availability and on whether the coach uses them together or as alternatives in the same role.
stages.distribution: Union probability 1 - prod(1 - p_m) under positive dependence across matches; pair overlap is a joint distribution of two interval processes.

stages.name: Scope and settlement wording
stages.description: Each series defines participation differently: entering with official playing time, playing for a team within a window, simultaneous presence, or squad naming. Whether friendlies count is explicit only for the pair contract; minimum minutes are undefined for the window contracts. These flags must be stored per series and decide which fixtures enter the union.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the flags; unresolved flags create two candidate fixture sets with different union probabilities.

talent_strength.note: Player quality enters through the coach's role and minutes allocation, not team strength.

opponent_matchup.note: Tactical system determines whether two midfielders fit together and whether a striker type is used against a given opponent.

role_personnel.note: Role, depth chart and positional competition.

availability_news.note: Fitness, suspension and eligibility states with timestamps.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach selection and rotation habits.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel do not determine whether a player is selected or enters; heat could marginally increase substitutions but substitution counts are capped by rule and captured in the entry model.

game_context_script.note: Score state drives bench entries.

pace_volume.note: Number of qualifying matches is the opportunity count.

efficiency_conversion.note: Appearance is not a per-opportunity success rate on the pitch; there is no finishing or conversion step between selection and settlement, so this category has no mechanism here.

distribution_variance.note: Dependence across matches and between paired players.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Season-end and pre-tournament matches change usage.

officiating_rules.note: Suspensions from cards; substitution limits.

settlement_contract.note: Participation definitions and fixture scope.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Five different YES events. KXPLAYWC is a squad-list contract that the final series assignment keeps in this archetype; it is modelled by the stage s1 national-team selection gate (call-up history, positional competition, squad-list rules) and fitness at the list deadline, and its re-filing to the squad archetype remains a proposal (series_mapping_issues). KXWCPLAY: the player enters the named World Cup game and records official playing time in regulation, stoppage or extra time; being listed as a starter or substitute without entering is NO. KXBALOGUNPLAY: the player plays for the USA national team before Jul 7 2026 (minimum minutes and friendlies not stated). KXRMAPLAYTOGETHER: two Real Madrid players are on the pitch simultaneously at any point in any official match May 7-31 2026. KXTRINITYRODMANNWSL: the player plays for any NWSL team before Dec 31 2026. KXPLAYWC: the player is named in his country's final World Cup squad, YES even with no appearances. Source of truth is not named in any sample.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; presumably official match reports/lineups (FIFA, LaLiga, NWSL, U.S. Soccer) via Kalshi's provider.
variants_and_edge_cases: Bench without entering is NO for KXWCPLAY; KXBALOGUNPLAY and KXTRINITYRODMANNWSL do not define 'plays', so a one-minute cameo presumably counts but is not stated.
KXBALOGUNPLAY's title says 'play in the game tonight' while rules give a window ending Jul 7, 2026; the window reading is what the rules state.

Friendlies: KXRMAPLAYTOGETHER restricts to official matches; the USA and NWSL contracts are silent. The KXBALOGUNPLAY window (before Jul 7, 2026) covers pre-tournament friendlies and, per the published schedule, the USA's home World Cup group matches from Jun 12 and knockout rounds through the round of 16 if the USA survives, so friendlies matter less than official tournament matches and the fixture count is conditional on USA advancement.
Pair overlap ends when a player is substituted off, sent off or the match ends; a player entering at the moment the other leaves does not overlap.

KXPLAYWC settles on final-squad naming ('If the player is named in the final squad but does not appear in any matches, the market still resolves Yes'); unlike KXWCSQUAD its text does not say whether a late replacement added after the initial announcement or a post-selection withdrawal counts.

player_squad_selection_and_lineup.label: Soccer squad selection and starting lineup
player_squad_selection_and_lineup.target: A named player is included in a national team's officially announced final tournament squad, or in the starting XI at kickoff of a match.
player_squad_selection_and_lineup.mechanism: Both contracts settle on a coach's list, not on play. A final World Cup squad is a fixed-size list drawn from a candidate pool by a coach who relies heavily on players he has repeatedly called up, subject to de facto positional quotas, the player's fitness at the deadline and, for veterans, the player's own decision to take part; late injury replacements before the first match add a path for reserves. A starting XI is the coach's match-specific choice given the opponent, fitness, suspensions and the stakes of the match, and is settled by who is on the field at kickoff.

inputs.why: Fitness at the list deadline or match day is the main reason a favoured candidate is left out.
Official lineup at T-60 nearly resolves the starting-XI contract.
Calibration of predicted versus announced XIs measures how predictable this coach is.
Coach statements before matches and before list announcements.
Rotation in dead-rubber group matches and the third-place match changes starters.
Group-stage clinch status and placement matches drive rotation decisions.
Yellow-card accumulation suspensions remove starters for specific tournament matches.
System choice for the opponent decides how many centre-backs or forwards start.
Injury hazard between now and the list deadline for currently fit candidates.
Calendar of list announcements and provisional-list dates.
Rules define final versus provisional lists, replacements and kickoff lineup.
Coach familiarity measured by recent camps and minutes.
Zero-sum competition within positional quotas.
Squad size, deadlines and replacement window.
Credible pre-announcement reports.
Veteran self-selection risk through retirement or declared unavailability.
Recent club minutes and starts (and international minutes, separately) measure sharpness and role; for fringe candidates and veterans this is the leading indicator of call-up changes.
Accumulated club and in-tournament minutes raise injury risk and rotation need; before the list it flags fatigue, during the tournament it feeds group-stage XI rotation.
A coaching change before the tournament resets the call-up pool and pushes fringe probabilities toward a wider prior.
Qualification state (clinched, needs a result, eliminated) before a group finale determines how many first-choice players start.

interactions.hypothesis: A rival's injury in the same position raises a fringe candidate's probability far more than a rival injury elsewhere, because quotas are positional.
Rotation is concentrated in matches with low stakes for the coach, such as a clinched third group match or the third-place match, which flips starter probabilities for squad players.
For veterans with long call-up histories, inclusion hinges almost entirely on stated intent and fitness rather than on competition.

An injury to a rival in the candidate's own position frees a quota slot and raises his probability sharply, while an injury elsewhere does nothing; the effect is largest for the first reserve in that position.
interactions.how_to_test: In past tournaments, compare inclusion of the next-ranked candidate when a same-position versus different-position regular was injured before the deadline.

interactions.hypothesis: Coaches keep their best XI until qualification is secured; once the stakes fall below a threshold (clinched group, third-place match) several changes happen at once, so squad players' start probabilities jump.
interactions.how_to_test: Number of changes to the XI by stakes bucket in World Cup and Euro matches since 2006.

interactions.hypothesis: Call-up history predicts inclusion only under the coach who made those call-ups; a coaching change before the tournament resets the regime and pushes fringe probabilities toward a wider prior.
interactions.how_to_test: Retention of the previous coach's regulars in final squads after mid-cycle coaching changes versus continuity cases.

interactions.hypothesis: Injuries to listed players between the list and the first match create replacement slots; the probability that a given reserve is called depends jointly on the injury hazard of listed players in his position and on him being first in line.
interactions.how_to_test: Count late replacements per tournament and the rank of the replacement within the coach's reserve list.

interactions.hypothesis: A tier-one leak a day before brings most of the information; the official lineup then adds little except for rare late changes, so the value of further reports falls quickly.
interactions.how_to_test: Accuracy of leaked lists and XIs by source tier compared with official releases.

interactions.hypothesis: For established core players call-up history alone decides inclusion; for fringe candidates and veterans with few recent camps, club minutes and match sharpness add information, so the club-minutes signal matters only in the middle of the call-up-history range.
interactions.how_to_test: In past squads, regress inclusion on call-up share and club minutes share with their product, within the low-to-mid call-up band.

nonlinearities.shape: steep logistic in recent call-up share
nonlinearities.why: Players called to nearly every recent camp are almost always selected and players absent from most are almost never selected, with a narrow transition band where most of the uncertainty lives.

nonlinearities.shape: step at the quota boundary
nonlinearities.why: Moving from first to second reserve in a position changes inclusion probability far more than moving between two ranks well inside the quota.

mechanism_review.summary: Final-squad inclusion is a constrained ranking. The coach has a fixed number of slots with positional quotas and fills them mostly from players he has called up and used in recent windows; candidates outside that core enter mainly when a rival is injured or out of form. Fitness at the list deadline removes some favoured candidates, and late injury replacements before the first match give reserves a second path. For veteran stars the coach's choice is near-automatic, so the outcome turns on the player's intent and fitness. Starting-XI inclusion is a match-level choice: core starters are fixed when fit, while squad players start when stakes are low (dead rubbers, third-place match), when a starter is suspended for card accumulation, or when the coach changes system for an opponent. Leaks and press conferences resolve much of the uncertainty before official release.

stages.name: Candidate pool and coach familiarity
stages.description: The relevant pool is players the coach has called up in recent international windows, weighted by recency and minutes. Coaches rarely add uncapped or long-absent players to a final list, so the call-up record under the current coach dominates club form or market value. A coaching change before the tournament resets this pool and widens uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Highly bimodal: core players near 0.95+, fringe candidates spread over 0.1-0.6, outsiders near zero.

stages.name: Positional quotas and rival competition
stages.description: Slots are allocated by position, so a candidate competes with direct rivals: three goalkeepers, a fixed number of full-backs and centre-backs, and so on. Versatile players can occupy two queues. Rival injuries or form changes shift a fringe candidate's chance without any change in his own status, making the outcome correlated across candidates of the same position.
stages.distribution: Negative dependence among candidates for the same position (sum of inclusions fixed by the quota).

stages.name: Fitness, intent and the replacement window
stages.description: At the deadline a favoured candidate can be excluded by injury; veterans can self-select out. After the list, injured players may be replaced until shortly before the first match, and under KXWCSQUAD both the withdrawn player and the replacement settle YES. This creates asymmetric paths: injuries cost favoured players only before the list but help reserves afterwards.
stages.distribution: Discrete injury shocks with timing relative to the deadline; replacement probability small but concentrated on the first reserve per position.

stages.name: Match-day starting XI decision
stages.description: For a starting-XI contract the coach chooses eleven given the opponent, system, fitness, card suspensions and stakes. Core starters are near-certain when fit; others depend on rotation, which is heavy in matches with little at stake such as the third-place play-off or a group finale after qualification. Press-conference hints and confirmed lineups at T-60 nearly settle the question; the residual is a warm-up withdrawal.
stages.distribution: Per-player start probability with a large mass near 0 and 1; announced-XI to kickoff changes are rare (well under 1%).

stages.name: Information release and settlement
stages.description: Official lists and lineups arrive at known times, preceded by leaks of varying reliability. Settlement uses the final list (provisional lists excluded) or the XI on the field at kickoff, and a match not played by the stated date resolves NO for the starting-XI series. Correct timing of each information release is essential to avoid look-ahead in back-tests.
stages.distribution: Step changes in probability at leak and announcement times; deterministic settlement thereafter.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities: a squad list or a kickoff XI is a single selection event, so possessions, shots or fixture counts do not enter the outcome.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion step exists between the coach's decision and settlement; on-pitch efficiency matters only indirectly through earlier form, already in call-up history.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Final-squad series (KXSOCCERPLAYCRON, KXSOCCERPLAYMESSI, KXWCSQUAD) settle YES if the player is named on his country's officially announced final 2026 World Cup squad, regardless of appearances; KXWCSQUAD also counts players added before the team's first match and keeps YES for named players who later withdraw; provisional or preliminary lists do not count. KXPLAYWC (Lamine Yamal) carries the same final-squad wording but the final series assignment files it under player_appearance_selection, which models it with the same squad-gate inputs; it is not a series of this archetype. The starting-XI series (KXWCSTART) settles YES if the player is in the official starting lineup and on the field when the match begins; withdrawn before kickoff is NO; substitute appearances do not count; if the match does not occur before Jul 20 2026 all markets resolve NO.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named; presumably the official federation or FIFA squad announcement and the FIFA match lineup.
variants_and_edge_cases: Provisional or preliminary lists do not count (KXWCSQUAD text truncates after 'Provisional, preliminary,'); only the final list matters.
A late replacement before the first match counts as YES for KXWCSQUAD; whether KXSOCCERPLAYCRON/MESSI treat late additions the same way is not stated.
KXWCSTART: a player not on the initially announced XI but in the official lineup at kickoff is YES; a late warm-up withdrawal is NO.
The sampled KXWCSTART event is the third-place match (France vs England, Jul 18), where rotation is unusually high.
Titles 'Will Cristiano Ronaldo play in the World Cup?' suggest appearance, but rules settle on squad naming; a title-only reading would be wrong.

KXPLAYWC has wording identical to the KXSOCCER* final-squad series; the final series assignment keeps it in player_appearance_selection, whose stage s1 models it with the shared inputs (call-up history, positional competition, squad-list rules), so this catalog entry does not list it.

team_win_streak.label: Team consecutive-win streak
team_win_streak.target: Whether a team strings together at least N consecutive wins across all competitions within a stated period.
team_win_streak.mechanism: The contract settles YES if somewhere in the calendar year the team wins at least N matches in a row across all competitions. The outcome is generated by an ordered sequence of match win probabilities (each well below one, with draws as frequent streak-breakers), the number of matches available before the year ends, and serial dependence from form, injuries and manager changes that makes good and bad runs cluster. The probability of a run of length N is a highly convex function of the typical per-match win probability, so modest changes in team strength or schedule order move it a lot; once the run is achieved the contract is settled.

inputs.why: Per-match win probabilities in order are the core input to a run-length calculation.

Residual serial correlation only, after drift from rating uncertainty, manager changes, summer reset and injuries is modelled; calibrate against out-of-sample streak frequencies so the clustering uplift is not counted twice.
Opponent-adjusted strength sets each match's win probability.
Uncertainty in team strength is shared across all matches and fattens the tails of the streak outcome.
Draws break a win streak; a draw-prone team has fewer streaks for the same points rate.
Venue ordering in the sequence changes which windows are winnable.
A manager change shifts strength and often produces a short-term run, a regime switch for the streak.
Key-player absences lower win probability over a block of consecutive fixtures.
Cup survival adds fixtures (often winnable early rounds) and congestion.
Which competitions count and whether a shootout win counts as a win.
Rules define the calendar window and all-competitions scope.
As-of run length and absorbing YES state.
Ordered fixtures across two seasons.
Summer change in strength for the autumn half.
Minutes load across league, cup and European fixtures lowers win probability and raises rotation inside dense blocks (Dec-Jan, cup runs).
Classifies cup ties drawn after 90 minutes (extra-time win versus shootout) under each scope reading of what counts as a win.

interactions.hypothesis: Positive serial dependence raises the streak probability most for mid-table teams whose per-match win probability is near 0.5, where independent runs of five are rare.
Clusters of home matches against weaker opponents create windows where a run is plausible; the same fixtures spread out yield fewer runs.
A manager change or summer rebuild resets the strength regime for all later matches at once, so the streak probability depends on a shared latent shift.

Positive autocorrelation lets good spells string wins together; the uplift over independent trials is largest when per-match win probability is moderate (0.45-0.6) and small for dominant teams that streak anyway.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed frequency of 5-win runs in Premier League club-seasons with independent simulations from the same per-match probabilities, by win-probability band.

interactions.hypothesis: A block of home fixtures against weaker opponents produces a high-probability window; the same fixtures interleaved with away matches at strong sides produce fewer complete windows, so order changes the result at constant average difficulty.
interactions.how_to_test: Permutation test: shuffle fixture order within a season and compare simulated streak probability with the actual order.

interactions.hypothesis: A manager change or summer rebuild moves strength for all later matches at once; if the shift is positive, autumn windows become far more likely to contain a run, otherwise the spring half dominates.
interactions.how_to_test: Streak frequency in the 15 matches after manager changes versus matched controls; summer rating shifts versus autumn streaks.

interactions.hypothesis: A team already on a three- or four-win run with winnable next fixtures is close to settlement, while a team with no run needs a fresh five-match window; the probability jumps when the run length crosses three.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test conditional probability of reaching five given current run length 0-4 from historical sequences.

interactions.hypothesis: In cup ties a draw after 90 minutes leads to extra time and possibly penalties; under a reading where only 90/120-minute wins count, draw-prone teams lose streaks in cups even when they advance.
interactions.how_to_test: Count streaks broken by shootout ties under both readings in historical club data.

nonlinearities.shape: strongly convex in typical per-match win probability
nonlinearities.why: Probability of a run of five requires roughly p^5 per window, so raising average win probability from 0.45 to 0.55 roughly doubles the chance of a streak in 20 matches (about 0.16 to 0.36 under independence).

nonlinearities.shape: concave in number of remaining matches
nonlinearities.why: Each extra match adds one more potential window, but windows overlap and share matches, so the marginal gain diminishes and is zero once the window closes.

mechanism_review.summary: A win streak of at least five in a calendar year is a run-length event over an ordered sequence of matches. Each match has a win probability that depends on opponent strength, venue, lineup and congestion; for a club of Manchester United's recent level, many league matches carry win probabilities around 0.4-0.6, and draws are frequent streak-breakers. The number of matches remaining in the window caps chances, and the order matters because runs need consecutive winnable fixtures. Results are not independent: form, injuries, a manager change or a summer rebuild move strength over blocks of matches, which clusters wins and raises the run probability above an independent calculation. The calendar window matters: if the event is calendar 2026 with an as-of date of 2026-11-08, only about the final two months (roughly 8-12 counted fixtures, depending on cups and Europe) remain, so the current run state dominates; if the '-27' ticker denotes a 2027 window, 35-50 matches are available and the sequence and strength-reset inputs dominate. Finally, the contract's scope rules (competitions counted, penalty wins, window boundaries) define the sequence, and the run state at the as-of date sets how far the team is from the threshold or whether it is already met.

stages.name: Per-match win probability
stages.description: Each counted match's win probability comes from opponent-adjusted strength, venue, lineup strength and draw propensity. For a mid-to-upper Premier League side, home matches against bottom-half opponents may approach 0.65, away matches at top sides 0.2-0.3. Draws, not only losses, end a streak, so a draw-heavy style lowers the run probability for the same points per game.
stages.distribution: Vector of probabilities with heterogeneity across matches; each match a three-outcome event where only the win continues the run.

stages.name: Ordered sequence and opportunity count
stages.description: Reading A (calendar 2026, as-of 2026-11-08): only the Nov-Dec 2026 fixtures remain and the run state dominates. Reading B (a 2027 window implied by the '-27' ticker suffix): the full 2027 calendar applies. Under the original wording the calendar year 2026 spans the second half of 2025-26 and the first half of 2026-27, with a summer break that includes the World Cup. The ordered fixture list, conditional cup ties and European matches (if qualified) define how many windows of five consecutive matches exist and how winnable each is. Cup survival adds fixtures but also congestion.
stages.distribution: Discrete count of matches (roughly 35-50) with a stochastic component from cup progression.

stages.name: Serial dependence and regime changes
stages.description: Results cluster because the team's true strength drifts and because blocks of matches share lineup and fitness conditions. A manager change often brings a temporary bounce, and the summer transfer window can reset strength for the autumn. Drift is modelled first (rating uncertainty, manager, summer reset, injuries); soc.latent_form_persistence is only the residual serial correlation left after that. These shared shifts make streaks likelier than independent trials and widen uncertainty about the run outcome.
stages.distribution: Latent AR(1)-like strength process with occasional jumps (manager change, summer reset).

stages.name: Run-length probability from the current state
stages.description: Given the run state at the as-of date, the probability of reaching five consecutive wins before the window closes is computed by a Markov chain on run length over the ordered match probabilities, integrated over the latent strength path. The response is strongly convex in per-match win probability: For scale, a 20-match horizon (not the remaining window if reading A holds) gives P(at least one run of 5 in 20 matches) is about 0.10 at p=0.4 and about 0.36 at p=0.55 under independence.
stages.distribution: Probability bounded in [0,1], convex in typical p, absorbing once the run is achieved.

stages.name: Scope and settlement
stages.description: The rules count all competitions in calendar 2026 but do not address penalty-shootout outcomes, friendlies, or runs straddling the year boundary, and the ticker suffix differs from the stated year. Cup ties that reach extra time or penalties are classified here as a settlement-scope question, not an officiating one. Each reading defines a different sequence, so scope flags must be recorded per reading and the streak computed under each.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the flags; disagreement between readings matters mainly when a cup shootout or friendly falls inside a candidate run.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXWINSTREAKMANU-27-5 settles YES if Manchester United win at least 5 games in a row across all competitions in the year 2026 (strike type 'greater', floor 4.5, so 5+). Consecutive means without a non-win in between in counted competitions. Whether a win on penalties counts as a win, whether friendlies count, whether a run that begins in late 2025 counts, and the source of truth are not stated; the ticker suffix '27' differs from the 2026 window in the rules text.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not stated; presumably official competition results as reported by Kalshi's provider.
variants_and_edge_cases: Shootout outcomes: a cup tie drawn after extra time and won on penalties is a draw in most statistical records; whether it continues or breaks the streak is not stated.
Friendlies: 'all competitions' normally excludes pre-season friendlies, but the rules do not say so; a July 2026 friendly tour could add or break wins under a broad reading.
Window boundary: a run spanning Dec 2025 into Jan 2026 may need all five wins inside 2026; the rules imply wins 'in the year 2026' but do not say how straddling runs are treated.
Other strikes (e.g. 3+, 4+, 6+) may exist as a ladder; nested strikes must give a monotone probability curve.
The ticker ends in '27' while rules say 2026; the event window could be mislabelled or the series rolled over.
